Loved this place and can't wait to return.  We went prior to a show at the Forrest Theatre.  The small plates that are meant to be shared was a perfect meal prior to sitting at a show for the remainder of the evening.  The squash taco and "meatballs" were delicious and the unique combination of flavors in the gnocchi and beans was refreshing.  CWAS is for the diner that desires to venture beyond the familiar.
Roasted and raw oysters, Sazeracs!  Very very good service!  Worth the walk from the Convention Center
Not much can be done with my hair, but Brooke did it.  Great shop with a cool vibe; I'm definitely going back.
I ordered from Uber eats and I'm so disappointed!!! I ordered a spicy salmon roll and a salmon avocado roll. Awful! No flavor at all! Such a waste of money

Worst experience ever and extremely overpriced! A/C went out on us and we woke up sweating, electric plugs didn't work so we couldn't charge our phones, the ceiling appeared to have leaked in the past, only good thing I can say is the beds were comfortable. Will not stay there again!

Great juicy mouth watering burgers here.  Perfect location near the beach and near downtown carp.  It has a little bit of a grungy feeling but for a burger joint, it's just fine.  I'd recommend it overall and it's my favorite burger place around.
Quick and convenient. Still don't understand why Jimmy Johns won't toast their subs though..
Fast service. General Tso chicken is delicious. Chicken is tender and not dry at all. Not too salty. Great flavor.

I just recently bought a monthly membership for them. The workers were very helpful, however, didn't seem to know about their promotion. I was asking questions and none of the 3 employees had a clue.

Otherwise, the beds are nice and clean!
Definitely get you tan quick!!

I went to eat dinner here with my mom and sister the other night and everything was superb. I got the impossible veggie burger and it really lived up to its name as it was the single best veggie burger I've ever had - it was so close to meat, I couldn't believe it! For dessert my mom got flan and I got the corn & rice pudding and we all shared. The flan was so rich, and I really enjoyed the textures of the purple corn syrup and dried fruit mixed in with the rice pudding. This is a great place to get ridiculously delicious food for a very reasonable price.

Very delicious build-your-own Mediterranean food. 

It's difficult for me to give stellar review about this place because at the end of my meal I found a bone in my chicken. The chicken itself is very tasty and well seasoned. Also, they didn't give me a plastic bag for my to go meal. I had some eaten at the restaurant but on my way home it's leaking. I wish they have carry out bag with their logo for their marketing purpose too. 

Pick your base: pita, mixed green, brown rice, quinoa, or barley. I tried barley and salad. Both are great. The barley has perfect chewiness.

Protein: chicken is great, turkey and mushrooms is good too with a kick seasoning in it but outside it's a little bit charred. I didn't taste the burnt, though

Unlimited Toppings: I pick cucumber and tomato, eggplant relish, red cabbage, and chickpeas. All of them are great 

Sauce: hummus,baba ganoush, and tzatziki.

When everything is blended together they taste amazing. The eggplant is awesome and the hummus is smooth and creamy well seasoned.

Download your app and you get free entree.

The website has nutritional information on each item if you want to budget your calories.

Maybe next time I will go meatless or try the steak (add $2) to avoid any bones

I bought a loaf of the cranberry walnut $10 and profiteroles. The bread is the best nut bread I've ever had. The profiteroles is very soft and delicate perfectly filled with vanilla ice cream with chocolate sauce.

I originally booked Stanley Steamer but canceled because their arrival window was 4 hours.  That was unreasonable and inconsiderate in my opinion.  I'm glad I canceled because KC carpet & upholstery was such a great experience plus I'm so glad I was able to support a local business. When I called KC carpet Joe answered his cell and was able to squeeze me in due to another last minute cancelation.  Joe was super friendly and professional (I'm pretty sure he is the owner) and told me that Mark and Steve would be at my house between 1 & 2 the next day. Mark called about 30 minutes before their arrival time which turned out to be 1:30pm, awesome!

When Mark and Steve arrived they were super friendly and enthusiastic and were happy to trek up to the 3rd floor of the house to get to the carpets.  They cleaned the carpets super fast, and did a great job!  I added the hallway carpet last minute and they didn't charge me for it.  They were very nice in their compliments of our newly purchased hosue and even provided recommendations for various things.  We have since moved into the house and are super happy about our carpets and service that KC Carpet provided.  I will definitely use them again and refer this company to others!

 

Thanks again guys!

I know Pizza City gets a bad reputation, but I think they make an amazing pizza! I typically stick with plain pizza and always find it to be delicious. They also make a solid cheese steak, as well. The price is also so reasonable, you can't go wrong!

I really enjoy the food, beer, service, and atmosphere at Iron Hill, with the beer being my favorite part.  The only reason I have given it a 4 instead of a 5 is due to the prices occasionally being a little high.

Ordered take out from Sandys around noon on a Saturday. Was surprised how quickly it was ready (~15 mins). First thing I noticed was how pleasant Stella was. She made sure I didn't have any food allergies before giving me a piece of the homemade spinach and feta pie. Also let me know that they serve breakfast ALL DAY. I ordered the Reuben with coleslaw and the famous potato salad instead of the fries. All for around $11! Very tasty and fresh. The Reuben came with a "Russian" sauce which was delicious. Everything was hot and grilled. The potato salad was excellent as well. Will definitely go here again!

The tiramisu is ok. Not using lady fingers. The sponge cake is dry and not too soaked with liquor. 

The pear and peach frangipane is really good. Buttery crust with refreshing raspberry and sliced almonds give a crunchy texture. 

The almond croissant is the best. It's humongous filled with custard consistency of almond paste. Perfect sweetness with flaky croissant.

A little loud, but some great food.

My daughter and I had dinner there the other night.  The ambience is nice, and the service was good.  We shared the meatball appetizer - Housemade Meatballs, tomato, local goats cheese, roasted almond for $14, which was quite good. Three large meatballs in a nice, thick tomato sauce.  I would say that some bread with this would have been a nice touch, but none was offered.

I had the Alberta Flank Steak, smashed potato, chimichurri, pea shoots for $27.  It was tender, and delicious.  

Finally, the beer selection was a nice departure from the usual domestic listing.  

In my view, Woodwork is a small notch away from a 5th star.  Some sound dampening would be a nice touch.  As well, the servers could up their game slightly.  The food is certainly of 5 star quality.  Some small tweaks would bring Woodwork to a new level, but it is a worthwhile visit now.

I ordered a car seat and a quilt from diapers.com. The delivery driver left my car seat and rang the doorbell. While I was trying to haul the car seat inside, pregnant mind you, he literally threw the last box at my door step. Thankfully there wasn't anything fragile in there, but seriously! At least have some decency.

Very friendly service. Food came out fast. Sashimi is really fresh.

Definitely come back to try different items

Second time eating from here. I got takeout and the portion and price was right on for Franklin. I had a martini while waiting and even though it was happy hour special it wasn't watered down at all. Great and timely service. Awesome noodles.

I have been to Copia before, and had a great experience.  I went again this past Friday and was rather disappointed by my return visit.  I will preface this by saying that the food was excellent; possibly five star quality.  
We had the Mediterranean Mezza, everything on that plate was fantastic, on my first visit we tried the Arancini, which I'd also highly recommend.  I had the surf and turf which was very nicely put together, and the perfect portion size.  The gf had the Osso Bucco which was also excellent.  Please note: if you plan on going for the food - Copia is one of the more expensive places you can find yourself in STL.  I'll also note that it is more of an Italian steak and seafood place than a wine bar.  If you're looking for something new and different in your food, this probably not the place to come searching for it.  
Now that the food is done, let's move on to the service:  I should note that I do not complain at restaurants, no matter how good or poor the experience.  I think about the movie "Waiting" when it comes to complaining at restaurants. 
Our waitress did checked on us once while we were eating and not again until 30 minutes after we'd stopped eating.  My wine glass had been empty since the appetizer.  Another 15 minutes passed before she bussed our tables and asked if we wanted dessert, coffee, an apertif, cocktail or a glass of wine.  I would have taken her up on that glass of wine about an hour ago, but when she came to ask about dessert, we were ready to go.  
After reading the filtered reviews, (Copia's overall score would be much lower if they were counted) I'm glad I didn't complain, because it sounds like the owners or management don't know how to receive criticism.  
I recommend this place to no one, there are many other great places to eat in STL where the service is stellar, the food is equally as excellent and the chefs are more creative.

We just went there for dessert but I loved the concept of the restaurant. The ambience was warehouse style but had a warm and cozy bistro feel.  They serve breakfast, lunch and dinner and have interesting cocktails, great pastries and delicious looking bread- something for everybody.  Our waitress was very nice and the general manager- Andy Dale- very helpful. I think this restaurant will be very successful in that location.

Not my first time to Sub Zero.  I was in the mood for a burger and you can't go wrong with a burger from Sub Zero.  I built my own with black angus, caramelized onions, american cheese and chipotle mayo.  The burger was perfectly mid-rare as I'd asked for and was exactly what I wanted, how I wanted it.  

We started with two sushi rolls: Salmon and Avocado (my all-time favorite) and spicy tuna.  I highly recommend the Salmon and Avocado - the texture of the salmon and the avocado melds beautifully and it contrasts that of the rice.  
I probably wouldn't get their version of spicy tuna again - it was good, but not as spicy as I prefer.  

They get a four because they're loud.  I could barely hear myself think.

Far and away my favorite place to eat in WC. 

From the wide variety of food options, to the fun drinks and ambiance, this place is a home run. I have eaten here a lot over the years and never had a bad meal. The wings are the best in West Chester and the entrees are creative and super satisfying. A nice break from all the Italian joints that line Gay St. 

Beer garden out back is great for a summer afternoon. Do wish they served a full bar out there. Overall, fantastic.

I ordered on Grubhub, the delivery time said an hour but it only took 30 minutes which was great, but...

I ordered the Pad Thai, Sesame Chicken and Seaweed salad.
The pad thai and sesame chicken were very bland!! I would not order again.

The seaweed salad was good.

My husband and myself were staying at the Hilton, and did not feel like walking anywhere. We thought we'd give it a try. Overall it's an okay place! The service was good, our server was friendly and keep our drinks full. The food left me wanting something more. It's not that it was bad, just nothing to brag about! I know we can get better food else where. The apple cobbler was the one thing I would say we did not like, not even a little.

This place is a life saver.  I thought that I was going to do my own invitations.  When I went to print them,  I ran in to so many issues my friends volunteered to pay for someone else to do the invites just to stop me from stressing.  Long story short- I went here for my invites.  Anne was so helpful and worked with my tight timeline.  The invites came out beautifully and I was still on track.  I couldn't have done it without them.  It was such a great experience.  I can't thank them enough!

Hands down, one of the best meals you can get in STL.  It is the perfect place to try something new, and offers many opportunities to do so.  I recommend it for a celebration, probably not for a casual date night.

The beignets are awesome, to start and the wine list is very approachable.  The waitress offered up some red wine suggestions which turned out to be perfect.  We split the (small) Sweet Breads appetizer to start and for dinner I had a pork belly special, which was one of the richest, but enjoyable meals I've ever eaten.  The gf had a filet with Bearnaise, stuffed with lobster and other gems from the sea.  Both meals were absolutely wonderful.

They have great broiled oysters. When you come here, make sure you order it. You may ask for extra bread to dip the sauce and olive oil. It is just simply great. This is the best broiled I have ever tried. The pasta here is tasty as well. The location is convenient too.

Came in right after the almond croissant just came out from the oven. It was sooo good. Very buttery and flaky croissant, including the pretzel croissant. Super friendly guy. The tiramisu is good too. I will definitely come back to try their other goodies.

Very good breakfast. The pancakes are very fluffy. 

I had egg whites omelette with asparagus and fruit instead of home fries. Fresh asparagus perfectly cooked.

I took a star down because my toast was a little bit burnt

This place has a lot of German products for Octoberfest. Streudel, cake, cookies, stolen, pretzels, everything looks so inviting. Of course don't forget to get the brats wursts.

One cashier lady was so nice and friendly.

The bread is amazing, particularly cranberry walnut. I had Niçoise salad for lunch. It's pretty good although I was expecting fresh tuna, it looked like it was from a can. Had baba rum for desert but I didn't taste the rum at all. I also bought French macarons, nothing special, I will not buy it again.

Wow! What amazing customer service and food! I stopped in because a girlfriend is renewing her vows and wanted a special cake. She couldn't go by the bakery to taste samples so she sent me knowing how picky I am about desserts. Wow, I was amazed. The ingredients are fresh and they only use real cream, not that nasty stuff you find on most cakes. It was heaven and the owner was so nice and so helpful I loved the sampling. We also ended up taking home gyros and salad for dinner to go along with the remaining cake! You don't find businesses like this very often. I recommend patronizing this establishment as often as you can!

Beautiful river view. There are Hardena at the back and Little Baby's ice cream.

The indoor is plain and not much going on. I wish there are more vendors

This place is on second floor at DiBruno's. The hostess was super nice and friendly. It's a nice open space with bar area on the left. I had margarita pizza to go. The crust is thin and crunchy. Sauce is enough and fresh

Was looking for a lunch location for a business meeting and the guests were vegan. Was told they had vegan options. I would have thought that at lunch time it would be relatively quiet and we sat outside but the music was so loud we could barely hear each other. The black bean burger without cheese, as they don't carry vegan cheese, was recommended as the best vegan option. They were ordered without buns because she didn't know if the bun was vegan or had a dairy wash. Unfortunately this burger came out almost in the shape of burger but the consistency was more like chili; as if the binder had been forgotten. Needless to say those guests won't be visiting again. If you are looking for true vegan options take your guests to Tate's at Sandpearl, Beachcomber, Bobby's Bistro, or Spotted Donkey. Additionally for a restaurant so close to the water you would think they would be more eco-friendly. Not at all. Try the other restaurants until this one catches up to the times of caring for the environment.

This is a 2.5 review. 

My check in experience was quite entertaining actually but Budget should be ashamed. The guy checking me in, who was very nice, was certainly embarrassed and kept apologizing to me. 

The lady who appeared to be in charge hates her job and the company. A lady called Cindy was checking people in and seemed to be working hard. Suddenly the manager lady appeared and started yelling at her about her lunch hour. At first Cindy was quietly trying to defend herself but after a while her voice raised slightly too. And the  supervisor started yelling at her to stop yelling. 

When Cindy left for lunch the lady in charge came to talk to the guy checking me in about something unrelated about the incompetence of all the staff. 

Then she turned to me to start telling me how done she is with the company! 

Budget needs to send their staff, and especially their managers, on a customer service training course.

Very good hummus place. My favorite is the traditional hummus. The chickpeas and wheat pilaf is very flavorful and so are the chicken schwarma and lemon. The eggplant hummus has funny taste. The tzaziki sauce is good too.

The coffee eclair is my favorite. The lemon tart is perfect, and so is the chocolate tart, which was recommended by the chef. Definitely get the brioche almond French toast. The traditional and chocolate financier are highly recommended, very light and addictive.

Avoid this restaurant. There are plenty of other options in the area to get a nice meal. 
Cracker Barrel is always one of our favorites. However, after our experience last night we will never eat here again. 

Visit 1 (a few months ago):  waited more then 10 minutes for a table (there were plenty of tables available in the restaurant, it wasn't busy). Once seated, it took another 10 minutes for a waiter to greet us and take our order. We ordered breakfast and the food was pretty good, so overall not a bad visit...I'd give them 3 stars for slow service. 

Visit 2 (about a month ago):  again had a longer than expected wait for our server. Eventually ordered dinner and the food was decent. The service was a little slow, but adequate. At the checkout counter  we overheard a conversation between an associate and a disgruntled customer about an entire family getting food poisoning and requesting a refund for a $150+ bill (didn't think much of it...we had just had a good dinner). I'd give this visit 4 stars. 

Visit 3:  since the service had always been a little slow in the restaurant we decided to order ToGo.  I arrived at the restaurant at the listed time on the order (31 minutes). I told the woman at the checkout counter that I was picking up a ToGo order.  She told me to go talk to the Host Station. I informed the host  about my ToGo order and he called back to the kitchen to let them know I was here. I waited for 10 minutes at the Host Station and no one ever came out with my order. Finally, the host asked another employee about the delay and they said I had to go back to the checkout counter to get my order. I paid at the counter and again they radioed back to the kitchen that I was here to pick up an order. Another 10 minutes goes by (by now there are 3 of us waiting for ToGo orders) and they finally come out with my order.  I get home less than 10 minutes later. All of the food is cold, the potatoes smell like sour milk, and I pulled a hair out of a slice of meatloaf...I'm now ordering a pizza. 

0 stars for this visit and they've lost my business forever.

Gado gado: the serving size is much smaller than than that at Indonesian restaurant. Great peanut sauce with fried tortilla to scoop the ingredients. 

Satay: chicken satay is better than the pork. The pork is dry.

Ayam bakar kecap / grilled chicken with sweet soy sauce: delicious. You can choose between chicken breast or thighs. It comes with small bowl of vegetable curry, rice, and crackers/ kerupuk. The curry has some kick of spiciness. 

Kwetiaw: very delicious. The flat noodles is perfectly cooked and chewiness, not dry at all. It has sliced of sweet sausage.

I wish they make fried banana

Great place to eat, service is always great and food even better.  Been coming for over a year and very consistent. Give them a try you will not be disappointed.  John is always here, he is the owner and a great.  Great service tonight from Latoyia

Came here after the remodeling. Very clean and bright store. Much cheaper organic and specialty products such as almond flour and almond butter. Brioche buns are more affordable.

A lot of hummus selections including chocolate hummus that tasted like brownie batter just like Trader Joe's.

The freezer section is so clean including selections of mochi ice cream.

Also a lot of varieties of specialty bread 

Very fast checkout process.
so good :) get the pico de gallo!! you won't regret it! also get the blue tacos  this place is a hidden gem! i can't wait to go back!

The review is for the delivery order.

Tandoori Salmon : flavorful, salmon is cooked well done without overly dry.

Papad: thin and very crispy it's salty.

Ekta dal: so far is my favorite. Seasoning is on point and not too heavy.
Quick service at the bar,  reasonable prices for carne  Asada and quesadillas.  Very good drinks and very good bartenders.  The salsa will warm you up...I will return soon!!

The review is for the pork shiumai. It comes in 4 pieces. Not flavorful and I only tasted saltiness. It's a disappointment.

My coworker had chicken broccoli and he said it's ok.

I went for the second time tonight after having a wonderful dinner the first time. Tonight I had the hamachi crudo and the fish of the day (cod). I also tried the plate of pork, and the animal potatoes. The fish was literally just that. A small delightful piece of fish. After finishing it in 4 bites, I was left wishing there was a bit more - a few more veggies perhaps (there was literally one small round slice of a zucchini). The plate of pork was ok - very fatty and in my opinion, the ribs were underdone. No complaints about the potatoes. Another disappointing part of the evening was the service. I felt so welcomed the first time, this second time was definitely not the case. I had reservations and was not acknowledged until almost 15 minutes after I entered, dinner service was also extremely slow. Barbareño is such a gem and very charming, I've had both an extremely positive and a very disappointing experience. Best of luck that your experience is the former!

Pretty good vegan ice cream option in south tampa. The matcha cookies were the best part. My non-vegan gf ordered the dog ice cream because she didn't realize it was for dogs. She liked it. She's a good girl.

All of the cookies are great. Taste like normal cookies. There are plenty of chocolate chips to give sweetness to the cookies. The banana chocolate chip cookie has delicious banana taste. 

The blueberry crumb bars are awesome. Very moist with perfect sweetness, melts in your mouth.

Chocolate chip banana bread is great. Moist and sweet.

The s'mores cupcakes is awesome. It has pretty thick graham cracker crust, moist chocolate cake and creamy frosting.

The brownies are sweet and moist. Highly recommend.

Don't forget to check out on the side next to the register the baked donuts, muffins, and gluten free tomato pie. The donut is very dense but still sweet and delicious. 

I enjoyed everything there.

Great place for authentic and cheap Indonesian food. It can be crowded during mealtime but food comes out fast. The sell Indonesian crackers (Kerupuk) and some traditional cookies near the beverage fridge. The portion is pretty decent, not too small. I can have the fried kwetiaw for 2 meals.

Very trendy hangout place. Most of the tables are communal where you share a long bench with other people. You can hangout at the bar or outside. Menu is very short. You can overlook the brewery from a glass door at the back. You can have tours of the brewery. 

Bavarian pretzel: don't get this. It's not Bavarian at all compared to Brauhaus. Very hollow and chewy crust. The mustard is really good though

Green salad: very fresh 

Ahi poke: fresh fish and served with sesame and macadamia which give crunchy texture. I mixed it with my salad to make it poke salad.

Pickled veggies: very fresh, has cucumber, beets, cauliflower, and carrots 

BBQ platter: this is the best meal. Sausage has perfect smoky flavor, brisket is very tender and melts in your mouth. The corn bread is soft and crunchy. The cabbage slaw is good. It's also served with potato salad which a little bit too salty. The serving size is for two people. It comes with short ribs too. 

Service is great. Very friendly staff, food comes out fast.

You can take home some beer and merchandise on your way out.

The roast pork is full of flavor, too salty for me but so good. Very juicy and moist because they put the broth with the sandwich. Add the sharp provolone and spinach or broccoli rabe for a complete experience. You can add hot peppers too. Pretty expensive though, around $10 for sandwich with cheese. 

This place is featured on travel channel

Definitely my new favorite Mediterranean eatery. What prompted me to order is 25% discount on your first order through Grubhub. I scheduled for delivery for noon but got a call that it would be before one pm. Long story short I got the food 1:50. The owner I assume who delivered the food was very apologetic and offered free delivery and dessert on my next order.

Chicken schawarma bowl is big and delicious. Cubed chicken was tender and juicy. Not over seasoned topped white white sauce that adds flavor. Yellow rice isnt dry.

Hummus and baba ganoush dip is awesome. Not too salty, the baba ganoush has its signature smoky flavor. It comes with warm pita bread. The pita isn't home made. My guess is Touffayan pita which I always buy.

The baklava is pretty big and delicious. It is not dry and perfect dessert to end the meal.

I would definitely recommend it and order again

Takoyaki is awesome. The best I've ever had. The balls are small but melts in your mouth. Perfect flavor and I could taste pieces of the octopus.

Signature ramen is pretty good. Great flavor of the broth. I got mine to go. My noodles was hard and clumpy. Maybe next time I have to detangle the noodle and let it sit in hot broth

The review is for delivery orders: 

Cauliflower appetizer: my favorite. It's creamy but not soupy. Dairy free. There's shredded coconut in it to give some crunchy texture. The cauliflower is soft, just melts in your mouth.

Eggplant appetizer: it's soggy but the sauce is delicious.

Vegetable samosas: it is big.  The skin is fresh, not too hard, not too greasy. The filling has some spiciness. 

Traditional naan and paratha are fresh and soft when they're warm. Eat it right away and use it for dipping. I use mine to clean up the sauce of the cauliflower and the eggplant. Highly recommend

Cute Italian dessert place. The staff is Italian, super friendly. The cannoli shells are from Italy and so are the fillings. They are willing to customize my cannoli with Nutella. There are varieties of sizes and kinds of shells, from mini to giant, from plain to chocolate covered with different toppings.  The filling can be plain or with chocolate chips.

The gelato is really good and smooth with perfect sweetness. They are imported from Italy too and definitely at the same quality as Gran Cafe Laquila. I say it is the more affordable version of it. The lady who helped me was wearing the same kind of Italian hat as those at Gran Cafe.
The Nutella and tiramisu are awesome 
The tiramisu is amazing. Definitely get this, really tasty with a lot of lady fingers soaked in espresso and perfect amount of mascarpone not whipped cream.

The sfogliatelle is greasy although the filling is very good and traditional Italian filling with a lemon flavor 

It's definitely a hidden gem

Good Italian bakery. It sells pastries, bagels,  pizza, and Stromboli. I had crusty bread which is very good. The lady suggested this bread for dipping. Vera Crusty on the outside but the inside is very soft. You can also buy dough too to make pizza or Stromboli at home, mine always comes out great. 

My other favorite is the kaiser roll which is soft and moist even until the next day. It's medium size.

The garlic and cheese bread is a perfect compliment with your Italian dinner . If you come in late of the day, most of them are sold out

There are a lot of gluten free products that are affordable. 

I bought sweet potato chips which are really good. It's thinly sliced, very fresh and crunchy and lightly salted.

I found interesting products here such as cheesesteak ravioli. I hope it taste good.

Every time I call to place my order I always get very friendly service who explains my questions of the dish that I ask for.

Vegetable samosas: comes in two pieces. The dough isn't thick, not greasy, enough fillings. It's not spicy and not heavily seasoned.

Vegetable tandoori: the veggies are crisp and covered with herbs. Delicious.

Chicken jalfrezi: it's not creamy and seasoning is well balanced. There are chunks of chicken but slightly on the dry side with slices of red and green peppers. It's light and not too heavy entree.

Good cookies. They are $1 each during the last half hour.
Lots of PA goodies such as soft and hard pretzels. They have chocolate and French macarons too

This place was just recommended by a friend and we decided to stop in to check it out. The atmosphere is upscale casual, warm and friendly. We ordered a traditional pie and a white pie and.. they were so ridiculously good. I can't say enough about this crust it's absolutely perfect. Best pizza I've had in South Jersey maybe even in Philadelphia. The people behind us came down from North Jersey and were raving about their gnocchi and homemade sausage. The owner took the time to come out and greet each guest individually and have an actual conversation with us. Very genuine person and a gem of a restaurant hidden in an unassuming mini mall. Can't wait to bring my husband back for a proper Italian dinner and try some of the specials.

You want to visit this place. If you go there you will be part of there family.  It is a great family restaurant and you will certainly feel like you are sitting in there home having dinner or lunch.  I suggest that you go often so you can try everything.  This is not your typical Chinese restaurant.  The head chef and I said chef is a wizard in the kitchen.  Infusing  Chinese with French and other international flavors.

Great service. Food came out fast. I had crab cake salad. It comes with 4 good size small crab cakes. Very delicious, no fillers, not dry at all. Perfectly broiled not drenched with mayonnaise so you can taste the sweetness of the crab meat . The salad is fresh with boiled eggs,and sliced cucumbers.

The BLT sandwich is triple decker, very good to with perfectly cooked crispy bacon and light layer of  mayonnaise. The French fries is perfectly fried, very crispy,  and not soggy or hard at all

This review is for the satay, gado gado, and toast.

Gado gado: it has bean sprouts, long bean, tofu , Tempe. The important ingredient is the peanut sauce. It is not my liking at all, it's not how it taste when I grew up in a Indonesia. 

Chicken satay: the good: no burnt part, chicken isn't tough or dry. However the only  flavor I tasted is coriander. The peanut sauce is the same as gado gado and definitely it taste different than what I am used to growing up. It's a disappointing dish.

The toast aka roti bakar. The bread is hard and tough. Not recommended . 

I want to get mung bean porridge but to my disappointment it's sold out. I came around 5:30. I was advised to come in earlier 

Free wifi is a nice feature here. 

I will give it another try for other items on the menu.

The best part is the service that deserves five star rating. The girl is super friendly and helpful. She helped me opening the door because I had a lot on my hands.

Nice store in South Philadelphia. Self check out is the fastest way to go if you don't have a lot. There's Starbucks at the entrance.

Plenty of parking space.

I placed another delivery order. This time my review is about the followings:

Chicken korma: chicken is dry and tough. I think it's over cooked. The sauce is delicious, not to heavy although it's creamy.

The peshawari naan with nuts in it is awesome. It has sweetness in it and some crunchy texture.

Aloo papri chaat: it's okay, the wheat crisp it's greasy.

Baingan bharta: it's creamy and the spice is on point.

Fresh high quality seafood . Very friendly and helpful staff. 

Seabass is my favorite. I usually buy the chunks or pieces which are cheaper than the main cut. They also have chunks and pieces of among others halibut, salmon, Mahi Mahi. 

The shrimp cocktail in several size options are very fresh too

Been to many high end salons in the city and Beauty Is is by far the best. Not only am I ecstatic and satisfied with both color and cut every time I walk out the door but the overall experience is what makes this salon stand out! Comfort and relaxation is always at forefront of your time here. You get what you pay for here unlike a lot of other places. Head and back massages, snacks, and drinks if your choice. I highly recommend coming to this salon and giving yourself the ultimate salon experience.

Very clean build your own meal place in the food court of Comcast building. It's where Termini used to be, next to DiBruno.

I took a star down because there's not much greens in it. The hummus and pistachio pesto was my spread and it's awesome. It's had the baked falafel and "meatballs ". Everything comes together perfectly. It's hard to find baked falafel. I am glad I found this place.


Skordalia is the almond garlic spread and is awesome too, great for dipping with your pita. Highly recommend.


The pita with hazelnut and banana is delicious too although my pita had some stale taste.? The hazelnut spread definitely not Nutella because it's not too sweet.

Very delicious tartes, buttery crust  and smooth custard fillings with fresh fruit on top. You can have in bite size or  full size. The chocolate covered  brûlée is so smooth and not overly sweet Canele is ok. It's missing the citrusy taste.

Great olive oil and vinegar. They also sell hot sauce, honey, and dipping herbs.

My usuals are lemon Meyer olive oil, Lambrusco red wine vinegar, black truffles balsamic vinegar. The gentleman at the store introduced me to the mix of Lambrusco with blood orange olive oil. So refreshing, I drank the mix from the sample cup. 

You can pickup recipe cards using their products. Definitely a must visit if you come to the Italian Market
Very cute small house. Friendly staff and the actresses who were portraying Betsy Ross and the laundry lady were very friendly and informative

Pernil: very good and juicy. Perfect flavor and seasoning.
Roast chicken: also tender and juicy, great flavor.
Arroz con gandules: very good,  has some chopped olives. Highly recommended.

The review is for the crepes. I picked strawberry, banana, with nutella and chocolate drizzle. They gave generous amount of the fruits but I didn't taste the Nutella. But for $5, it's a decent crepes.

They also have a lot of flavors of ice cream, cut-up fresh fruit, and other frozen dessert including chamoyadas. 

Great Mexican dessert place. Service is fast and friendly.

Pita is not homemade, it's dry. Naf Naf grill has the fluffiest pits and made there. The babaganoush and hummus are decent. The eggplant salad is pretty good. I had chicken schwarma and it's salty. I had baklava and it's the worst I have ever had. It's very dry an stale. I will not return. I am still on the quest for best schwarma in town.

Good popcorn but it's at extremely high prices. Got the sea salt and cracked pepper yesterday. Was over $13 for a bag about 24" tall and 4" across. Go to Kroger and get the $4.99 big bag of popcorn. Your wallet will thank you for it. This bag would be over $20 here.

I've walked by this place so many times without giving it a second thought and after checking Yelp, I was shocked at what a gem it was! My husband and I live a few blocks away so we walked there the other night with our three kids. A double side by side stroller will not fit through the door as we learned the hard way, but I removed a seat, collapsed it and we were good to go.

Inside is small with two 4-seater tables, a 2-seater and a few seats at the counter. We went off peak so we got a 4-seater table. The salsa was so good! My 6 year old who is usually anti-tomato (let alone tomatillo) approved! El pastor tacos were good and the husband like his fajitas. The kids' burrito was a bit heavy on the rice, but they ate so I won't complain too much. 

We will be back without the stroller next time!

I arrived here 5 minutes before it opened. I was greeted by Mike who asked me to wait on the couch. The waiting area is very spacious and homy. Mike is very friendly and knowledgeable about the menu.

Panzanella salad: very delicious. It has shaved brussel sprouts, small diced purple carrots, raisins, hazelnuts, and croutons with light and not acidic dressing. It's a crunchy salad. I had small but I can easily finish the big one.

Roasted branzino is served with pastina and capers. It's a little bit too salty because of the capers. The fish is perfectly cooked. Portion size isn't bog so it's perfect for lunch.

Budino: rich chocolate but not overly sweet. Great way to end your meal.

Service was excellent. Everyone was friendly, courteous, and welcoming. I had a delightful conversation with Mike. I feel I've known him for years. He accompanied me to the elevator because I had a heavy shopping cart. 

Definitely come back more often

My search for the best birria tacos is over. This place is the best. I follow the Instagram for its location and hours. Most of the time it is available at the corner of 7 and McKean from 3-9.

I got there at 3 on a drizzly afternoon. There were already a couple of people waiting for their order. Besides the birria tacos, they have guacamole and chips. Very friendly and welcoming. My order was ready probably in 10 minutes. Much faster than the other popular birria tacos food truck several blocks away.

The tacos have two layers of crispy tortilla with caramelized melted cheese adding umami to the tacos. It automatically comes with cheese so if you don't want cheese I recommend that you tell them when you place the order. The cheese are evenly distributed and melts on  tortilla perfectly, not too much to create a glob of cheese. The tacos are filled with good amount of tender beef with finely chopped onions. The tortilla is completely soaking the flavor of the consommé already drizzled on it during the cooking process. The moment of truth: the consommé flavor. It's amazing, balanced flavor with a subtle heat, very refreshing, and don't forget to squirt the lime. I keep on dunking the tacos in it. If you like more heat to your tacos, they have it covered by providing creamy chipotle sauce in the bag. There's also some shredded beef in the consommé. Not too greasy, I don't want to waste any of it. Maybe make a ramen with the leftover consommé. I saw an Instagram post of ramen with birria consommé.

Guacamole is fresh with enough heat from the chopped jalapeño with chopped tomato and red onion. It comes in a paper coffee cup with a lid.

What I like about this truck is the consommé and the guacamole are not in a styrofoam cup. The tacos and the chips are in styrofoam container. I hope they can change it to more environmentally friendly container.

Delicious chicken tinga burrito. Chicken is tender, good flavor. If you want more heat, you can put more chipotle that comes with it.

Plantain is hard and not sweet, which I assume it's from unripe plantain. I prefer sweet and caramelized plantain. It's a pass from me.

Churros is fresh. I ordered the one with caramel fillings but didn't notice it at all. It comes with chocolate dipping. The dipping is more like chocolate drink instead of melted chocolate. Definitely recommend this

Very affordable. Kwetiaw goreng and siram are really good. I ordered gado gado and ikan pari bakar (grilled sting ray). They are good. The fish is perfectly cooked. Service is great, food comes out fast.

Amazing products, great service.

You can test the products there.

If you are not happy with it you can return it even after using. If you don't have the receipt, they will give you store credit.

This review is for Colony2 delivered by Caviar. When I got it the pizza was not hot. Although it is thick, the dough isn't heavy. It's airy and light with a nice crisps on the edges. The bottom is a little bit soggy. The jalapeño gives a nice heat to the pizza balanced with sweetness from the honey.

I see Dr Whitten. I originally went there for diagnosis workup because I couldn't get an OBGYN to do anything. Overall, I had about 15 months of treatment (diagnosis, 4 IUI, 1 IVF, 1 Laparoscopy) until I became pregnant. Dr Whitten was AMAZING through all of it. He spent lots of time in his office face to face with me and my husband, and made sure we understood everything(answered all questions very patiently). Overall, my experience has been very good with the staff. Aida is the most amazing there, so kind and compassionate in every situation and always returns emails within 30 minutes. 
Overall, my experience has been really great. Mark at the front desk is always so kind, Vanessa (usually administers shots and such) is always a pleasure to see, all the staff for IVF is amazing and so so compassionate and kind. Everyone in billing is great. You'll see here that most, if not all, the staff is just amazing, friendly and welcome. 
I did have one issue with a staff member which I think is notable for whoever reading this review to know and what I wished I would've known going into treatment at NCRM: 
The PA, Jonna. 
 1. She's always very rushed, and performed my IUIs so quickly that I would have bad cramping. I had two IUIs performed by her, and two by others. The only time I had a painless IUI was when Jonna was NOT performing it. 
2. She was always very quick to correct or belittle me. I had a procedure performed there called an HSG-- she criticized me for researching the procedure. At a later time, I asked if the catheter used in the IUI was the same in the HSG, and she responded with "Oh what have you been researching now" I also called an IUI "artificial insemination" and instead of just explaining that IUI is intrauterine insemination, she responded "that's for animals" 
3. She made judgemental looks several times. One example was when I told her I had never had a papsmear (again issues with OBGYNs not willing to treat me). She literally side eyed the other person in the room when I said it and made this weird facial expression. She did this several other times whenever I could tell she thought something was weird.
4. She refused to give information on office policy. I asked her about office policy once, and she refused to answer because of my age(and even made it clear by responding "um.. well you're *inserts my age*") When I started treatment there for diagnosis, I was pretty young and she made it pretty clear through several appointments that she didn't support me being there considering my age. 
5. She kind of gave me false hope. My first round of treatment, she specifically said "we will call you in two weeks with the good news." I could tell that in her mind I was "young and fertile" and she didn't think I'd be struggling to conceive. Obviously, moving onto IVF proved that wrong and her responses definitely starting changing the more failed treatment I had. Luckily, I wasn't naive to where I thought my first round would be successful, but it wasn't fair to get that kind of speech. 
6. She was never encouraging or compassionate. Leaving appointments with Jonna were starting to make me so discouraged and upset about her comments, that I actually made a policy myself where I wouldn't go to my appointments alone if she was performing them. It wasn't worth the risk of the belittlement and judgement I would get from her.

The good thing in all of this, is I did talk to Dr Whitten about one time Jonna was so rude that I left the office crying, and after that, I had barely any problems with her. Rather than rude comments, she just distanced herself a lot more in my appointments and definitely makes me feel more like a number than a patient. I didn't tell him about all of this because it doesn't do any good complaining over something that I didn't feel would change BUT I could tell Dr Whitten had talked to her when I did address one issue. So he did hear me, understand me, and did something about it--again, another reason why Dr Whitten is SO wonderful. Like I said earlier, the rest of the staff is amazing too. I'm not going to give them a horrible rating because the clinic is AMAZING, but no one struggling with infertility and heart ache should have to go through what I did with Jonna.

A hole in the wall pizza place that has fantastic pizza! My partner got the vegetarian white pizza and she says it was so good! The guy at the counter was so nice and accommodating too.  They do gluten free pizzas which is what I have to eat AND they do gluten free breakfast. I'm definitely going to go back and get gluten free items. Will update this post accordingly.
This review is for the tandoori chicken. It consists of pieces of bone-in chicken. So tender but spicy. Great flavor.

The review is for the delivery order.

Very nice service because they can accommodate my special order. I ordered korma with cauliflower and it is delicious.

Peshawari naan: I was expecting dry fruits and nuts as described in the menu but I found only a thin layer of ground nuts. That's why I took a star down.

Lachha Paratha is pretty good. Both bread came warm. 

Baigan Bharta and Masaladar Chola are full of spices. It's good but not mind blowing. 

My delivery comes with styrofoam plates an utensils. The food is still piping hot. Nice service 

I want to try the non vegetarian dishes next time

Guy's is back with their friendly service and overstuffed shrimp poboys. The shrimp seasoning is great on the numerous large shrimp, but a few suggestions - the leidenheimer's bread is wonderful but make sure it's totally fresh and reduce the mayonnaise on the sandwich. It was too sloppy. Otherwise everything was great.

Delicious tacos. The Korean beef tacos is spicy enough to give it a kick but not overwhelming that dominate the tacos. Generous portions of tender meat. You can choose between two or three tacos per order. 

I ordered takeout and the tacos were in environmentally friendly containers.

The staff is friendly. The place is clean but not many seatings.

Definitely come back to try different kinds

Sfogliatelle: the pastry is crunchy with lots of fillings. I was expecting citrus flavor in the filling. Unfortunately I only tasted a hint of it. The cannoli and zeppoli has pretty good ricotta fillings.

Gelato: I tried tiramisu but didn't taste tiramisu at all. I had the baci because I love Nutella. The flavor is just a hint. 

Overall it's ok, I didn't find any wow factor there.

Very friendly staff. They have danish, muffins, bagels for breakfast 

For lunch or dinner they have pizza and Stromboli. 

There are different varieties of Italian bread and rolls. Accept orders for catering.

The entrance is on Mifflin street across Southwark school. There's a staff giving direction in this big building. The elevator is nice and clean although the ride to 8 floor takes forever.

The restaurant is nice with original grafitti. The chandelier is beautiful. On the deck you can see the view of south Philadelphia.

The waitress is very helpful and friendly. Knowledgeable on the menu item. We had baba ganoush with warm flat bread, chicken chicken cheese confit and lamb with eggplant. Portion is small. Everything has great flavor , well seasoned .

Baklava is a must. The syrup is poured on the table. Very crispy and fresh. The tahini brownie is another good dessert option.

Brunch is available on Sunday morning.

Kale salad with chopped apple and pear is very good. The fruit is cut in small dices. The dressing has perfect acidity and sweetness, perfect compliment to the salad.
Lemon waffle is highly recommended. It has buttery flavor but the lemon and yogurt make this waffle not a heavy meal.

Turkish breakfast is very interesting and unique. It's served on chopping board consisting sausage, spicy olives, chocolate tahini spread, fig jam, goat cheese, arugula, eggs, and crusty yet moist sourdough bread. It's a good breakfast experience.

My  husband had Bloody Mary and Bloody Cesar and both are ok, not impressive.
Beer is average definitely needs more hazy beers like tired hands and not so malty and clear. Food and atmosphere is good though

This is a family owned and operated establishment that has the BEST breakfast and lunches by the courthouses. The family is Greek so the gyros is amazing. Definitely stop by if you are near the courthouses. You will not be disappointed!

The $7 off for order $25 or more at Grubhub is a good deal as it covers the delivery fee and taxes. As usual I ordered the schawarma bowl, babaganoush, and this time I tried an eggplant dish called mosskah. I placed the order around noon. I got a call to let me know that they opened at one so my food would be delivered at 1:30 and I would get free baklava. Sounded like a deal. At 1:45 my food hadn't arrived. I called and was told that it should arrive in 5 minutes. Just like 2 orders ago it arrived at 2. 

I would never order for lunch because it's always late. They should be consistent with the store hours. The yelp info states it opens at 11.

As always the chicken schawarma and babaganoush didn't disappoint me. 

The eggplant has some spicy kick and so good for dipping with the warm pita. There's some grease floating around but very tasty. Definitely recommend it.

I came here for the first time after they renovated the restaurant. The entrance is right outside the mall. The seatings are congested as before. More seatings at the back of the restaurant. There are flat screens TV but I miss the wayang kulit aka shadow puppet picture.

The staff is completely different than before, very much younger. I called for my favorite fried kwetiaw and was told it took 20-30 minutes. The restaurant wasn't crowded when I arrived. I was surprised by the waiting time. In the past after I put my order in I went to the supermarket briefly and when I returned the food was ready. This time I waited a while and after about 20 minutes I asked whether it would be a while to get the food. The girl said that she already told me the time, she said that in an unfriendly and annoyed way. Too add to my disappointment to the service, the kwetiaw was bland. Not as delicious as before. It's missing the sweet Chinese sausage.

Service is bad although he's friendly. Our server Dave forgot our seltzer water and when I asked my plum dessert to go, it's served on the table. My pretzel appetizer came out late with entree.

Complimentary bread: pumpernickels and sourdough from Metropolitan bakery. Very good, especially the sourdough, it's soft and moist.

Pretzel: it's cold and not as big as typical Bavarian pretzel. Maybe because mine came out late. Disappointing.

Roasted chicken: the purée and the vegetables are very delicious, perfect seasoning. The chicken is salty, not too much flavor. The salt dominates the flavor. The chicken breast is on the dry side.

Salad: fresh. 

Red cabbage: really good. Definitely get it.

Sausage platter with potato salad and sauerkraut: the sauerkraut had pork in it. The sausages are delicious but not recommended to those in low sodium diet because they are salty. Again, my husband asked for not getting sausage with herbs but we got one with herbs. It's the waiter's mistake.

Dessert: apple streudel comes warm with vanilla ice cream and vanilla sauce. It's thin slice with thin crust. Fresh apple. Good combination with ice cream. Overall it's okay. Not what I expected from a German restaurant with layers of crust.

Plum: comes in slices of sweetened plums wit crunchy streudel in a small glass. It's okay. You can skip it.

Hazelnut mousse: the most decent one with thin chocolate layet on the bottom so it's not overwhelmingly sweet. The hazelnut flavor isn't strong. Overall it's okay.

Location is ok, pretty clean, but portions are pretty small compared to the A&W on Plumb.$31.00 for 3 people on the 3-piece cod basket was actually 2 1/2 cod fillets, Mt Dew tasted like it had root beer in it-YUCK!

Vegan food truck slinging gyros off of Howard?! Sign me the heck up. The truck was located in the parking lot behind Bella's (toward Bayshore) and there was plenty of parking!

This sandwich was, as the kids are putting it... BUSTIN! Whatever the sauce they put on it was, I would like by the gallon. The veggie portion on the gyro was extremely refreshing, and it was overall a great meal. Loved how soft the pita was!

The best part? $10 gets you a gyro (probably about 9 inches, that thing was big!!) delicious crispy French fries AND a friggin drink. Sounds too good to be true, but it ain't! Can't wait to go back! 

Also got a side of the Nc Fil-A sauce, which tasted exactly like honey mustard. While everything else was reasonably priced, a small side of the sauce was $2!! Probably will do without it every other time, but it was pretty good!

We love to see the vegan spots around town! Thank you for existing, Vegan Halal Cart!

Very Disappointing!! Coffee was like dishwater- in New Orleans- very embarrassing. Someone needs to teach the chef how to make grillades and grits.  What was served was more like tasteless carnita with watery sauce over even more tasteless grits. My husband who never complains about his food commented that his omelet was dry and very overcooked.  The potatoes were served cold and had a bad taste. I highly recommend a new chef.

I came here after seeing pictures of burrito mojado where a big burrito covered with sauce. Looks very enticing.

This place is very clean, spacious, cozy, and bright from the sunlight. I arrived 10 minutes before it opened. I saw a staff cleaning the restaurant. 

The menu is available by scanning the QR code at the hostess station. I ordered burrito mojado rojo. She asked my preference on the spice level. Very courteous and friendly lady.

It's November 14 but the restaurant is nicely decorated with Christmas decorations. There's also a bowl of trick or treats candy near the door.

Unfortunately the sauce is leaking from the styrofoam container so by the time I got home, there's nothing left on top of the burrito. I was disappointed. However, the burrito was delicious, flavorful is on point. Al pastor meat is not dry.

I didn't realize that the restaurant hadn't returned my credit card. Fortunately the staff reached me through my Instagram to notify me. What a customer service.

My suggestion is to put the wet burrito in a sturdier and more sealed container or put the sauce separately in a sealed container. Maybe next time I will bring my own sealed container because I will definitely come back.

By the way, they are serving brunch too.

I ordered for delivery because of the promise of free delivery and dessert due to lateness of my order several weeks ago. However, after I got the total I don't think I got what was promised to me due to communication issue. It seems it's lost in translation. What disappointments me is that there's no receipt showing all of the charges. 

This time my chicken schawarma platter is served in an environmentally friendly container. The white sauce is what makes the dish so delicious. I wish I can just buy the white sauce. The quality of the food is consistent since my first order. I am really hooked on this place.

This place is between 16 and 17 (closer to 17 street)on Chancellor street which is between walnut and locust. It's a small street with a lot of constructions.

The place looks dark with bar on the left and open kitchen at the back. I placed my order to go at the bar area. Really friendly staff. 

Margarita pizza: very simple but perfect flavor with fresh basil. Dough is stretchy and moist. It's not a heavy pizza to eat.

Rotollo: prosciutto and ricotta rolled in pizza dough with pistachio topping. It's a disappointment because it's dry. I feel like it's not freshly made.

Tiramisu is pretty good but too much whipped cream fillings. I didn't taste the mascarpone. 

Cannoli is decent. It's not as good as Termini's. 

Small size pizza is round but large size is long.

This restaurant has a spacious parking lot at the back. Very spacious dining area. They can accommodate a couple of groups of private parties.

They do not have paper menu. You can see it by scanning the QR code or they will lend you an iPad.

Our waitress was very nice and attentive. The complimentary Italian bread is warm and crusty. 

Fried calamari wasn't heavily breaded. Instead of being served in rings, they came in bite sizes. Fresh and perfectly cooked. 

Pear salad: arugula with poached pear and goat cheese. I normally do not the bitter flavor of arugula but this one isn't bitter at all. Very delicious and didn't have too much dressing.
My entree is halibut with crab meat served with potatoes and vegetable. Big slice of the halibut, the crab on top is a bit too salty.

Dessert menu isn't available online. Instead the waitress brings you a tray of the available dessert options, very inviting.

Peanut butter pie is delicious and so is limoncello cake. Tiramisu is ok.

I made reservations for New Year's Eve with no problem.

As usual, service was great. We had ceviche special of the day served with slices of fried plantains chips. It's a perfect appetizer. Not overly salty and not overly acidic either. Subtle hint of lemon was enough to make it not fishy.

My husband had tuna and I had surf and turf. My steak and lobster were perfectly cooked. It's served with potatoes and some greens. Great flavor.

Piña colada is highly recommended, not too sweet.

At the end, when they presented the bill, they gave each of us a NY hat, tiara, beads, and horns. It's very nice of them

This place is my favorite Mexican restaurant in south Philly. Great drinks and great service. They are well staffed so food came out fast and give full attention to the customers' needs.

Mojito is my favorite drink here. Not overly sweet, good balance of the amount of liquor.

Our orders were specials of the night.

Soup is delicious too, perfect for a cold night 

Brisket tostadas: served in 2 tostadas , beef was tender and perfectly seasoned. Blue corn tostada shells were freshly made.

Flounder with rice and chipotle sauce. Fish was perfectly cooked, not too much rice, the chopped fresh pineapple balanced out the spiciness of the chipotle.

Fish tacos: beautiful presentation. The tortillas were rolled and  tied with corn husks

Yes. After a long search, this has been by far the best place in town. All barbers are solid. But Dylan is my go to guy.
Keep the good work!

I ordered build your own salad bowl with roasted veggie. The greens fresh, the veggies are perfectly cooked and very flavorful. 

Hummus is great and creamy 

Baklava: traditional and Nutella. Both are delicious. Very crunchy pastries and they stay intact. You should get these.

The container is environmentally friendly

Stromboli is long but not wide, it is the size of Italian bread. Got the Italian and cheese which is pepperoni and capicola with mozzarella cheese. It's very fresh. You can take home in a box or paper bag. To heat it up just put in 400 degree oven for about 5 to 10 minutes. Very simple but delicious. You can slice and make it as appetizer for a party maybe wit marinara dipping.

I love ordering the food directly from the restaurant because there's no delivery fee and other service fees that can add up your food bill. Very friendly service and willing to adjust the level of spiciness. 

Mango chicken: I asked for very mild but still tasted the depth of spice of the dish. It's not a heavy meal, I dipped my paratha into this creamy and flavorful gravy. The chicken cubes is a little bit overcooked.

It takes about an hour for delivery.

This is the best wedding reception I've ever had. The outside has beautiful garden perfect for a ceremony and taking pictures.

At the lobby, you will see grand staircase with a beautiful sculpture.

At the cocktail area you can find several food stations: Asian, Mexican, pasta, potato and Mac and cheese, lamb. Besides that, there's a big table with assortment of cheese, crackers, fruits, and beautiful carved watermelon. You also can pick more appetizers from the servers who are passing around more food such as lamb chops, spring rolls, dumplings. 

The ball room is big with gorgeous chandelier. The backyard is also beautiful for taking pictures.

The main dinner course starts with salad followed by refreshing sorbet. My entree was branzino, perfectly seasoned and cooked.

Dessert is also epic. There are: donuts, chocolate fountain with all of the fixings, cotton candy, pretzel, funnel cake, churros, fried Oreos, s'mores station, varieties of cakes and pastries, milkshakes station, waffles, shaved ice cone, popcorn, tons of selections of candies. Unfortunately I was super full and had no room for the dessert.

Service was awesome. Very professional team. The manager asked around about the food.

If you have the budget for such grandeur. I definitely recommend this place.

Ordered flank steak and chicken pho, and shrimp roll to go. The broth is full of flavor. However, they are missing the bean sprout, lime, jalapeño and basil which are typically served in pho. I am disappointed about the lack of those ingredients. The shrimp roll is good, it comes with peanut dipping sauce.

Cash only but there's an ATM in the restaurant. 

This place isn't spacious. Tables are close to each other. Came in on Sunday night and it was packed. I made reservations through Google, so convenient.

The complimentary blue corn chips is served with red and green salsa

I started with cactus salad. It's very delicious. Cactus is perfectly cooked, fresh and not soggy with perfect amount of olive oil. It's served with very mild cheese cut in very small dice. It's a good appetizer.

Salmon in lemon sauce is served with creamy sauce with rice and fresh steamed broccoli and sliced carrots. Salmon is on the well done side so it's a little bit overcooked. The lemon is subtle but perfect compliment to the salmon.

My husband had tuna which is special menu. It's served with beets and sugar cane. Since it's Christmas time, it's decorated with a poinsettia. No wonder I  noticed that the poinsettia in the kitchen was bald by the end of the night. My husband really enjoyed his entree.

For dessert we ordered lava cake. It's served with strawberry ice cream and diced mango. I was very disappointed when I cut the cake because I didn't find the oozing melted chocolate flowing down from the center of the cake. It's basically only a warm chocolate cake. That's why I took a star down because it's definitely not a lava cake.

Service was great. The waiter gave great descriptions on the specials.

Nice presentation of the food too.

The lady at check in was very nice and friendly. The rooms are like all other Residence Inn''s:, basic, clean and comfortable enough for a night or two. The price is reasonable. It's close to the airport, but you don't hear planes landing or taking off. We stayed here because we were delayed due to a snowstorm and they are totally unprepared for it. This morning they have not cleared away the parts that have turned to very slippery ice or put any salt down, so that's making walking conditions outside to the breakfast or to get to the car a little treacherous.
This is a wonderful place and it is not in the heart of China town.  The food was excellent.  I highly recommend this place forever to try.

My to go place for oil and vinegar. Very knowledgeable staff and friendly. They can suggest the best pairing.

My favorites are the lemon paired with Lambrusco or black truffle. The garlic mushrooms is my other favorite. 

They have small bottles for most products. You can ask some gift plastic wrap too.

You can sample with the amazing Sarcone bread

You want to visit the place. If you go there you will be part of there family.  It is a great family restaurant and you will certainly feel like you are sitting in there home having dinner or lunch.  I suggest that you go often so you can try everything.  This is not your typical Chinese restaurant.  The head chef and I said chef is a wizard in the kitchen.  Infusing Chinese with French and other international flavors.

This is an awesome place to get German products. A lot of prepared food, such as stuffed chicken, cutlets, bacon wrapped chicken, stuffed pork, stuffed cabbage. My downfall is the German dessert such as the streudel, Black Forest cake, and holiday cookies such as pfefernuse, stolen, and ginger cookies. They also have pierogies including fruit filled kinds. 

I had the stuffed chicken and split pea soup. Highly recommended both of them.

Fresh spaetzel, red cabbage, and German potato salad are must have side dishes to get. 

The crab cake has a lot of fillers, I don't recommend it.

Service is fast and they definitely reinforce the mask. I saw the staff reprimanded a customer who didn't cover his face. 

My recommendation is to bring a bag if you shop a lot because they only provide paper bag.

The crust is thin and crunchy, the texture is similar to the crust of sourdough bread. So if you are expecting a stretchy kind of dough this isn't for you. 

Because it's thin, the pizza is very light. I ordered margarita pizza. I was expecting more ratio of the tomato sauce and more basil topping. In my opinion what I got is cheese pizza with some basil on top. 

Super friendly staff, there are some menu outside. I was disappointed for not getting a tiramisu because it's not available although it's on the menu

This is the first time I dine in here. The restaurant was very busy and full on Black Friday afternoon. We were seated by the bar. Service was nice and food came out quickly.

Rotolo is a must have appetizer here. It has ham and ricotta rolled in dough with chopped pistachios.

Fall salad consisted of among others sweet potatoes, brussel sprouts. The vegetable were perfectly cooked with some charred parts. It comes with some flavorful romesco and light dressing. Highly recommended 

Margarita pizza: we ordered the large size for three people.  Nice stretchy dough with fresh tomato sauce and mozzarella cheese

Very nice and clean restaurant. I ordered chips and guacamole for appetizer. The guacamole had the consistency of soft serve ice cream. Not recommended. 

My salad was fresh with nicely seasoned shrimp. 

My husband ordered tacos al pastor, the tortillas were small with good amount of meat.

This place is a sister restaurant to south Philly barbacoa. Very welcoming staff. Food is very authentic and flavorful.

Fried plantain: plantains are very soft and covered with I think sweetened condensed milk that create a very gooey texture. Very good.

Tamales is small but flavor is on point. Pork is fresh and the cornmeal is perfectly cooked.

I had to swing by this new spot when I heard some nonsense about vegan nachos with jackfruit!!! Was it true? Yes the heck it was. I arrived at around 2ish on a Sunday, right at the tail end of brunch. I was not impressed by the Lodge (previous establishment) at all, so I was pleasantly surprised by the new decor and atmosphere at Luv Child. The menu is a Cuban fusion, the decor is very fun and pretty and the music was a blend of 80s hits!!! 

Here are the details:
- fast & friendly service
- inviting atmosphere  
- several plant based options 
- outdoor & indoor seating
- $3 brunch mimosas (get watermelon, it's fresh squeezed juice - none of that syrupy garbage)
- plant based nachos were 9/10 (wasn't a fan of the cashew queso but also not a fan of "cheese" in general)
- I heard the French toast was "really freaking good"

Aldi is a good place if you  want to save money for basic grocery items and don't care about name brand.  Surprisingly they carry some organic products such as organic eggs. There are some raw nuts, nut bar, and "healthy" snacks too such as quinoa chips and black bean tortilla.

They carry several gourmet German products such as spatzel and German cookies and chocolate.

They don't provide you with plastic bag. So bring your own or buy a reusable bag.

The cashier  is really fast in moving the line. There is an area where you can pack your groceries.

I went here on Saturday morning and noticed that there's a guy ordering tamales at the prepared food section at the back of the store. Very friendly lady at the counter. They sell three tamales in one pack. I got rojos and mole. $6 a pack. Big size and a lot of filling with authentic flavor. Highly recommend them. 

Besides tamales they sell other items too such as empanadas, steamed yuca. I will definitely come back

Very crusty bread and bagel. Fast service. You can place your order on the ordering station.

Cherry bread has a weird artificial flavor. I'm not a big fan of it.

Canele has a nice crunch shell with moist filling but it is missing a citrusy flavor, it's quite bland.

Egg tart. I thought it would be sweet like those in Chinatown but to my surprise it's savory. Nice creamy custard.

Chocolate croissant and chocolate cookie are my favorite from today's haul. 

Bagel is relatively small.

In the middle of the bakery there's a shelf with bread as a display. You can also pick up some coconut pretzel shortbread and burnt toast biscotti. Against the wall on the right you can grab some flour.

There's no sign of the capacity so some people are waiting outside. I suggest that there's a sign indicating the room capacity for social distancing

I ordered through DoorDash. The food came in a sturdy environmentally friendly box.

Taco salad with shrimp is really delicious with some thinly sliced tortilla strips to give a nice crunch.

Fried plantains with a couple dollops of peanut butter is a nice dessert. Plantains are not burnt and not too mushy. Highly recommended

My girlfriend purchased a fridge and mattress at to great prices here. We had issues with our delivery at first which is a third party company. The delivery company was a no show and no call. on a Saturday when we had a snowstorm. So the not showing up we could understand, but the no call was upsetting. However after a few calls, we were contacted by Denise Shull who looked in the matter and offered us a credit towards our purchase for the problems with the delivery but at first was not able to get our fridge and mattress delivered  the following Saturday. We were offered  the Tuesday after that as the earliest delivery date which didn't work well because we both work weekdays. So we figured we just had to figure something out. Well yesterday  Walter Jurczak the District Manager emailed me to get more details about our issue. Then today we received a call from him telling us that he was getting our fridge and bed delivered today the Saturday we wanted the re-delivery! The delivery guys showed up right on time and to our surprise were actually contacted on their day off and they really came through for us. Now our guest that is arriving later tonight will have a bed to sleep on and we have our fridge. 

The purchase process was great and the response from the upper management was great. If you want to find a good product at a great price, this is the place.
These guys are very busy. I always get an iced green tea. They made it perfectly. The wait was about 20 minutes on a Sunday evening.

Gino's is my favorite restaurant in Boise. Boise doesn't really have any legit 'fine dining' spots, so I call Gino's my favorite restaurant, even though they fired my sister. Boise has had a few really good restaurants in the past- Sogno's, Amore, and, most notably: Desert Sage. Unfortunately, these are all closed now. Gino's is hands down the best Italian in Boise and also the best finer dining place, though Richard's is up there. I've yet to go to Red Feather, but it seems a bit cheasy. I've also heard that The Milky Way is good.
Cannot say enough good things about this pizza place: delicious, big slices & excellent customer service! It's a slice of NYC in St. Pete; we will definitely return!

What a great find! Have been here twice now. First time was with a group and two of us split the tonka truck of wings. They smoke their wings and these were absolutely amazing! And yes, they came out in a real Tonka truck! The second time I got the thighs on Texas toast which was equally delicious. Their sides were also very good. They have two for one tall boys for $5.50 making this one of the best beer values around. Only reason not five stars is the sides come in styrofoam containers and they use pizza pans for their plates. Not really "bad" but could be better with a different presentation choice.
Good service. Complimentary crackers. Lunch special comes with rice and spring roll. It is OK. My shrimp dumplings are pretty good. I will give this place another try

I have to preface this by saying we don't have an IHOP where I live.  I really enjoyed this place, four times in six days.  There is outdoor seating undercover.  The service was ok, the last day, Sunday, we had a breakfast waitress full of sass, and I kind of liked it.  Of course, the pancakes were amazing!

Super chill environment with some nice snacks that offer clean, fresh, goodness.  

*** Free wifi *** Just ask for the pass.  

If I lived in this area, this place would definitely be my go to spot.  

Coffee from illy and a good variety of croissants, light sandwiches and deserts complete their menu.  

Oh, easy to access bathroom is a plus for those long visits.

The review is for chocolate and cheese bread. I asked for it to the staff and she picked it up for me. It turned out the bread is dry and stale. The combination of chocolate and chese is great, though, although I wish the filling is more in it.
Great restaurant in Downtown SB. Out of the tourist path. Food its amazing and probably the best Italian rest. In SB.
Great addition to the neighborhood! Never shopping at an Ulta or Sephora again!! Owner is super welcoming and helpful and the store is super fun! Always hosting some type of charity of event!

I used to order from here all the time. I loved the  broadway show-stopper dinner meals and the pizza. However in the last year the business has taken a serious turn for the worse. First sign of trouble was when I had ordered the show-stopper dinners ..sausage and penne. I had ordered this many times before and been very peased with nice sized pieces of italian sausage and an elegantly flavored sauce with pasta. This time however I was given a large amount of pasta and what seemed like a scoop of some sausage crumbles. I called and the young lady was very apologetic, explaining that because of the food drive they had just done (which is wonderful and admirable but never at the expense of your regular customers), they were out of italian sausage and needed to substitute. I politely asked to be informed of a substitute next time and was offered a free meal.
I never took them up on the free meal since the next issue I had was with a delivery driver whom I felt was disrespectful. After my experience I called to comment to the owner and even recieved a personal visit which I felt was above and beyond. We decided to give them a break for a few months after that, but recently decided to go again. Once we ordered from grubhub and after an hour and a half our order of 2 pies were not ready for pickup, they said the grub hub orders dont always come through and next time we should call. Tonight we CALLED to order and the same thing..we waited an hour for pick up. ..they knew we were there and said they weren't ready but then we prompted them to check the two pies on top of the oven and they were ours. Who knows how long they were actually done. To top it off when we opened our pizzas they weren't even cooked!!! It looked like roller skating rink pizza. I was livid when I called and they did get two more pies out for delivery right away but I am done with this place. The people seem very nice, unfortunately being nice is only a portion of running a sucessful restaurant. I wish them the best with the expansion but we will not be going back any time soon.

My husband and I had a lovely meal on the balcony at Tableau.  The whole restaurant is nice but the balcony overlooking Jackson Square is particularly lovely.  I had a delicious seafood salad but my demi fish was very plain and not particularly tasteful.  My husband's chicken Tableau looked good. Dessert, a custard tart, was fair.  Service was great except they neglected to bring any bread for a long time - bread was fair with butter tasting like margarine.  All in all it was a nice experience, and we will be back.

Awesome.  The first dogs were so good and reasonably priced that we went back for seconds. It was a Wednesday special, $3 for the dog of the day. We had the Chi Dog, which had pickled onion, relish (with green pepper), pickle, tomato, pepper.  The bun was good too.  Plus they serve beer to go with your dog, cannot be beat.

The spicy miso ramen soup had noodles that didn't feel like ramen noodles, the texture was way off putting grilled chicken in the soup didn't make it better either I would suggest putting it on the side on a plate, they at least gave you a full egg which was cooked perfectly the soup tasted good. Wife had the chicken teriyaki bento box classic, tasted very good,tempura was fine just like any other jap restaurant the teriyaki chicken was great, salad was proportional and fresh. 

Ordered small maki spicy tuna for the wife, it tasted fine nothing special but it was the first time I ever had sushi where I actually had a piece of fish bone in it.
Tried the dragon eye roll as well, it was very big and crunchy that it became very hard; which made it very hard to bite into and can hurt the top of the roof of your mouth. The taste did not taste on par as other places who makes dragon eye rolls, Tokyo express's dragon eye roll tasted much better.

Bought a day pass on Saturday. Waited 40 minutes for a Riverfront car. Finally one came. Waited 45 minutes for the St Charles car. Never saw one.  Then 45 minutes for the Canal line. Gave the Riverfront one more chance. Car never came. Took a taxi from Harrahs.

Great hot pot, went here for my birthday with the wife and child.
