I tried the satay base, I didn't think the taste was strong enough and was a little flavourless good thing they had a big sauce station with so many flavours which was a great plus. My wife's cilantro and century egg soup tasted great, while my mother in laws Chinese herb soup was so aromatic. The food came out fast and were nice and fresh, the oyster was the size of my hand which was awesome and it tasted great and didn't shrink much at all like other places. One of the best thing here is they make all their meatballs, fish beef etc all fresh there and not bought from other pre-made places and they were so good. I wished I bought the ice tea as I saw many people did and they were HUGE, will make sure to try next time. The seafood tasted excellent and didn't smell fishy and very fresh, they had sashimi too which was surprising very tasty and fresh.

Came here for CTIA 2012 and had a pretty decent experience throughout the week.  

Passed on the starbucks cause the line looked like disneyland.  They also offer a food court that has a pretty good variety of junk food that will fill you up at a decent price.  

Parking is pretty expensive for the day, expect $20-30+ There are meters around the center that allow you to park for 1.5 hours at a time so you can get your quick fix if needed.  

I suggest finding a hotel with a shuttle.  Much more convenient.

Some things are better left unchanged.... This is one of them. I miss the old Poca Cosa - old location, old school charm, old finesse and care of customer. The back wait staff are attentive and eager. The server, unfortunately, upon hearing we preferred no alcoholic beverages to start our dining experience, appeared to be running a marathon to deliver with rapid fire the menu's description and to quickly serve and flip our 4-top for the next (albeit non-existent) dining party. The neighboring 6-top was greeted with equal speed as their bartender/server raced through the slated menu, despite the older gentleman's reminder that they wanted to enjoy their cocktails and chips/salsa, regardless that appetizers weren't an option.  Suggestion: Slow down, take a little pride, and enjoy the art of service, allow your customers to dine: you might not win the marathon, but you might rally a few more repeat customers... That in itself would be gold!

Tucson International is a breeze in terms of convenience for boarding, wait time, and access to/from the City. free Wifi, Ike's Coffee and Tea, and mega doses of sunshine helps pass the time til boarding.

I didn't think this was anything special. Definitely a one and done for us.  Two of us went for dinner. There were a couple people at the bar and no other tables. Our waitress left I guess after taking our app order and we got a different waitress. She didn't introduce herself and when I asked about the apps she didn't know that we had ordered them . When the apps came out they were a little cold but we ate them anyway. She was not that friendly and just went thru the motions of asking if everything was okay.  The food was just okay. Nothing special that it should have cost $22 a plate for pasta with beef sauce.

Lean fixin's.  Rude cashier.  When I noticed she overcharged me, she got mad at me.  Whatever.  When I asked for my receipt, you'd think I wanted her first born.  Mediocre sandwich for just under $9.  And unsanitary.  I noticed her wipe her nose and then put her hand on the sandwiches after mine to cut them.    Yuck!  Tucson hurts for good sandwich places.

We discovered this gelateria shortly after it opened and both the owners and the gelato were great.  We have shared our enthusiasm with lots of people.  Unfortunately tonight it let us down somewhat.  We were rushed through the line even though we weren't being overly slow and the gelato was soft.  Hopefully next time will be a better experience.

So I love the taproom, the beer selection is always outstanding and the food does not disappoint, usually.  One thing that is absolutely necessary to get as an appetizer is the poutine.  You cannot go wrong with frites smothered in gravy and melted cheddar cheese curds.  It makes my mouth water every time I think about it.  I got the veggie burger for my entree, though.  I was not pleased at all.  I've eaten veggie burgers around STL and this one had to be the worst home made one I've had thus far.  It was served on a pita and was impossible to pick up, it had to be eaten with knife and fork.  It was a bunch of mush (beans) and roasted veggies on top.  I realize that it's hard to give veggie burgers a decent consistency and I see that they were trying to cut down on the chewiness of a bun by replacing it with a pita, but it was all around disappointing.  
Don't hesitate to try the turkey burger, though.

I have been going to Dr. Helsing for a couple of years and I always have a great experience. Dr. David Hesling is who I typically see, but Dr. Matthew Helsing is just as good. They are both super nice and friendly, and they explain things well throughout the exam. I've never had doctors that were so happy and nice every single time I see them.  The office staff are also very friendly, Michelle and Cathleen are always knowledgeable and helpful. 

The last visit I had, I met some newer staff for the first time. The person who did my preliminary exam was nice and she was quick, but I would have liked a little more explanation of things from her during the exam. I am used to Dr. Helsing and others explaining things clearly and going into some detail about the procedures and tests and so forth, and that usually makes me more comfortable. 

The woman who helped me pick out my glasses was also new to me, and she was very friendly and helped me pick out an excellent pair of sunglasses. She also helped me navigate through the terrible world of insurance to figure out the best options.

They have a good selection of both designer and non-designer brands, including regular glasses and sunglasses with various lens options and they also do contact exams and sell contacts. They take all types of insurance and have no problem explaining benefits and outlining choices to stay within a budget. 

Overall, I love this place and would recommend it to anyone looking for a great eye doctor.
Great old time candy store.  There aren't many of these left, so enjoy!  Most of their candy is homemade and delicious.  If you're looking for a specialty candy, this would be your best bet.

Such an amazing place! Great food- great coffee! The employees are very nice and super helpful as well. It is a little pricey but it's worth it! 

Not to mention most of it is healthy!!!

I really dig UCBC.  I'd tried plenty of their beer in the past year and finally got the chance to give them a go at their brewery/bar.  They did not disappoint.  The atmosphere on Saturday night was really cool.  There was a really good, if not unusual mix of people (hipsters, hippies, hoosiers); there was a good folk band playing which was enjoyable background music.  Even sitting a table away from the band wasn't too loud.  I tried a number of the beers, all of which were uniquely styled and offered some solid distinct flavoring.  
I highly recommend coming out to UCBC; the Cha Cha Chow truck was out there before we came, they ended up leaving around 915.  UCBC also offers a small menu of their own.  
One of the best things is that the beers are $5-5.50, and depending on the size of the glass that they're served in, it's a decent price for craft beer.

Great and fast service. Very accommodating to my food allergy concern. Food came out fast. Chicken schwarma has lamb in it. Babaganoush an hummus is good. Israeli salad is very refreshing. Rum balls are good too.

I had Chi take-out yesterday, shared 5 rolls with the gf.  Everything was great except for the rice, which seemed under-cooked.  That's the first time I've ever been disappointed by Chi, but the rice is everything when it comes to sushi!  Without the smooth texture and light sweet/sour flavor of proper rice, the sushi didn't meld together.  

I can't attribute it to transfer time because I live 5 mins away.  This is the first time I've been disappointed, and I expect that it was accidental.  

Sorry Chi....

I've been going to Santilli's for years. I went here when the dealership gave me a ridiculous quote on something and I needed a second opinion. George found and fixed the problem for $50. He could have told me anything and I would have believed him. I have never gone back to the dealership and have stayed with Santilli's since then. Get great service here.

The best breakfast in Delaware. Everything on their breakfast menu is amazing. Be sure to come early (especially on the weekends) since they are always busy at least until noon, but usually the wait is about 5 minutes at worst.

This used to be a place where I would come often for brunch, dinners, and happy hours but definitely getting tired of the ever changing standards and menu.

We often would come for the shoestring fries, Jerrys burger and a lot of other pretty great meals but every time we go either something changes (the bread, no longer on the menu, out of it) it has turned into an undependable establishment.

Not to mention it took one hour for our breakfast to be served  without one apology from the server. By the time I was fed, I had too many beverages to keep me occupied that I was too full. With a $90 breakfast bill you should leave happy and full... no longer the case here.

Needless to say, this was my last strike, and I will no longer will recommending to out of towners.

Im here right now for grand opening. This is one of the coolest places I've been for pizza. The pizza itself is great. It's about $9 for a "full" pizza (comes in a rectangular box). You get as many toppings as you want which is great. But the homemade sodas are just as great as the pizza. I seriously could come here just for the soda. Try the mango passion fruit. 

For grand opening they had break dancers in the street, and a black carpet, and gave away 215 pizzas for free. We were coming from a work event and were one of the last people that got the free pizzas. Seriously, we each got different pizzas and tasted all of them. I'm really big into good pizza and this is very very good. Seasoned well, cooked well, and very fast. They flash it in the oven so it's out in about 2 minutes. 

The inside looks great too, it's all black and white themed and tables long and big enough for a few dozen people. 

Overall experience: 9.7/10
Very cute candy shop. Famous for the caramel and buttercream candies. At the back you can get hot chocolate.

Very nice looking,very poor tasting.I bet that many people voting with high rating for this restaurant have never actually been in Italy and eaten the real Italian food. In this restaurant they use lots of cheap fat cheese and olive oil.But yeah,it is very hard for a European to find a tasty food in US.However,when it is cheap it does not hard that much as in this case.

I ordered the ribeye tacos which happened to be very small and a bit bland in flavor. The sopes on the other hand was pretty good. I ordered the campechano (ribeye/chorizo) and was completely satisfied with the serving size considering it was only .50 cents more than the taco and it was definitely packed with a bit flavor and toppings.

What a disappointment!  Don't choose Tableau for a celebration.  After calling ahead to plan for a double birthday celebration, my request for a pre cocktail on the balcony was not honored ( we were going to have to wait despite my called in request), nothing festive was done at the table, including dessert even though I specifically asked for candles in their respective desserts.  No one even mentioned their birthdays at all!! The food was fair as well.  The seafood and asparagus salad that I had loved a month ago did not quite have that special tarragon vinaigrette flair that it had before.  The restaurant's style of giving you your entree whether it be steak, fish, or veal unadorned on the plate with nothing else is just un appetizing to say the least.  My paneled veal was in edible, breaded mystery meat fried in grease with no flavor.  They were kind enough to comp us for that.  Desserts were ok.

This place is great.  I just moved to PA from Indiana and needed to sell my car.  This couple and I were doing a "car swap"--I bought their car and they bought mine. My car still had Indiana plates, registration, and my driver's license was Indiana.  I clearly had no clue of how PA did vehicle registration and licensing.  Stephen was a tremendous help and really nice about it! He told me exactly what I needed to do and where I needed to go and he threw in a few jokes to make an otherwise frustrating  experience funny.  Stephen is great and full of information, if he is not the owner he sure acts like it.  He has a lot of integrity and runs the business like he owns it (so he must be the owner?!) Anyway, it doesn't matter because this is the place you should go for your complicated or simple registration/insurance/notary/auto transaction.

Brennan's is back with a bang!  The renovations are beautiful- very tastefully and elegantly done, each room having it's own individual flair ( including the bathroom).  Brunch was very good - from the best turtle soup I've had in a long time to delicious eggs Benedict with crusty french bread with good butter.  It was fun as always to see them make bananas foster which I thought was the best dessert, but everyone else raved over the praline bread pudding.  Thanks Ralph and Terry - y'all did a great job.

Very big supermarket with affordable price. You can find sushi at the entrance. The salad bar is pretty extensive with plenty of varieties of veggies, fruits, pasta salad, tuna salad. Antipasto Bar is near by. Very friendly staff.

I absolutely love this place!! My goto if I have an important meeting or date and don't feel like dealing with my hair.  Special treat to show up at 7 AM and walk out ready for work.  My blowouts have been great.  If I don't exercise they can last at least 3 days. Since I found this place I am here once a week.  It is so relaxing.   

I have been to both locations and they are both great.  Washington Square is newer and you can tell from the finishes.  It is extremely clean and pretty inside.
Much bigger airport than expected. Very nice. If delayed they have fun slot machines to keep you entertained

The best gelato ever, more on the sweet side without overwhelmingly sweet. The texture of the gelato is very smooth and silky. You can sample before purchase. There are different sizes of cups: small for one scoop, medium for two, and large for a three. 

Everything is delicious, hard to choose. I had Nutella, tiramisu, and amaretto. The dark chocolate might be for my next visit. 

They have sandwiches and other Italian dessert such as tiramisu, baci cookies, etc.
This is a great place to meet friends and family. The food is outstanding and the service is great! Kat, the owner is always around to greet you with a smile. It's always a good time!

This place is awesome for foodies both locals and visitors. Plenty of food options. From Asian such as Takorean, dumplings, Philipino food; Italian, Egyptian, Mexican, Indian,sandwiches. For your sweet tooth; Scoop Deville for ice cream, Barry the buns for sticky buns and cupcakes, Chocodiem for French macarons and chocolate Olive with a twist for Olive oil. 

You can enter from 4th and 5th Street. The food vendors are on the sides and seating area is in the middle.

Don't take you care here! I took my car in because I needed new break pads and they were only place still open when i got back from work. I get a call that they want to replace the rotors along with bearings and other things I didn't want. They quoted me at over $500!!!. I asked how come so much since break pads are not that expensive for a 1998 Ford F150. They said I needed new rotors as well. I called a good friend to ask if i was being ripped off and he said it shouldn't cost me more than $250 for everything. So I called Pep Boys back few minutes later and asked if they could do just my break pads and the guy said thats not how we do it here. I asked why I couldn't have just the pads done and come back for rotors or go elsewhere since my truck is barely worth $500 itself. Once again he didn't really have answer beside we don't do that here. I asked if they already started and he said yes. At this point I felt like I had been trapped. After calling around and doing research I feel I over spend by $200. Then I found out they charged me more for the parts then what they sell them for online, which makes no sense. Oh ya to top it off there was a misc charge for $35 with the description of use of store tools. So apparently they charge you for their mechanics to use their own tools. Don't take your car here!

My review is for the waffle cake in the form of dog paws.

I arrived there when they just opened. I wanted to order that dessert and was told that the machine was not ready and asked me to come back in 15 minutes. 15 minutes later I saw customers wanted black tea but was told it was not ready. Only green tea was available.

When the store is open they are supposed to be ready for any kinds of orders. Customer isn't supposed to wait for them to be ready.

I tried to connect to WiFi by following the password on display but didn't work.

The waffle cake has 3 varieties: plain, custard, and red beans. There's not much fillings as pictured in the poster. It's soft and nice when it's warm with crispness on the edges. I like red beans and the custard is my second best. After it's cold, it has lost the crispness. I tasted something artificial in it. 

I will not getting it again next time.
A lot varieties of olives at olive bar

The review is for the dessert.

Tiramisu: a lot of lady fingers but I didn't taste the signature mascarpone and the liquor coffee flavor. It's okay.

Hazelnut cannoli is a better dessert option. The shell is very crunchy and definitely taste the Nutella in it. The chocolate or Nutella under it is awesome.

We ordered to go and it was a mess. They were busy and no one seemed to know what to do. It took forever! 
When we finally got our burgers home we were disappointed. Flavorless... even the fries were not that great. Totally overpriced for what we got. Overall just a bad experience.

Wide array selections of cheese and meats. You can sample cheese before purchase, even the meat. In March you can vote between two cheese samples which will be in a brackets of winners every day just like basketball March madness. My favorite cheeese is Lamuse Gouda. It's very nutty taste like butterscotch, very addicting. The Swiss cheese is great too. Brabender goat gouda is great paired with salted caramel and apple or recently they had sample wit banana jam. I was so happy that the carry the famous Van Leuwen ice cream from Brooklyn and local ice cream maker Weckerly. Sometimes they have sample tables too sush as olive oil or crackers. Their cheese spread are amazing too. I recommend provolone Chianti and the fig kind. They have prepsred food to, crab cakes are great. There is more options upstairs with seating area.

My review is for the crepes cake. It's small $3.75 a piece. There are matcha, red beans, mango, or taro.

My favorite is the red bean because you can definitely taste the red bean . The mango is pretty good too. What I like about it is there one layer that has the most filling so you can taste the flavor. It retains the shape and not overly filled with whipped cream like those at A la Mouse. The container for the take out is sturdy and you get a cute small spork to eat it.

The curry chicken is full of flavor, the meat is tender. I took a star down because the container was leaking. It's a styrofoam container. They should put it in a plastic container.

Sides: steamed cabbage is tender but not soggy.

Plantain: perfectly cooked 


Candied yam: delicious, flavor is on point. Perfect compliment with the jerk or stew.

Pineapple salsa is fresh and gives some sweet and refreshing touch to the spicy dishes 

Beef patty: nice size. Not dry at all and has spicy kick in it

Chicken stew: tender and very flavorful with enough sauce so that it's not dry. I had mine with plantain and yam. The plantain soaked up the sauce to add flavor to it.

Both the curry and stew have very generous spice.

Super friendly staff. Food is prepared fast.

I had ancient grain pasta in pesto. Pasta is perfectly cooked and pesto is perfect and not too overpowering with basil flavor.

Spaghetti meatballs: I had mine to go and when I got home the pasta is dry. I guess it's absorbed in the pasta. Next time I will try it freshly made.

Tiramisu is pretty good but I barely found the lady finger. Perfect coffee flavor.

Such a great meal. I ordered the pappardelle and the short ribs. Both were delicious! The short ribs came with a side of carrots, charred broccolini, horseradish au gratin potatoes, and a salad. The dressing on the salad was fantastic as were the rest of the sides. Don't forget to ask for bread and butter, simple yet WOW. I'd go back just for the bread alone. I am looking forward to tasting more. In addition, the service was fantastic!

You can get the awesome Sarcone's bread. There are a lot of kinds of bread for your carbs need. From brioche to artisanal bread.

It carries the famous 4th Street cookies. Also you can find selections of really good cookies from Flour and Oats. Highly recommended.

What is interesting at this store is you can find vegan salami made from figs  near the produce section at the entrance on Chestnut St. side

They have really good cheese spreads. My favorites are the Chianti provolone and the Pinot Grigio-fig. You can spread it on a bread or crackers or even use it in your pasta.

I went here because of the exterior of the restaurant that looks like a bank with a Greek architecture look. Inside is spacious with bar on the right and booth seatings on the left. In the middle and back the seatings are high chairs.

I asked for booth seats which are actually church pews, for me and a friend. First the hostess said that they are for large parties. However there were two booths with only two people in each. After our argument based on that fact, she gave us a booth.

We were greeted by a friendly waitress. I ordered house  salad with additional salmon my friend ordered avocado grapefruit salad with crab cake. Mine came with a medium piece of grilled salmon, on the borderline of over cooked, not too dry though. Her crab cake is pretty big. However it looked that it's fried. My friend tried to avoid fried food. So when she asked the server whether it's fried, she said yes. The waitress said that it's pan seared. She offered to change it but we decided to keep it. My friend said it's very good. The grapefruit with the lemon citrus vinaigrette is a perfect combination. She really enjoyed it.

I also ordered Bavarian style pretzel. It's big, made to order and very soft with nice touch of butter on top. Only available for brunch. Definitely get this.

I also ordered the veggie burger to go. Very packed with shredded carrots , zucchini, and chopped broccoli. It's served in a soft bun with fried and a pickle. Delicious.

Definitely go back.

I haven't even been picked up yet this morning, and already I want to rate this place a 1 star. The woman who answers the phone, I'm assuming the office manager, needs to be fired. If it's her business, she needs to be a fry cook at McDonald's where she has the least interaction with people. The other reviews about her being rude and sarcastic are SPOT ON. I'm sitting at my pickup location waiting on my cab now, and am so angry at this woman's condescension that I almost want to walk 2 hours to work from here. 

The only reason I called was because my train was down between link belt and Doylestown and I go to Chalfont every morning. So after seeing there are NO Uber drivers anywhere near that area, I called them. She cuts you off when trying to speak, her tone is disrespectful, it's almost as if you owe her something, when in reality, you're bringing her business. If I wasn't afraid my review would be deleted and not seen, this review would be 50% curse words directed at that woman. 

UBER! PLEASE PUT PEOPLE IN THIS AREA SO YOU CAN RUN THIS PLACE OUT OF BUSINESS.

The food is amazing. It's definitely one of the best if not the best restaurant in Philadelphia at the moment. 

The service is excellent, the servers are knowledgeable about wine pairings and what to order based on what you like. They communicate about other amenities such as chefs tasting menu. 

It's a pretty large spacious restaurant, but I would say the bar is pretty small in comparison. 

The only reason I give a 3/5 rating is because it's almost IMPOSSIBLE to ever get in here. You can't book a reservation more than 60 days in advanced. More times than not you will not be able to get a table even if it's on a Monday. If you do happen to find a time slot it's usually at an obscure very late time of night like 9:45 on a Tuesday. That's pretty late for dinner honestly. Don't expect to just walk in, however you may have luck sitting at the bar. Although, even that is tricky. I have been there right at 5pm only to find all the bar seats already filled. 

Prices are to be expected. You'll definitely be spending a good chunk of change here. But if you want to splurge I do highly recommend doing the chefs tasting menu.... it offers a great selection/overview of the menu.

The bagel is relatively small. The outside is crusty, you can hear the crunch when you bite it. It's a chewy kind of bagel. I had cinnamon raisin and it has a lot of raisin. It's really good. 

They are generous with the toppings. The poppyseed is really covered with it and so is the everything kind.
Very nice and friendly staff. The selection of frozen yogurt was a little limited in flavors and I've had better. But still, it is conveniently located in the hotel and a nice snack.
I had amazingly delicious gelato here called spumone. Sponge cake soaked in liquor between chocolate and hazelnut gelato. It's only available for a week. I wish they make it permanent.
This review is for the curry shrimp. The shrimp is big. Very flavorful curry with fresh broccoli and peppers. The callalo is tender. It's a lot in the meal.
This is a great place to meet friends and family. The food is outstanding and the service is great! Kat, the owner is always around to greet you with a smile. It's always a good.

Went in to this location as the one on Vista does NOT honor the Subway promos (feeding 4 people adds up), and was told this location is under new management and DOES accept coupons/promos.   They were very attentive and friendly, the store was really clean. They were helpful but not pushy, which is a plus in my book. Definitely be setting THIS store as "my store" in my Subway app!
These cookies were amazing! You can watch them making the cookies while you order and they tasted great!

Been a customer for some time. Figured it was time to give some credit where credit is due. 

For years, Starrs has been our go to place for easily the best in-house roasted coffee in STL, bar none. Bud's Dark - our fav - rocks, if you're into dark roast. And their decaf rivals any others out there. Plus their prices are better than anyone in town. 

Aside from the coffee, their fresh fish flown in every Friday can't be beat. You just have to get there reasonably quick or it sells out. Plus the price is right! Speaking of which, the prime strip steaks are the best in town and at the same price or less than Schnucks choice. They cut them off the whole piece right there and trim them nicely.  Racks of lamb are equally tasty. 

Prepared foods also well worth checking out. Pizzas rock. Lasagna is quite good as well. Big selection of cheese and specialty foods. 

Both Bud Starr and John Nash are very good at recommending wine too. Tell them what characteristics and price point you're looking for and they can point you in the right direction. 

Starr's has made some very big, positive strides the past couple years. If you haven't visited in a while you should definitely check them out.  

Yes, as some reviewers have pointed out, occasionally the service could be better, but its improved dramatically the past year or so and it's something I can tell they've really worked on. As a regular I've seen huge improvements in that regard.  I highly recommend Starr's.

I've always ordered delivery, because otherwise everyone around me would need to wear lobster bibs, or maybe shield themselves with open umbrellas, considering the shark feeding frenzy I go into while I slurp an entire pound of shrimp with heads in Shake sauce, by myself, in my own land of shrimp heads, some kind of oblivious-to-all-else, altered state of  consciousness. 

However, I will order their delivery no longer, between egregiously rising delivery fees, plus The Shake's gradual decline into skimping on sides until they no longer even offer free corn or potatoes with the food at all (!) (shame on them!).  I've docked them 2 stars (maybe should've docked 3), and I'm not going to visit there, either. 

Instead, I back-engineered the Shake sauce to make for myself at home, found a Korean market source of $6.99/lb shrimp with heads, and now my (94 grams of protein in one sitting) feeding-frenzy can splatter the walls with awesome sauce at a fraction of the cost. This, with as many sauce-soaked corn and red potatoes as I care to add, and btw I'll buy them organic, too. Thanks for the inspiration, Shaky!

Nice selections of signature poke. You can also build your own poke bowl or poke burrito.

First, choose your base. What's special here is kale noodle. Other options are romaine or white rice. 

Protein: raw tuna, salmon, and the spicy versions of them, and they have scallops although they are small. There are also cooked shrimp and tofu.

There are a lot of topping and crunchy options. Definitely get the lotus crisp. It gives a nice texture to the poke and flavor.

Because they have just opened, they didn't have the custard dessert, I was disappointed. 

Overall it's a good poke place because of nice spread of toppings and the fish is fresh.

You can go to the website to check nutritional info.

Friendly and patient service.
This review is for the salmon. It's perfectly cooked with some herbs on it but not outstanding. It comes with slices of soft carrots. You can pick 2 sides. So far my favorite is the shrimp.

Came in for the grand opening but one get one. I arrived around 5:15 and the line started to build. Service was fast but they were out of edamame. Thankfully right before checkout they had more for me. They weren't generous with the toppings. My first order couple weeks ago was a full bowl but this time only about 75 percent full. It's a bummer. I might not come back and prefer the one on 18 and chestnut.

Also disappointed because they didn't have the dessert shown on the board. Cmon, it's been a while and they still don't have it?
You can get the awesome Sarcone's bread. There are a lot of kinds of bread for your carbs need. From brioche to artisanal breads

My favorite poke because it has the most topping selections. Now it has rewards for every purchase by using the same credit card for payment. I believe free poke bowl after 10 points. Also deliver through caviar.

I took a star down because I found 2 pieces of crab shells in my poke. Be careful.

It's convenient because it is on Columbus blvd. 

The sweet stuffed pretzel is a nice treat for snack. The pretzel is crunchy and warm, not salty and has a creamy melt in your mouth fillings. The cream isn't too sweet at all.

My favorite gelato place.

Coffee: very strong. So if you're coffee lover you need to try it.

Kinder: has some chunks of  I think kinder bar on in it.

Baci is similar to Nutella 

You can try different flavors before making your selections.

Ricotta cheesecake is pretty good. It's light and you can pair it with gelato

Jonathan's has a great atmosphere and the wait staff is always nice and friendly. They have a really good happy hour. They usually have any football game or baseball game you would like to watch. If they don't they will put it on for you. It is a great place to relax with friends.
The review is for the round tomato pie. $6.50 for the whole pie. Crust is thin, sauce is light so it's a light meal. Nice and crispy outer crust.  Friendly staff and fast service.

This review is for bouche de Noel. Very beautiful, perfect as center piece for Christmas dinner. I ordered ahead to be picked up on Christmas Eve. It stayed intact during transport. It's a chocolate rolled up cake with caramel. It's pretty good. Everybody at dinner loved it.

I was really excited to go here after reading all the positive reviews, but I was incredibly bored when I ate there. The miso was bland, the teriyaki chicken was bland, the sushi was bland. The waitstaff were friendly and helpful, but I do not regret my choice not to return.

Delicious jerk chicken. The meat is so tender and juicy. The stew is very delicious too with flavorful sauce. I took a star down because the fried sweet potato is a little bit burnt. It's kinda a wide and thick sweet potato chips. The plantain is good and sweet. 

Disappointed because they didn't have chicken patty and rum cake

Best soup dumplings I've ever tasted -- so amazingly good, I couldn't stop eating them. I just hung around, ordering more and more food, both for there and to go. Another order of steamed soup dumplings, a meat bun, and 3 leftover pan-fried chicken dumplings await me in my fridge, for as soon as I can fit them in my belly.

And the sweet dipping sauce. And the smoky hot oil. And you can get the black vinegar, to mix with either. 

The chicken dumplings have beautiful chunks of tender veggies inside: carrots, a green veg (not sure which, but I loved it) and corn. Just the right amount. Perfect crispy sizzle on the bottom of the dumplings.

It's a really cute, super clean little place, so new that construction is still being done on ductwork for better heating/cooling, but there's no sign of it while customers are there, I guess it's done in off hours, and it will be finished this week. I chatted with the friendly woman who was my server, telling her I'd be back soon, and I will. I want to be a regular, and try everything on the menu...

This is a build your own Asian meal you can think of: poke, ramen, and stir fry. They have bento box too.

Poke bowl: salad based with salmon, octopus, and king crab. The bowl is small compared to poke spot. Everything is fresh. You can pick 4 mixed in, 4 toppings, 4 crunchies. 

Takoyaki is good and not greasy.

Nice and clean store with more seating upstairs.

I found a staple in my food. I will never come back here again.

The summer roll is ok. The dipping sauce doesn't taste much peanuts in it .

Piazza pod is a great addition to NoLib. There's free parking lot if you show your receipt.

Empanadas are ok. I had veggie but mostly cheese.

Tiki Takonis great. The pork tacos and guacamole are delicious. My big disappointment was I was expecting crab meat in my guacamole as the title was written but it turned out to be imitation crab. I complain to the manager and was told that it's krab so it's fake. 
 Essen bakery has its awesome babka 
Lil sum: only shrimp shiumai, soup dumplings, and custard buns are delicious. The rest that I tried wasn't good at all (dan dan, veggie dumplings)

Coconut ball: the vanilla cake is light with smooth coconut flavored custard filling. The outer part is a thin layer of meringue covered with shredded coconut. It's very good with perfect sweetness.

Lemon tart has sweet meringue that complements the lemon filling.

Staff is super friendly and knowledgeable of the products.

I've read some really good reviews on this place and have come to the conclusion that everyone was intoxicated when they ate here. The food was okay. The spinach is frozen not fresh which is absurd considering there's a produce store literally 100 feet away. The omelet was 10% egg 90% vegetable which is weird. Whatever, I'm stealing the hot sauce (just kidding) and never going back.

Very delicious dinner and dessert.

Roasted salmon: perfectly cooked with flavorful corn and succotash. Highly recommend 

Banana bread pudding: comes with vanilla ice cream. You can taste the banana, the bread is moist with perfect sweetness 

Chocolate mousse: rich chocolate without being overly sweet 

Overall it's a great dining experience with beautiful surroundings

absolutely loved it- the food, drinks, atmosphere, and service were all impressive, especially considering how new the place is. the menu is creative and not too flashy. our server was extremely kind and attentive without being pushy. love that the menu has a pasta encyclopedia on the back! can't wait to return.

Cheap home decorating products. The settings definitely give you ideas for home improvement.

The cafeteria has cheap food and don't forget to visit the marketplace section at the exit area. The cinnamon buns look enticing. The cookies are delicious and there are some Daim goodies

This place has sliced square pizza similar to Rione and Alice.

After you pick your pizza, it's reheated in the oven. I had margarita and marinara. The sauce is fresh, the dough is pretty good a little bit thicker than those I mentioned earlier.

I took two stars down because first there's no take out container or box. Second customer service is horrible. There's only one guy who does everything. He's very cold, unfriendly, and unwelcoming.

I don't want to go back

This place is great to satisfy your sweet tooth. Upon entering you can find pastries such as croissants and danish. Next you can find gelato followed by sandwiches. At the back is where you need to have self control. Nicely decorated and very enticing cakes including bite size and sliced cake. Next display is the chocolate covered pretzels.

Rum cake: very good with thin layers of chocolate and vanilla custard covered with whipped cream and sliced almonds. Very light cake. 

Tiramisu is decent, no signature lady fingers. I can find the espresso taste good in it but not an authentic Tiramisu. I couldn't taste the mascarpone because most of it is whipped cream. I am not impressed with it.

Opera cake is awesome and very rich in chocolate, especially the ganache. Highly recommend.

I tasted the hazelnut gelato but I didn't and disappointed because it was tasteless. I was expecting Nutella flavor. It's dense not smooth like Gran Cafe Laquila. It was a pass for me.


French macarons were ok, very skimpy in filling, dissapointed for not finding Nutella or espresso flavors.


Unfortunately the payment system wasn't working when I was there so I had to pay cash. Fortunately I wasn't over indulged with all of the goodies.

Our new favorite for cheap Mexican and pitchers of margarita. I love chili Colorado and theirs is the most flavorful I've tasted. The combo K is a lot of food for the price as well. We most recently went during happy hour and two dinners with a pitcher of margarita set us back only $38. We would usually spend $60 plus elsewhere. They're also taking covid seriously and temp checking at the door and masks on all staff. Bonus for smokers, you can smoke on the patio (we don't).

This ramen place is definitely one of my favorites. Super friendly staff and knowledgeable about the menu. The walls are nicely decorated with Japanese paintings. Very beautiful dolls are perching on the shelves. Unfortunately during the covid pandemic customers are allowed to eat outdoor. 

The outside window has pictures of the food inviting passerby to stop by.

Takoyaki: melt in your mouth. Not too salty or drenched with sauce. Perfect amount of sauce and the flakes.

Akamaru Modem Ramen (spicy) and Hakata ramen are highly recommended. The broth is rich in flavor and umami. The noodles are al dente. They have so many varieties of ramen. I am looking forward to trying more

Waiting for an hour for BOGO on grand opening. Definitely worth it. The place is not big with some seatings, it's hot because of so many people waiting in line out to the side walk. 

Worth the wait for unlimited toppings. It's the only poke that has zucchini noodles. There are so many topping choices that when you put it all together you'll get very flavorful poke. I recommend adding the snow crab worth additional cost. Don't forget the seaweed. The bonito flakes is another topping that you usually find on takoyaki. It definitely adds umami flavor to poke. I recommend adding this,

The pharmacy is mediocre but functions as intended, but I just have to mention that the pharmacy tech/cashier with dark hair blue eyes and glasses really throws me off with his demeanor. he looks so miserable and inconvenienced that it actually makes you feel uncomfortable. I've been so friendly towards the man but every interaction I've had with him he's always managed to make me feel like I'm doing something wrong. Never had this problem with any of the other cvs employees or any employee anywhere as a matter of fact. I'm not sure if it's just his facial expressions and body language that I'm misinterpreting, I try to give people the benefit of the doubt, but his customer service skills seem to be seriously, seriously, lacking. You work with people all day at least act like it! I've heard this from other customers as well and he may have been mentioned in previous reviews.  The encounters make me feel so awkward that I avoid even coming into the store just because of that one employee. I wouldn't pay much mind to it if it wasn't so in your face.  Go there and check it out for yourself you'll see what I mean. CVS should consider hiring people who don't look like they wish you were dead.  On a positive note the store has the best beauty and skincare section of any of the drugstores in the area and most of the employees are very friendly and kind.

In order to re-register my Ridgeline, I had to get repairs done to pass a smog.The staff are nice, has a waiting room with decent seating. HOWEVER, had diagnostic done and O2 sensor replaced, (paid $367 for the repair-emission light still on/failed smog, got a waiver for 1year) told they hadn't checked the other O2 sensor bank. Took to another garage, diagnostic done-SAME O2 sensor is bad, plus another one. NOT HAPPY! Hoping this time repair is actually done and I can get my truck registered!

I had the lava cake which is excellent. It takes 25 minutes to make but really worth it. The chocolate flows as soon as you cut it wit mini syringe with matcha cream. It comes with matcha ice cream. Perfect combination. Definitely get this at this place. The fruit crepes is ok not flavorful. Nothing compares to Lady M in NYC. The tangerine cheesecake is really cute but mostly contains mousse instead of cheesecake, a little bit disappointed.

Delicious warm cookies. My favorite is s'mores cookies. It has gooey warm marshmallows perfect with warm melting chocolate chunks with some graham crackers.

The double chunk cookies is ok. Not many chips in it.

I took a star down because they were out of oatmeal chocolate chips. 

You can make ice cream sandwich with that warm cookies. I believe it will be great

This place is huge and clean. It's more like a supermarket compared to Aldi. Upon entering you will find delicious cheap pastries. Croissants are moist and light. They even cary egg tarts which isn't overly sweet. Definitely get the Bavarian pretzels. It's not overly salted and not hard. 

My downfall is in the cookie aisle with strop waffles, wafer rolls, and Cafe Noir.

A dozen of eggs are $1.15. So cheap.

The reason I take a star down is because they don't cart shredded coconut. 

There are several self checkouts too

I have been ordering by using Uber Eats to take advantage of free delivery from sharing it with nearby orders. This time besides the bear dessert, I tried Matcha Chocolate Terrine. When I slice it, the sweet matcha filling flowed out from the center just like a lava cake. It's so good, there's no bitter taste of matcha, instead I find I quiet sweet that makes you want more. Highly recommended.

Very friendly and welcoming staff. The place is very clean. Has a sink to wash your hands. I was told to wait my order outside. They have some tables and chairs outside.

Grilled swordfish: milk bun is so soft and fresh, fish was cooked perfectly. Definitely recommend this.

Grilled sourdough with squash is really good too. The nuts on top gives a nice crunch.

Grilled sourdough with hazelnut butter and grape jelly is a gourmet version of PB and J. Not overly sweet and topped with slices of fresh apple. 

I also recommend both of the toast

Containers are made from paper but they are quite sturdy so they are environmentally friendly.

Stayed at the Westin during the crazy time of CMA fest, which my family and I attended for part of the time while we were visiting. The check in process was smooth and rooms were nice, no frills. Beds are comfortable but pillows are flatter than pancakes. Everybody was very kind here, but I have to add the lack of accessibility to food and drink establishments in the hotel was a downer. There is one small restaurant that maybe seats 20 people that offers light bites and small meals, and 1 full bar. There is a no vending machines for waters, a coke, or any quick snack. There is no gift shop or anything close to get booze or beer or snacks to bring to the room. The pool fits maybe 7 people if you just put your toes in and 5 chairs to lay on. Early bird gets the worm there I guess? There is a bar on the rooftop which is nice but as always very expensive for even a beer - $10.00 for a bud light. 

Close to downtown, easy for walking and has a lot of things to do around the area. But still far enough from the crazy street of broadway and hustle/bustle of the city. 

Hotel smelled amazing and overall had fun experience for the CMA feat, just frustrated over the lack of amenities and basic necessities for food/drink/other needs.

Ruen bing: it's really delicious however the shrimp is tough and dry. The wrap is very thin but manages to hold it together. Very flavorful.

Bian dangs: I had the king oyster mushroom. Mushrooms are perfectly cooked and fresh. The forbidden rice is something unique, worth to try. Veggies are perfectly seasoned. Highly recommend.

Potstickers are really small: the chicken is really packed with meat. The veggies kind are good too but I tasted too much peppers. 


Gwa baos: the baos are really soft. I had mine for takeout and upon arriving home the bottom part is really soggy.
You place the order at the touch screen. Make sure you check your order. I accidentally ordered too many bao.

Service needs improvement: the girl who helped me wasn't friendly at all. Very cold service.

If you want to have a great experience in eating food in Philadelphia go to zahav.  However to warn you plan early to get a seat nut I've beeen told you can always sit at the counter or bar and eat. It is the beat in Israeli food.  I suggest you get the chefs table choices. It is a lot of food but a wonderful experience.

This is my first time dining here after pandemic lockdown. Sansom street is closed from traffic for outdoor seatings. My husband and I were directed to tables next to parking garage. Very unappealing. Thus, we requested indoor seating. We were the only people upstairs.

Service was fast. The esquites was served in a disposable paper container. Tacos come in four instead of three as I know pre-pandemic time and as a result it's more expensive.

I ordered my usual cauliflower tacos. Overall, they were not as good/flavorful as pre-pandemic time. Now they have a little bit spicy green spread at the bottom. A lot of chopped beets. My husband gets his favorite: shrimp tacos and he said that they tasted different too.

Our drinks were never refilled. My husband asked for hot sauce because there's no more condiments on the table. After we got the bill, we were charged $1 for the hot sauce.

This is an awesome place for vegan and gluten free people.

Staff is very friendly and helpful.

Amaranth porridge is perfectly cooked the pineapple purée gives enough sweetness. It's a nice portion size.

Tiramisu is amazing. It's dense because there's no lady fingers but you can taste the coffee flavor. Definitely get this.

Black bean brownies is delicious . It melts in your mouth. Very moist and sweet.

Chocolate peanut butter and blackberry cake are really good . Very moist with perfect sweetness. Everything here is amazing
Every time I come here it's so great. Everyone is really awesome, Felix is my favorite. It is very clean, good vibes, nice people - the Best just like the name!! :)

I have heard so many great reviews about A5 Wagyu beef and as soon as I saw their Instagram post about the arrival of the Wagyu beef, I had to stop by. It is a bit over $100 per pound so I got a little less than 1 pound. The guys working there are super friendly and welcoming. He explained that the beef came from Japan. He recommended the best way to cook this precious beef. 

It melts in your mouth. I cooked it on a hot ungreased non stick skillet, seasoned with salt and pepper. It only takes 6 minutes to cook on both sides. For once in a lifetime, you need to try this, worth every penny.

Huuuuuge store. Definitely an improvement than the old location.

At the first floor you can see a lot of nice handbags. Downstairs you can find clothing and home essentials.

You can spend a day shopping there.

Very affordable. I found a lot of fitness outfits.

I'm really hooked with their tacos. My husband loves the grilled wild shrimp. I tried the fried Mahi Mahi-mahi. The fish is perfectly cooked with jalapeño mayonnaise that gives it a kick. Very friendly staff. I ordered mine to go and the food came out fast. The reason I took a star down is because it's not handicapped accessible because of the pretty long stairs. 

Great interior, very clean, and definitely an improvement from the previous restaurant (Nodding Head)

Cannot wait to try more

Very flavorful healthy meals. 
First you pick  the base: farro, brown rice, or greens. I picked greens. It's not much though. 
Second, you pick two sides. That's tough because all of them look  delicious. I picked root  veggies and sweet potatoes.
Third you pick the protein. I picked salmon.

The staff is super friendly and helpful. Very patient in answering my questions  .

My meal was so tasty. Well balanced flavor and very appetizing. Salmon is on the well done side but not too dry.

Best Mexican on the West Bank! We usually go to the Mexican restaurant closer to the house, but decided to give this one a try. Absolutely delicious and authentic Mexican food! I can't wait to go back, the staff is also great.

Love this amazing team at Tranquil! I've been going to Tranquil for a very long time now, and have never been disappointed. It's such a relaxing atmosphere and Lauren & Allie (the receptionists) are very professional. Whether you get your hair done by one of the amazing stylists, makeup done by Rita or Chelsea, or your nails done by the wonderful nail team- you will love the service! Highly recommend booking a massage or facial with Rochele, you won't regret it!

The food is mediocre. Our waitress was nice but could be more attentive to us.

Stuffed flounder is ok, not much seasoning.

Apple streudel: the pastry is soggy and not crispy at all. It seems stale.

Black Forest and German chocolate are ok, nothing special.

As usual esquites is a good appetizer. Also the plantain empanadas are another option. Each is filled with mashed sweet plantains.

Quinoa salad is perfectly cooked. I added shrimps that have great flavor and complement really well with the quinoa. They are medium sized shrimps.

Choco tacos are awesome. Not too sweet covered with chopped peanuts. Great way to end the meal.
Very good chocolate, high quality with a lot of varieties. Don't forget the chocolate covered pretzel.

Mixed feelings.  I went once for cleaning and exam and found dentist and back office staff great.  Front desk was edgy with me for no reason, but I was pleased with chair care.  

Months later, I called to check next available appointment and said I would call back to schedule.  Turns out front desk made me the appt anyway.  I couldn't make that time, which is why I didn't schedule it.  Not a big deal because I got text alerts and I  phoned to cancel/rescheduled.  Receptionist sounded angry and pissed off at me, although I was the one correcting her mistake.

Then, I get more alerts for the same appointment, which I never made and already phoned and cancelled.

Dr Denny's Email address doesn't work nor does their website contact form.  So I phone AGAiN to confirm that I do not have an appointment on a day I can not make.

Oops, turns out she had booked two appointments and she only cancelled one.  She was not polite.  As the front desk is so problematic, I decided to cancel further appointments. 

It's a shame Dr Denny's business is being crippled by unprofessional front desk person,  most of the reviews are fake.

Super crowded during the weekend leading to Halloween. A lot of varieties of pumpkins and squash. There's an area for mini zoo, food vendors, hay ride, train ride, maze. Good place to take kids.

Pumpkin pie and apple caramel walnut are delicious.  Fresh ingredients and not overly sweet. You can buy frozen pies too. Apple cider donut is highly recommended. If you are lucky you can get it fresh from the oven. Not greasy at all
So good!!! The fried chicken is a must and the collard greens are so flavorful. Chicken tatizini was amazing also

Very fresh poke. I had build my own bowl with greens but don't expect much of it. I asked my miso dressing to be put on the side for my to go. I couldn't find it after I left  the store. Either they forgot or it's mixed in. 

When you build your own, you check mark the ingredients that you want. You can double or triple it to meet your limits. The staff is really helpful in explaining the ingredient that you aren't familiar.

Don't skip the seaweed. It's fresh and really good. Perfect complement to my poke.
There are some seats available for dine in

Happy hour? Yes. 7 days a week? Yes. Is this real? Yes. But do they have vegan options? YES. Did the Bucs win the Super Bowl last night? Questionable - waiting on the recount. Might storm the stadium, tbd.

Happy hour 3-6 every day - which includes $5 impossible meatballs. FIVE dollar impossible meat, meatballs. Don't tell anyone. Also $5 wine, $8 cocktails and some other stuff.

This is my second time coming here. Everyone is super nice and the prices are fair. The pedicures are great, but the gel manis- not so much. The first time, there was dust under the polish. When it dried, you could feel all the little specs. But I decided to give them a second chance. This time, I asked to wash my hands after my nails were prepped and before the polish to avoid any dust specs. She told me to just use water, no soap. Everything was going well until I got home and noticed how uneven and bumpy the polish on my left hand was. The right hand looks good, but the left looks horrible. I was hoping this second time around would be a better experience, but I think I will find somewhere else to go from now on.

I ordered for pickup through Grubhub. Got $10 off. The restaurant is nicely decorated with some paintings on the wall.

Pupusas: pork and cheese. It's so fresh and delicious. Not hard or dry. Highly recommended.

Empanada: nicely fried and fresh, good amount of fillings but not too flavorful.

Al pastor: it's ok, there are some fatty parts that makes it chewy. 

Tamales: the corn meal is so soft but not much filling.

Fried green banana is like banana chips

This review is for tiramisu cake. 90 percent of the cake is whipped cream. The soaked lady fingers are pretty good. I barely couldn't taste the mascarpone. 

The sliced version is much better

UNREAL dining experience!! the quality of pasta is unlike anything I've had in Philly. We tried the gnocchi, almond tortellini, and sausage ragu. The outdoor dining was actually pretty cute and felt intentional, not like you're just plopped on the side of the road. The drinks were fantastic, I definitely want to try the pasta water martini next time! Can't wait to return.

I came in on Saturday around 11:44 and saw a sign stating that they were out of chicken and shrimp. Thankfully I didn't order anything with it. 

I ordered signature spicy salmon and at the end the guy who helped me with my order had to go to the basement to get the sauce. I saw only him at the store.

It's completely a different scene than the last time I was there. It seems like the store is not prepared for business.

It's a shame to see because it's my favorite poke place.
The matcha cream puffs is really good. Only available on weekends. The matcha layered crepe is highly recommended when you come here. They also have matcha lava cake for dine in only

This review is for tiramisu cake. 90 percent of the cake is whipped cream. The soaked lady fingers are pretty good. I barely taste the mascarpone. 

The sliced version is much better

This place is great for brunch. Upon entering you can find very enticing pastries by Machine Shop Boulangerie such as almond, chocolate, ham and gruyere croissant. Their pastries are very delicious, buttery and crunchy. On the right corner you can find some Dutch goodies such as strop waffles.

The staff is super friendly and welcoming. Very knowledgeable on the pastries. 

I ordered the stir fry vegetable. I asked the waiter what kind of veggies in it and I was told it has zucchini and squash. I asked for wheat toast. When my order was served I  noticed that my toast was white bread. I was told that they were out of it. The did not notify me and just changed it to white. Also in my veggies there were some red potatoes. I am on low carb diet. If I knew that there would be potato I would've ordered something else. 
That's why I took a star down.

The veggies stewed with tomato. Really delicious. Great flavor. It blends well with the sunny side eggs with runny egg yolk. It also comes with some fresh salad. Highly recommended.

This place is worth to try for good Mexican food with some Asian flare. At the window  you see a poster of bubble tea indicating that it serves bubble tea as the drink. At the  cashier  table you see very cute waving lucky cat. Lucky  bamboo plants are all around, stems of roses decorate the tables.

The gentleman who took my order was super friendly. My order came out in  5 minutes .

Al pastor burrito is pretty good. The meat isn't spicy but tender and  not dry. The rice is red Spanish rice with pinto beans,?and they put the lettuce and tomato on the side. They also put green and red salsa on the side.

I will definitely come back to try other items on the menu 

I w

Forest cakes is delicious. It has layers of chocolate cake and mousse covered with chocolate ganache. If you like mousse you will like it because the mousse layer is thicker than the chocolate ones. Not too rich with perfect sweetness.

Cupcakes are delicious especially the red velvet. They are moist, perfect density, good amount of frosting.

Cookies are great too. Chocolate Biscotti is perfect, not too hard and not overly sweet. The almond cookies are recommended by the staff. It has nice crunch and not hard.

Chocolate covered pretzels are fresh, especially the toffee, really addictive

I ordered for pickup and was greeted by a very friendly staff. She called me to let me know that the order was ready for pickup. What a service.

Pad Thai: I asked for it to be not spicy, but it still had some kick. It's so delicious. Perfect combination of sweet and spicy. Noodles were perfectly cooked. Not too much meat though but had flavorful chunks of fried tofu. Make sure you mix the sauce to blend the flavor evenly. 

Dessert: green sticky rice with sweet cream of coconut with half mango. The mango was super juicy and sweet. Great dessert. I wish they give the whole mango. The mango was still intact with the skin. 

Their container is made from paper instead of plastic so it's more environmentally friendly than the usual take out service.

I'm looking forward to trying different dish

The bear dessert is too cute to eat but it's amazing The hazelnut crust is crunchy and the hazelnut flavor is perfect. 

The tiramisu pot is very watery. You can skip it. 

The Hokkaido cheesecake is great. The cheesecake isn't heavy at all but you can taste the cheesecake part of it. It has several light layers and overall it has the perfect sweetness.

Sweet potato layered crepes has no taste at all. You can pass on this

Finally I had the chance to have a sit down dinner here. It's 5:30 and it's already crowded.

Empanadas: it's fresh and soft but still had crispness. It's not thick at all. Flavor is on point. Not too greasy. Highly recommend.

What I like about the dinner menu is you can order one taco so you can try different kinds 

Short rib taco is okay. It's spicy and that's all I tasted. You can pass on it.

Cauliflower tacos: they are amazing. The cauliflower is not hard but still maintains the form. It's accompanied with beets and sunflower seeds served on turmeric soft shells with a slice of avocado. When you bite the whole thing the flavor comes together and made great combination. I can eat them all night.

Shrimp tacos are my husband's usual so I assume it's good.

My friend had mole taco and she said it's spicy.

Fried plantain was served with cheese. It's okay I think it's overly charred.

Tres leches: the citrus pure and chopped mango gives a refreshing touch to the cake. The cake is a regular vanilla cake not too sweet but it's not soaked as I expected but I don't mind at all. So if you're expecting a soaking cake it's not for you. Overall it's ok. You can pass on it.

I took a star down because our server took his time and checked other tables to come over when I raised my hand for his service.

Got my usual of cauliflower tacos and it never disappoints me.

Salad: I found a hair in my salad, my waitress quickly replaced it with a new one, apologized, and took it off from the bill.

My husband had breakfast burrito and we goin found inedible onion skin.

Carnitas has great flavor.

Bloody Mary: very spicy 
From my several visits here I think the need to improve food prep quality. In my previous review I posted that I found found avocado stem.

The review is for the tamales that are available on weekends. I tried verde, mole, and rojos, I forgot the other one. 

The gentleman who helped me with my order was super nice and friendly. I felt really welcomed. 

Tamales were still hot, decent size. However most of them are cornmeal. Not too much meat and on top of that they lack  flavors.

I used to love this gym. However, as the weather got colder, I decided to look into quitting (because I moved somewhere further away and I knew I wouldn't make the time to walk to Sweat if it was too cold or snowy). In December, I asked the rep at the front desk about the cancellation policy, because I had read that cancellation required 60-day notice, and I wanted to start the 60-day countdown if so. He said that since my membership was a transfer from another gym that closed, I could terminate my membership immediately AT ANY TIME, and no longer be billed, full stop. I said great, thanks, and decided to stick around for another month or so.

Flash forward one month- I called at the end of January to cancel, and told the rep on the phone what the other guy had told me in December. He pushed back at first, but after speaking to his manager said "OK, you're cancelled now and won't be billed anymore." I think: Great, that was easy, thanks for the memories Sweat!

Two weeks later...I get a charge on my account! I called to get to the bottom of this and spoke with the manager, Jack, who said the policy is 60 days notice for ALL members, no exceptions. I explained that two of his employees gave me misleading info in that regard, and asked if he could make an exception to remove the charge from my account. If I had known in December that I actually did need to give 60 days notice, I would have done so in December! His response was "no, I can't make an exception, but don't worry, February was your last bill." Not sure how that makes 60 days, but whatever, I'm glad I got him to email me after the call saying I wouldn't be billed in March.

So, moral of the story...if you do cancel at Sweat, or receive any info from a rep there that seems too good to be true, GET IT IN WRITING! It would have saved me and the manager so much headache if he had just apologized and removed/reimbursed the charge on my account. I would have been leaving a 4-5 star review, because I really did like going here! But unfortunately the management and staff completely soured my opinion of this gym. Happy to be gone and will not be looking back.

The service here is the best. My friend wanted the shrimp tacos but she couldn't have spicy food so the waitress helped her modify the tacos by substituting the spicy ingredients with fresh avocado. The shrimps were perfectly cooked and seasoned. Even with modifications they are still delicious.

Tuna ceviche was awesome. Beautiful presentation and the papaya purée gave sweetness to it. Highly recommend.  It comes with a bowl of chips that are thin and crispy but not greasy

I have been to Citrus Park Eye Care three times now; 2 regular exams and one unfortunate incident with a kitten claw to the eyeball. The staff is always nice and extremely helpful. Dr. Helsing (David is the only one I've seen) is always super nice too and I always feel like he goes out of his way to explain things to me and I never feel rushed or like just a patient to him. The frame selection is good, I always find a pair I like. I changed jobs last year and am very thankful they take my new insurance too!

This place is perfect for a nice outdoor lunch or breakfast. Staff is super friendly and helpful, very attentive. The restaurant itself is small but it has a nice outdoor seating area. The chairs are very comfy as if you are sitting at your backyard. Very relaxing with the umbrella to shield you from the sun. Each table is nicely decorated with a small vase of flowers. 

Mango salad: definitely get this. Mango is super fresh, sweet, and juicy. It has some sweet lump crab meat. The refreshing vinaigrette definitely completes the flavor.

Seafood salad: mostly are chopped if octopus. The vinaigrette isn't as good as the one with mango salad. It's very okay. 

Portion is pretty big. They use paper container instead is styrofoam. It's always a plus when a restaurant uses environmentally friendly container.

I definitely recommend this place when you visit Italian Market.

I am pleased with the responsive management regarding the disappointing Sacher torte. 

The raspberry chambord is really good. Very smooth mousse with nice raspberry flavor and makes it not a heavy dessert.

The truffles are great too. I had the Meyer lemon, lemon chiffon (both had refreshing lemon flavor). The hazelnut and Gran marnier are pretty good. All the truffles are smooth. Palet D'or is not too sweet at all. 

The liberty bell chocolate is $25 and requires a couple of days to order

Came here again on Wednesday and it's crowded.

Charred broccoli salad: it's spicy. The menu indicates that the pepper is in the dressing that's why I asked for dressing on the side. It turns out the pepper is on the broccoli. The presentation is pretty. The menu is misleading.

Avocado tartare is salty. It's the only flavor I tasted. The crispy quinoa gives a nice crunchy texture. I found the hard part of the top of the avocado. I brought it up to the waitress and the manager apologized and took it out from the bill.

The Mahi Mahi is perfectly cooked but the cauliflower is still my favorite.



The waitress is really nice but my water was never get refilled.

This time I got lemoncello strip: strong lemon flavor, very refreshing. Highly recommend.

Carrot cake is moist with shredded carrots and raisins.

Key lime tart is delicious too.

I took a star down because I wanted the liberty bell mousse but it was only a display. I was recommended to order ahead of time

Have eaten here several times now. Overall great food but have had a couple of service issues (minor). Pro tip #1 - happy hour pricing doesn't apply if you sit at a table in the dining area. Happy hour pricing is Only in bar area (non-reserved seating). Their website menu doesn't warn you of this. If there in happy hour times where you sit will change the price. We were charged $12 for a $6 happy hour item because we were at a table and reserved. Pro tip #2 - the meat and three is A LOT of food and it is wonderful, order it. Is enough to split between two people especially if getting appetizer or dessert. Expect a mild to medium heat level, it is Indian food after all. Pro tip #3 - the Tandoori Chicken Poutine is just simply amazing. Order it for the app and split your meat and three. Finish dinner off with the Gulab Jamun Rose cheesecake and you are sure to have a wonderful meal.

The esquites is a good way to start your meal here. The corn is fresh and sweet loaded with cotija cheese but there's no lime flavor.

I always get the cauliflower tacos. I tried the shrimp tacos which is perfectly cooked. Nice size of shrimps but too salty for me. The cauliflower is still the best in my opinion.

Came in for dinner in the outdoor dining area. They put a big tent that provides nice coverage when it rains. When it gets darker at night they turn some lights on. 

Servers were friendly. I ordered the tamales with crabmeat. It's served without the corn husks. Nice presentation with some cooked greens underneath the tamales. Fresh cornmeal, perfect flavor. Highly recommended.

My usual is the mango salad. It has good amount of mango and crab meat. Dressing is awesome, not too sweet or too acid because you already has the sweetness from the mango.

Tiramisu is a nice dessert with strong coffee flavor. 

The small flower arrangement on each table is a nice touch for the dining area

DiBruno's carries Isgro's pastries now. The peach cake is my favorite although now it's not soaked in liquor as it used to be.

Tiramisu is ok. I don't taste the coffee or mascarpone.

The restaurant is upstairs with plenty of open spaces perfect for a beautiful summer day. The ocean blue color is the themed color of this restaurant that gives an oceanic feeling.

Service is standard, my waiter didn't give me my request for a room temperature water. After several requests I still got cold water.

Food came out slow. Even the hostess asked us if we were being helped.

For restaurant week deal $20 for appetizer, entree and dessert sounds like a good deal.

Salad: Caesar salad was small but the dressing was amazing, very garlicky.

Veal Marsala with spinach and mushrooms: sauce was super salty, didn't taste the Marsala. I could feel my pressure went up. The mushrooms looked like from a can. It's a disappointment. I should have sent it back but I didn't want to miss the movie at Ritz.

My friend had salmon and risotto. The salmon was overcook but the risotto was pretty good.

The tiramisu was surprisingly delicious not overstuffed with whipped cream.
This is a must stop after shopping at HMart. The cake is so enticing. If you don't need the whole cake, you can buy a slice. My favorite is the mocha cake. So light and not too sweet.

The bear dessert is my favorite. It's not too sweet, perfect size for personal dessert. The tangerine cheesecake looks like real tangerine. Although it is described as cheesecake,  but it not dense at all, the consistency is more like whipped cream or mousse.

I recommend following them on Instagram to discover their new creations. They just come up with cinnamon rolls with the labneh icing topped with chopped hazelnut drizzled with Concord grape preserves. It's awesome. The hazelnut gives the crunchy texture and sweetness he grape drizzle gives a natural sweetness.

Maybe it was the fact that I couldn't sit inside to eat and the outside seating didn't give me a big feeling of being comfortable.  The good that we took out though was very good and I certain would go back again.

This space is awesome. Plenty of social
Distanced outdoor steating and a bonus courtyard in the back. I have yet to eat here but the drinks are on point. I love their rotating frozen drinks. They have music, an art scene, lots happening. If you're still not feeling being out in the world you can grab a bottle in their bottle shop & take cocktails to-go!
The ice cream sandwich is really good. Thick ice cream but not too sweet, it's balanced with the sweetness of the cookies. Perfect portion size
A lot of varieties of delicious Indonesian dessert and prepared food. The groceries is vast too. Great store for your Indonesian food needs. Very friendly staff

What an improvement. The entrance is bright and more modern with the Sphinx in the middle of the room. 

Staff is very friendly and reinforcing the COVID-19 guidelines such as the proper use of mask. My friend's mask didn't cover her nose so she gave her a disposition mask. 

My favorite is the Egyptian and Chinese collections. 

Closes at 5

Cute little place . I've been here a couple of times - good coffee and Greek avocado toast ..... served on really good fresh bread. 
Service was good today the last time it was a little slow but that's ok usually just a couple of people working so they are juggling .... but it's worth it .

I heard so many good reviews about this place. After a nice conversation with a fellow foodie while waiting in line for an hour at Curiosity Donuts, I decided to give it a try based on her great experience with the Rigatoni with Fiorella sausage ragu, and that was exactly what I ordered for pickup.

The food was ready when I got there. Very friendly staff. Do not expect to have a skinny rigatoni like those from the box. This rigatoni is giant, cooked in perfection. Al dente with tasty fresh sausage and a splash of red sauce with a hint of cream. The grated Parmesan on top completes the flavor. I wish there's more sauce , because I can soak it all with a good crusty Italian bread. Portion is big, you can share it with another person, big you can easily finish the whole thing because it is so delicious.

It's definitely the best pasta in the city.

This is a nice, basic Residence Inn in a great location. The staff are very nice, helpful and friendly. The breakfast is adequate. The rooms are very basic. As with most hotels since Covid they provide no bells and whistles like a small bottle of lotion, for example, which used to be the standard. The building is old and so is the furniture. But it was ok for a one night stay and it was reasonably priced.
Very nice airport. It's clean and spacious and has lots it's of shops and restaurants. Security was organized and easy to get through.

It's a good place to watch Liverpool game. 
Super friendly owner and staff. There are outdoor seatings at the side. 
We were sitting at the back next to the AC and I was freezing. I had to buy a sweatshirt to keep me warm. I'm small and they only had medium size. I didn't care about the size, I took anything to make me comfortable.

Salad with crab cake. I love the crab cake because there's not much filler. Good portion size.

Wings: a lot of topping options. I had apple bbq, delicious.

Great experience start to finish! Very easy to schedule and book the move. The team arrived on time and was very professional and efficient throughout. Would highly recommend for anyone looking for moving services in Philadelphia area.

I recommend coming here on weekends because there are more varieties of prepared food. Now they accept Venmo for payments.

Follow the Instagram post for new arrivals

I'm very happy that this ice cream place has opened in Philadelpha. It has been in my list of places to visit in NYC. Now I don't have to go to NYC to enjoy the ice cream.

The list of flavors is on the wall. You can ask for samples. There are several options of non dairy ice cream. The pints are available in the freezer. I was hoping to try Mac and cheese ice cream by the scoop but it is only available in pints.

The employee who helped me was friendly. I ended up getting PB brownie chips and mint with waffles cone. The waffle is ok. The mint is refreshing and I could definitely taste the peanut butter.

Love how it is advertised that this store is open until 9:00 pm EVERY WHERE on Yelp and online but when I arrived at 8:37 the employee working yelled THROUGH THE LOCKED DOOR that they closed at 8:30. I won't be returning.
Great service. Ben is the best. I didn't know the style that I wanted but he gave me some ideas from a book and customize it to me. It looks great.

Average food. They offer a buffet, full menu, and take out. I got the lamb vindaloo which was ok but the sauce had a BBQ sauce taste to it which I didn't really like. My wife ordered lamb korma which she said tasted more like onion gravy. The prices were fair for the amount of food we got.

Probably the worst ihop I have ever been to. Service is very slow and most of the staff seems poorly or improperly trained. Waitress did not know the menu and had to look at it to figure out what we were trying to order. This is the only ihop I have ever seen that isn't open 24hrs.

This rating is for amazing whole wheat baguette that you can buy at the restaurant to take home. I got it warm so it's very crunchy on the outside but soft and warm inside. $3.50 per baguette plus tax.
Very cute beauty supply store. You can find a lot of selections of combs, hair dryers, and other salon supplies if you are in that place industry. Very affordable price.
Great service. Ben is the best. I didn't know the style that I wanted but he gave me some ideas from a book and customize it to me. It looks great

The Rathskeller was a welcome hearty meal, but make sure to come hungry.  The portions were very generous.  They let you share a plate (for a charge) and you each get your own sides and salad or soup.  You also get warm bread and pretzels with your dinner.  The sausages were excellent, the sauerkraut was excellent, the beer was excellent, the ambience was exactly what you would expect from a German restaurant.  And if you can be there for the live music out in the Biergarten you will be in for a treat, it is a great space.
Great location. Great food. Great atmosphere. And a place to chat with Santa Claus today. Loved the Irish Omelet.

I am a new patient to this practice.  While the call center who schedules appointments (from a central location someplace) isn't the greatest, the in-person staff is EXCEPTIONAL. I had a very thorough eye exam. Shortly after the appointment I had two (unrelated) situations arise.  They handled everything quickly and thoroughly and even fit me in for an emergency appointment, same day! Dr. Pelino is absolutely wonderful--explained everything thoroughly, put my mind at ease, and really seems to genuinely care. I thought no one could be better than my last eye doctor (who passed away recently) but I have been lucky enough to find Dr. Pelino and his staff. They are efficient and kind and very good at what they do. I plan to stay with this practice even if my insurance changes.
