Not exactly what I had in mind for my anniversary weekend.  I went back down stairs, some 25 floors below, to register a complaint about my room.  The line to get to the reservation desk was again massive and I did not want to stand in line again for another 45 minutes.  I went to the VIP office to see if they could help me or at least get someone to assist but the lady in this office had no idea what customer service is all about at all.  She could not have cared less for my ordeal and said I would need to stand in line again.  Long story short, I was finally assigned a room with a King Bed and a nice jacuzzi bath which my wife was really excited about testing out.  Again, the bath was nice but the jacuzzi motor did not work at all.

Conclusion
This location is just ok but needs a tremendous amount of work.  I learned later in my visit that the hotel had gone through bankruptcy and had been purchased by a new management group.  I would not stay in this hotel until the new management company had completed their major renovations.  I would be very cautious after that date until I had read more reviews to see if things improved.
The review is for a the summer rolls. I had a the tofu, which has fried tofu with sweet sauce. Very good. The shrimp is plain but decent size and fresh. The skin is chewy.

Best breakfast in town...and it's not even close. 

I have eaten here too many times to count and have tried a lot of their menu items. I can say with confidence that there are two cant miss items. The Tuscan omelette (prosciutto, basil, tomato, provolone) and the andouille gravy over biscuits. Good coffee and hash browns as well. Staff always provides a pleasant experience. 

Always a treat to end up here on a Sunday morning.

Friendly staff who explained the menu well and gave good recommendations.

White tuna salad: fresh lettuce with melt-in-your-mouth white tuna. 

Naruto roll: fresh fish wrapped in cucumber. Very healthy.

The restaurant itself is very small. 

Definitely come back to try the tuna dumplings.

The gyoza is made in the house

My review is for plain Jane pizza. Strong cheese smell and flavor particularly from the provolone. Nice thin and crispy crust. reminds me of Artichoke pizza in NYC which is my standard of great crust. Pizza Brain is close to it. 

It's best eaten when it's fresh. The leftover is not as good as the fresh one. 

I took a star down because according to the menu there should be fresh basil but not on my pizza that I ordered through Uber Eats.
Great place with great food! I ordered cajun pasta. It tastes great! Much better than the four-star place I visited yesterday.
Friendly staff with a lot of bagel creations. Fresh bagels and it's amazing. Try the Nutella on French toast
Really enjoy their Sunday brunch.  Great service and good food.  The live music is a plus!

If you spend $25 or more you can get free gift. Just show your receipt to the person near the exit.

I can find packaged jackfruits and rambutan at this store.
This review is for the chicken tender: it's more to the salty side. The batter is crunchy but not hard. It's greasy though. When I heated up in the oven I could see some grease on the pan

Very small store so it's pretty hectic when it's crowded.

Don't miss the day-old rack near the entrance for discounted items. I got canele and it's still good and chewy with a nice crust. I also got raisin challah for  French toast.

Nice selections of dried food, nuts, trail mix, chocolate covered pretzels, and candies.

Different types of roasted peanuts with shells. From light to very dark roast.

Big bag of popcorn either salted or unsalted.

They have dried seasonings too. By using your phone numbers you can collect points.

Bella's provides the closest thing to fresh, authentic Italian pasta that I've never had. The very second I sat down at my table, my server informed me of her Hogwarts house. We quickly moved past our differences with a few rounds of rock, paper scissors and she ultimately brought out a #FREE plate of bruschetta. 3 points for Hufflepuff. If you didn't think this story could get any better, it does. There are vegan options. FRESH homemade vegan pasta. Right here in our backyard. The penne pasta with the marinara sauce literally sent me into another dimension. When I came to, I was my great grandma Nonny, roaming the streets of Italy in 1910. I will be back for happy hour.

I got veggie burrito with spinach, quinoa, corn, beans, and pick de Gallo on whole wheat wrap. Very good and healthy. Wrap is soft and flavor is on point. I took a star down because I realized that according to the menu it comes with salad but I didn't get salad. I had mine to go. Also I tried to substitute spinach with romaine but I was told that I couldn't so I said to omit it. When o got my order there's spinach in it. 

My husband had shrimp tacos. He said it's good and the shrimp is huge. 

I was lucky to ask for flan and they had it. It's pretty good with enough sweetness and nice density. It comes with strawberries and blueberries.
Small store with Philadelphia themed clothing. Don't forget to take a picture with Kim Cattral's mannequin. Staff is very friendly and helpful

Finally it's open. Got a mug an coupon for grand opening when you spend $15 or more.

There were not many pastries ready around 7:30 so I was a little disappointed. Mostly are breakfast items.

The cakes are available to grab. 

Friendly register staff but I didn't get a response from one of the employee when I said good morning. Customer service needs to be improved especially when it's just opened. The one in Chinatown has more selections and better service.

This Asian market is not as big as the one on 11 and Washington but it can meet your basis needs of Asian groceries. It sells roasted duck, chicken, and pork. On the side of the supermarket there's Pho restaurant. The vegetables are not expensive at all. You should check the snack section filled with shelves of enticing traditional Asian or regular goodies. They have vast selections of Loacker wafer from Italy. You can find a lot of varieties of Pocky sticks. On the side near the register you can find baked dessert mostly by a bakery in Chinatown. There are more snack options at each register.

The thanksgiving turkey burger is pretty good. The patty is thin but moist. I like the addition of butternut squash in it.

Fluffernutta is a disappointment. I didn't taste Nutella, no marshmallow fluffs. one side is grilled but not the other side . I won't order it again.

I had Caesar salad with crunchy haddock. The fish is perfectly cooked with crunchy crust. The romaine is fresh

The review is for the tiramisu French toast. It has two slices of brioche bread, not too thick without thin layer of mascarpone. It's served with lady fingers soaked in coffee topped with pieces of coffee beans. Everything blends nicely and it's very delicious.

If you are ordering takeout you can place your order with the barista

Came in to use my coupon. I noticed that the variety is not as complete as the Chinatown. I couldn't find the lava cake and tiramisu. I think the cappuccino cake is smaller than the one I bought last year.

The wheat bread is thick but still moist and soft. Great for toast. I found that they placing of the merchandise is odd. There's crunch peanut butter bun in the cabinet and there are more on top without label. 

The tiramisu tart is pretty good. The filling is basically cheesecake with tiramisu flavor.

Took my '08 Ridgeline to Joe's for an O2 sensor issue so I could get my truck registered as the last mechanic shop didn't fix the problem after $367... they were busy but worked me in and after 2 hours and only $120 which included the smog and I was out the door, less than half the time and $ than I was expecting which was a big blessing! The guys are both respectful and willing to answer questions and explain things, which is a plus. Definitely worth taking your business to them, as they don't overcharge like many other shops.

Got here around noon so there were not many bagels left. I tried the black sesame bagel. The black sesame gives a unique flavor but the bagel itself is dry and a little bit hard. Nothing special about it.

Came in 7:30 in the morning only to find limited items. Mostly breakfast.

I said good morning but no friendly response from one of the employees who was near me.

There are cakes but not many sliced ones.

I had the chocolate hazelnut cake in a box. As always the cake has chiffon texture so it's very light and moist. I didn't taste much of the hazelnut but overall it's pretty good.

They need to improve customer service. The service and the variety of rolls the product is not as great as the Chinatown store.,

I came to redeem my coupon for castella but they are out of it. I came on Saturday and didn't find a lot of varieties. Even the cake display looks bare.

I will not come back here and stay with the Chinatown store
My favorite is surprisingly German goodies such as Kinder and Hanuta, which are awesome Nutella and hazelnut goodness. Get this
A very nice small version of Target. Clothing and groceries are downstairs and upstairs is for beauty and household sections.

Wish I could give zero stars. I manage a store on South Street and thought this would be a great place to order from regularly. Never again.

I went in after ordering online, with the website telling me my pizza and wings would be ready for pickup in 14-17 minutes. Okay, great. I show up over 20 minutes after and my wings aren't ready, just a few more minutes. No big deal. I'd rather them be fresh and hot anyway.

So as I am waiting, the girl up front disappeared into the back and I never actually saw her again. Over 15 minutes past and another girl asks if I've ordered. I said yes. She went to the side, and picked my order up. It had been sitting there for about 12 minutes and due to the lack of communication between their team, I was left standing there wasting my time when I could have just got a slice at Lorenzo's. And the WORST part is, because it was sitting there, my pizza was cold, not warm, cold, and the wings were clearly microwaved and tasted like shit.

Falafel salad: great mix of greens including mint plus diced beets. Refreshing dressing perfect compliment to the salad and falafel. I got tehina dates dressing too which was awesome. The falafel isn't big but not dense, it's moist and perfect flavor, not greasy.

Dates Tehina shake is unique and very good although it is too sweet for me. I already asked for reduced sweetness. It's dairy free, made with tehina, almond and soy milk.

There are other products that you can buy. I bought chocolate tehina. It's sweet and good for toast.

I made reservations for myself which later on I wanted to add my husband  about 3 days prior to my reservation date. I was surprised that I was told it's fully booked because I thought it would be easy to add another person to a one party reservation. I was seated to a two seats table so he could have been seated together. 

I learnt that JG SkyHigh serves small plates while Jean George on the lower level serves full course dinner.
The front desk lady is super friendly and helpful. My server was nice but reserved and not as welcoming, warm, and friendly,like the others. 

The sourdough bread is super soft and moist. The texture is more like white bread. It comes with a high quality of olive oil which is poured in front of you. The person who serves it is very courteous. You can have a refill for the bread

Shrimp "satay". I write it in parenthesis because it's not a real satay. I'm from Indonesia so I know it's not a satay. Satay is supposed to be grilled. It's kinda an insult to my culture by naming it a satay . The three huge shrimps are breaded in panko on two sides and fried. The sweet and sour dipping sauce is watery and flavorless. The shrimps are juicy though. 


The chocolate cake with marshmallow icing is really delicious. It's not too sweet. It's dense and fudgy.

I asked to take home two slices of my leftover bread and to my surprise I got a full serving of bread.
Overall the view is more enjoyable than the food except the chocolate cake. I think the selling point of this place is the view and atmosphere.
Excellent St Joseph cake with Ricotta filling. Perfect sweetness with chocolate chips. Available until around Easter.

There are so many varieties of macarons you see upon entering. Some flavors tasted a little bit stale but some are fresh. The good ones have good  texture and good amount  of fillings. Decent size.

The pastries are by the register. All of them look very inviting. They have innovative croissants such as peanut butter and jelly. Lots of peanut butter. I tasted the jelly at my last bites.

Kouign Aman: apple pie is filled with sweet small dices of sweetened apple. It's like eating apple pie. THe lemon cream cheese   KA is ok. I didn't taste the lemon curd until the last bites.

Nutella pudding crioche has lots of fillings but I didn't taste the signature Nutella flavor.

All of the croissants have great crunchy exterior. 

Cruffins are ok, not much  cream fillings.

We've been a frequent Chow Bistro patron since the restaurant opened in Collegeville. We loved the food and atmosphere of the place owned by a married couple who split front of house and cooking duties.

For Valentine's Day 2019 I reserved a table in advance by phone for the 5p seating. I tried to order the insider-known fireplace table. After being told that table was unavailable (drat) I was told in a follow-up call initiated by someone at the restaurant that our reservation listed was now linked to that special requested table (yay)!                                                                                                                                              
However, when we arrived, not only was that table unavailable (other people were sitting there), both the greeter/reservation-lady (whom I'd never seen before) and our waitress were cavalier and both spouted unprofessional statements about their "no-big-deal" mistake. Why did they not understand the lore of the special fireplace table?????

When we were offered the worse table in the place the greeter/receptionist-lady was annoyed that requested a different table not in the wait staff walking pattern that has the worst front door cold windy air draft.

Then our mostly MIA waitress refused to listen to me when I attempted to very slowly and  precisely give her my order before she accused me of being upset and then refused to serve me.  

Because I didn't see the front of house owner I asked a bus-guy to send over the manager. Instead the greeter/reservation-lady appeared and claimed to be the owner. Boy was I baffled.

Before the replacement waitress arrived to successfully take our order, I checked the restaurant's website and was confused when I found the original Chef Owner's information on several pages.

After two courses I asked for my entry to be packed to go.  Had lost my appetite. Something seemed SO OFF about this place. Creepy, uncomfortable experience.

Our nice waitress arranged for me to take home my paid-for dessert, which earned her a 20% tip.

MYSTERY SOLVED.

I have since learned that Chow Bistro had changed ownership 44 days earlier. YIKES!

Hey NEW OWNER.  You may have bought the restaurant, dining paraphernalia, and recipes.  What you FAILED to understand is the Chow Bistro customers didn't chose this restaurant only for the food. The original level of service and atmosphere was no where to be found under NEW ownership.

And in good faith you should delete the old owner's information.

Otherwise youre are perpetuating BAIT AND SWITCH.

Arrived at 1 pm on a Saturday, bakery was stocked with more options than your little vegan heart could ever imagine. I took 3 shots of insulin and plunged head first into the VEGAN CHICKEN DONUT SANDWICH. Four words we never thought we'd see mashed into one item description. Highly recommend to all the vegan and non-vegan folks!

Chicken Adana kebab is pretty tasty, comes with rice.

Bread: the texture is more like focaccia so don't expect it to be like pita bread. It's a  "meh", little bit dry. I won't order it again.

Baba ganoush is pretty good.

Baklava is cut in the form of skinny long triangle. It melts in your mouth. Really good and fresh.

Kunafe is awesome. You must have this. The shredded wheat is crunchy and fresh with soft cheese in the middle. It comes with ice cream. The forgot to put it in my order but they made it up by delivering the ice cream later. It's too late since I already devoured the kunafe

One of my favorite breakfast spots shared tables classic location friendly help and it starred in M Night Shyamalan movie The Happening. So worth the time to drive around the detour roads. See you there!

When you are in Passyunk area and you are into cheese, don't forget to stop by at this store. It is a small mom and pop store selling mostly Italian products. They are well known for their fresh mozzarella. You can choose the bigger braided kind or the balls. You can choose either salted or unsalted. They are great as antipasto, perfect firmness.

Amazing donuts. Very moist, light, and fluffy.

Devils food: it's a cake based, very fudgy and moist perfect for chocolate fans. The donut is fully covered with fudge.

Lemon: very good and refreshing with lemon curd in it

Banana foster: very good with strong banana flavor bread in the cream inside the donuts 

Crime brûlée: very unique with hard crunchy sugar shell and some salt. The cream is very good complement. However the salt gives a weird after taste.

Chocolate coconut: cake based, very moist and fudgy with crunchy toasted coconut on top

This review is for my purchase of the donuts. They are wrapped in paper and put in paper bag. As a result, the donuts with icing lost most of the icing because it sticks on the paper. I wish it was put in a box.

This restaurant has ornate Azteca themed decorations even on the bathrooms. 

You need to get table side guacamole. It's made right in front of you and you can select what you want in it. The avocados are mashed in a stone bowl. Really fresh.

I had la flaka salad with chicken and shrimp. Some of the chicken was dry but most of them are perfectly cooked. Shrimps were nice size and perfectly cooked.

Chorizo and bacon Nachos are not stacked. My guests enjoyed it.

I took a star down because the food came out so long. Don't come here if you are starving. You might end up eating couple of bowls of the complimentary chips.

Staff is very friendly. The drinking straw is made of paper.

The margarita pizza in Sicilian style: dough is thick but soft, nice crispy bottom and side crust. Good amount of tomato sauce. Very filling.

Veggie pizza: good amount of veggies and not overly cheesy.
Cheese pizza: good amount of cheese.
Both has nice crust, not hard or dry.

Garlic Parmesan wings are delicious: the Parmesan gives an umami flavor. 

Chicken salad is pretty big. Good amount of chunky chicken. Chicken was juicy and tender.

Ordered delivery through Grubhub, got a text to let me know that the food was dropped off at the front door. I appreciate the no contact delivery but where's my food? I texted the delivery person and didn't get an answer right away, I was about to complain to Grubhub. Finally I got a text that the food was delivered to my neighbor . Luckily it's still there so I could get it. Whoever delivered the food needs to pay attention to the address.

Schawarma is delicious, chicken is tender, rich in Mediterranean spice. I had mine with hummus. Perfect pairing. Highly recommended. 

Baba ganoush is ok, not on my favorite.

Falafel isn't big and on the dry side.

Baklava: you get 2 decent size baklava. Not too sweet but buttery. I can taste the butter. Nice crisp phyllo 

Next time I will try the schawarma platter

I ordered through Grubhub because of a discount. I got my usual pan fried pork soup baos and tonkatsu ramen. I got a complimentary red bean bao with a note wishing Happy New Year. It's a very sweet surprise. The bao was fragrant and generous with the fillings. 

The baos were really good and the dipping sauce really amplified the flavor. Highly recommended.

Tonkatsu ramen: the ramen noodles were al dente with perfect flavor of the broth. The chasu pork was different from other ramen places as it had caramelization. It came with chilli oil and seasoning for toppings 

Overall it was a great meal

I made a reservation through google and it's very convenient. If you prefer convenience, you can park at the parking garage near Reading Terminal Market on 11st between Filbert and Arch. 

Upon entering the restaurant I was greeted by a friendly hostess. Our waiter was very attentive. A lot of mixed drinks options. My husband and his friend ordered Coronarita and they enjoyed them.

All orders came out fast and served in disposable plates and bowls.

Appetizers: takoyaki balls are not too doughy, perfect amount of sauce. Shrimp wrapped in noodles were crunchy with spicy mayonnaise dipping. Edamame were warm and fresh. Sushi and sashimi: fish were fresh, enough amount of rice.

Main course: tan tan ramen and spicy ramen. My husband and his friend enjoyed them a lot.

Sushi rolls: the regular rolls are small but had good amount of fillings, not too expensive. Signature rolls: I forgot the names. I think one of them is tuna crunch and the other one has strawberry toppings with mango glaze filled with shrimp tempura. The one with strawberry is very different than regular sushi because it's sweet. The temperature had a nice crunchy batter.

I love the wall paintings depicting the Chinatown scenes.

Very friendly and helpful staff. I had mango crepe cake and red bean crepe to go. Mango crepe had a lot of whipped cream filling, barely tasted the crepe and mango. I had better one in Chinatown. The red bean crepe filling is whipped cream with red beans . It's pretty good but not memorable. 

The interior is very pretty and romantic. 

Next time I want to treat the soufflé and lava cake  which cannot be ordered for take out

I wanted to get mocha cake but out of stock. They recommended to call a day ahead to make sure availability. The coffee bread is really good. When you open the plastic packaging you can smell the aroma of the coffee. The bread has perfect coffee flavor with amazing crunchy topping and some raisins, not too sweet but very addicting. The coffee roll is not recommended because it tastes bitter. The green cake strawberry cake is ok. Very light cake with fresh strawberry and whipped cream. Basically you get half cake and half whipped creamI still recommend the blueberry chiffon. The long chocolate chip pastry (feuiletti au chocolate)is very good too. Perfect amount of chocolate chip filling, soft and moist.

I went here for our company party and Addi did a wonderful job on directing everyone. I felt bad for her because there were three groups that she had to handle completely on her own. I know there was another worker on shift, but he didn't do anything to help her at all. She did a very wonderful job managing all three groups and was very quick to respond with any questions. 

The one complaint, which it seems there were several, is that there were a lot of malfunctions in the rooms themselves. Addi was very kind to give us our time back with one of the malfunctions, but several people in our group complained that they had issues in their rooms too. It doesn't completely ruin the experience, but it can be very frustrating when you're doing the right thing and its not working.

The size of donut is pretty big. The texture is like regular donut.  It's very moist and fresh. I can taste the nutmeg in it.  I was disappointed for not getting the cookie butter kind.

Coconut caramel is decent. Not much caramel.

Boston cream is good, the cream filling isn't too sweet and it's smooth but not too much. The chocolate icing isn't overly sweet either.

Overall it's a good vegan donuts that taste like regular kind. You won't expect it's vegan based on the taste.

They have muffins, scones, fritters, donut holes, and cinnamon rolls

Absolutely horrible service. They seat you and leave you. Food is typical quality for any Chili's but service is horrendous. No one here gives a damn at all about customer service. Entire staff needs retrained at least, replaced at most.

This is the best place to get breakfast/brunch on Sundays! I've never been here for lunch or dinner, but love going for breakfast. The food is amazing & they also offer healthier meals. Each time we've been the waitress/waiter has also been great! Best hash browns in the greater New Orleans area!

On a Friday afternoon my friend and I wanted to check out this restaurant and if were lucky enough to get seatings.
The ride up was an experience by itself. Great view of the city. On top you can explore the city. My favorite site is the Art museum.

The lobby of the hotel is beautifully decorated with huge flower arrangement. On your left is the restaurant.

We were lucky to be able to dine without reservation. They recommend 2 months in advance.

I had carrot cake. It's very moist and not too sweet. However I found only few shredded carrots without other typical ingredients of carrot cake such as raisin an had coconut. The icing is smooth and not too thick. Overall it's not a heavy dessert.  To be honest I was underwhelmed because I had high expectations from this restaurant. It's delicious but for lacking of the wow factor.

On the other hand, my friend's cherry pie wa amazing. It's a mini pie fully filled with delicious bursting cherry without any corn starch fillers. The crust isn't your typical pie crust. It's super flaky with layers like croissant. It's served with almond sorbet.
The food is cheap. Water glass was disgusting and the pad se ew literally sat in a pile of grease.

Everything is amazing except the almond croissants. I had almond croissant with no filling at all. I had raspberry almond and only found raspberry. The heavenly cheesecake is light, next time I will try the soufflé cheesecake . Castella and moist cakes are very good. Not too sweet. Red bean bun is full of fillings. I had te trio macarons, the green one tastes weird, not recommended
I saw fruit flies flying around the fruity pastries inside the display. I was totally turned off by this condition. I will stick with the one in Chinatown.

The best rum cake because you can definitely taste the rum. Very light cake with perfect sweetness of the custard.

Their specialty is the frannoli., which is donuts with cannoli fillings.

The twist is really good too. The jelly donut is filled on order, and it's very generous too. You can have powder or granulated sugar.

The peanut butter and jelly is not to be missed.

Everything here is delicious .

Very friendly and helpful staff too.

This Stephen Starr restaurant is not eye catching in South Street hustle and bustle. Upon entering we were greeted by very friendly and courteous staff. This place is dark at the center area but there are lamps on the booth seatings also by the kitchen. I saw a diner using the flashlight from the phone to read the menu.

Service was great. Our waiter Mike was very friendly and knowledgeable about the food and drink and helpful in accommodating my gluten free friend.

Scallops: you must get this. Beautiful presentation, looks like an art. It's thinly sliced swimming in buttermilk . Topped with a dot of soy. The soy is salty so after I removed it it's more enjoyable.

Complimentary rice crackers is served with butter and bean spread. Light and addicting 

Japanese eggplant: perfectly cooked, not mushy at all served with crunchy pistachio. It's very good and well seasoned.

 Peekytoe crab with poached pollock : very good. It's a light entree, perfectly cooked fish. Highly recommended.

Crispy Pork belly: not too fattening, tender meat, melts in your mouth.

Dessert: definitely get the rocky road, it's a cold pudding with sweet marshmallow. The squash panna cotta is served with pepitas and cocoa nibs, not very sweet.

Great place to have both the hot pot and Korean bbq. Very friendly staff. You get several side dishes right away.

Jap chae. Not much flavor. I could only taste sesame oil. Skip this.

The dumplings, shiomay, and gyoza are all fillers and salty. Not recommended.

Beef tongue is thinly sliced and tender. It's my favorite.

The fish is ok. Squid is pretty good.

My husband really like the bbq pork belly.

Dessert station is near the bar area: big chunks of fresh fruit. The white fungus is pretty good too. Next to it you can find a lot of kinds of sauces.

Very attentive staff. When they notice that the bbq plate is burnt, they change it right away.

The mocha cake is amazing. Very light and perfect coffee flavor. The coffee bun is very moist with crunchy top. The cranberry pineapple pastry is great, with chunks of pineapple and custard. Definitely one of my favorite. The sweet potato pastry is ok, not too much flavor in it. The mango pastry has artificial flavor. The boxed angel cake is amazing too, very light with tangerine flavor. You will be addicted to it. The pain au raisin is very moist but I wish there is more raisins.

Super fresh and cheap tortillas as they are made from the machine in the store. You can choose between 15 or 30 tortillas. 

I recommend enjoying it the same day because it gets dry after you put it in the fridge.

Really beautiful building. Perfect for wedding and party.
There are bars up stairs, which is the main bar and a small one downstairs 
Kobe sliders are delicious. Very juicy.

Tenderloin: medium rare and tender.

Roasted potatoes are well seasoned.

Mushroom risotto is perfectly cooked.
Mushroom ravioli has a lot of fillings.

A lot of varieties of prepared seafood and sushi. Also plenty of options of fresh and enticing side dish with some Korean flare such as jap chae and bibimbap. 

A meal of 1 protein and 2 side dishes is $12. You can also buy side dish by pound.

Salmon teriyaki: great teriyaki flavor without being overly drenched with salty teriyaki sauce. Salmon isn't dry, it's cooked well done. Personally I prefer more medium. 

It's near Beiler's Bakery.

On the side you can find salad, including seaweed, octopus salad.

Jap chae is decent. 

Udon noodles are perfectly cooked with balanced flavor. Both of them are not overly salty with soy sauce.

Shrimp shiumai is small but you can taste the shrimp in it.

Service was fast and friendly staff

Amazing homemade chocolate store. Ask for sample. Recommendations are

Dark Chocolate covered marshmallows. The chocolate is not too sweet at all. The marshmallow is very fresh, soft like a pillow 

Toasted coconut marshmallow. Again, very fresh and soft, melts in your mouth with nice toasted coconut texture.

Dark chocolate covered pretzels

Non parelis

Triple chocolate candies. 

Very friendly and accommodating staffs. They have sugar free too

This target is small and in the morning there are always boxed merchandises in the aisles. The reason I am writing this review is because i found Tastykake pecan rolls that were out of Best before date. On March 6, i found items dated end of February. I advise to read the date before buying.

I'm a small ramen place but service was great.

Takoyaki has chunks of octopus. It's not dry with sauce. I think they put too much sauce. Next time I will ask to put it on the side.

Pork gyoza: it's small with thin dough but the meat is tender and it just melts in your mouth.

Salad is small, nice presentation with enough refreshing dressing.

My husband enjoyed his ramen

This is a hidden gem in South Philadelphia. Only opens Wednesday until Sunday from 5 to 9. I've never had birria tacos before. I saw their post on Instagram and looks amazing. 

The food truck is located on 7 street near the corner of 7 and Moore. When I got there around 5:15, there were already several people waiting for their orders. It took a while to get your order. They put the menu on the board. I ordered birria tacos comes in 3 tacos. It definitely worth the wait. Tortilla is very fresh. Beef is tender, hot sauce on the side is spicy. Definitely put the lime and dip it in the consome that comes in separate container. The broth is very savory, not too salty, perfect flavor. Although it is red, it's not spicy at all. I can drink it like that. There are some pieces of that beef  in the consome. Very authentic.

Friendly service also they use paper container for the tacos instead of styrofoam. 

Very responsive to my questions through Instagram 
Cash or Venmo.

The banana egg tart is highly recommended. It has banana pure at the bottom with perfect crust. Lava cake needs to be heated for 45 seconds. Mine falls apart when I cut it. The chocolate filling doesn't flow out like typical lava cake, it becomesa little messy. Flavor wise it is good, a little bit sweeter than its typical dessert, especially the filling. It will be perfect served with a cup of ice cream

Just opened at Reading Terminal Market near Beiler bakery. The displays look clean and enticing. A lot of seafood options and side dishes. Also some Korean dishes. On the side you can find sushi, rolls, salad, shiumai.

You can pick one fish and 2 dishes as a meal for $12. You can buy other side dishes by the pound.

Jap chae: pretty good flavor.

Udon noodles is perfectly seasoned too.

Shrimp shiumai are small but you can taste the shrimp in it.

Service is fast. Staff is friendly and helpful.

THIS PLACE IS AWESOME.  I've been telling everyone about it.  My husband and I have been here twice and both times the ice cream has been fantastic.  The owner is so nice and makes awesome recommendations.  I told him what I got the last time and he recommended the cookie monster this time.  Great ice cream and great owner.

The margarita pizza is delicious. Fresh tomato sauce, not too acidic. Overall is not a heavy meal, I could easily eat several slices of those.

Ordering online is very convenient. Food came fast. Very friendly staff. 

Everyone was enjoying the spicy wings.

Best experience thus far buying a vehicle! I love my new RAV4! My sales consultant, Harshaan, made the process easy and not overwhelming. He ensured I got the car I wanted with the features I wanted for a price I felt comfortable with. I was in and out of the dealership within 1.5 hrs, my add ons were installed within the next week and I was provided a complimentary rental while my car was being worked on. I highly recommend working with the team at Team Toyota Glen mills for your next car purchase if you'd like a stress free process from start to finish! Thank you!!

Favorite hot pot place in Philly! The spicy broth is very authentic and I would say it's definitely the best spicy hot pot in Philly. It's also one of the rare place that have Japanese sukiyaki style hot pot. I was so excited to try their that. The beefs are always very good, not like the ones from all you can eat type hot pot. Not only they have high quality meats, the service are very great too! The staff have been super nice and thoughtful for the past few times I've been.

I passed this store everytime I went to the gym.  I recently stopped in to get a strapless bra and shape wear for my wedding dress.  It was the best experience I have ever had bra shopping.  The lady who helped me just looked at me and came to the dressing room with my correct size bra and shape wear.  I loved the bra she picked out so much I bought s second one in a different color.  Not only did I have such a great experience there,  but when I went for my dress fitting,  the seamstress commented on how great my undergarments were and she wished all brides wow what i was wearing.  I highly highly recommend this shop!!!

The review is for the pizza which is available only on Fridays. The crust has perfect chewiness,  not to think or to dense. Tomato sauce is fresh. The square is pretty big. I finished eating one slice of it in a heartbeat.

They have : white, pepperoni, tomato pie with some fresh mozzarella and Parmesan. I had the tomato pie and it's awesome. Perfect amount of the sauce with balanced flavor, not too sweet or too acidic , the crust is crispy but not too hard. 

I took a star down because as I was waiting outside the store (only 2 people are allowed in the store) I saw an elderly lady wearing her mask on her chin , thus not covering her mouth and nose. The employees didn't say anything to her. So disappointed that they didn't treat this Covid seriously.

I haven't been here since pandemic and I was surprised with the transformation. There are no more tables displaying chocolate. There's a counter at the back displaying the chocolate. Sugar free section is on the right in a glass display. It looks more modern and brighter.

Near the window you can find Liberty bell chocolate.

There's only one employee, she's super friendly and helpful.

A must visit for chocolate lovers

This place has plenty outdoor seatings to enjoy a beautiful day. But, since it's a hot say, I prefer indoor dining. 

Rachel our waitress was very nice and attentive. 

I ordered Hawthornes salad with salmon. All of the food is served in an environmentally friendly container. My salad was fresh, the salmon was perfectly cooked, the skin was crispy but very salty and had a lot of black peppers.

My husband had omelette with shot ribs served with home fries and toast. The potatoes had a nice crisp and not dry. Although it looked small but the omelette was very filling.

If you want great croissants with a lot of fillings, you have to go here. Pistachio is my favorite. Peaches and cream has big slices of peach with creamy custard. 

Baguette doesn't have hard crunchy crust but moist and perfect chewiness, great for sandwich like banh mi. If you don't see the baguette you can ask the owner. He will get it for you. 

The brioche toast is delicious. I had apple kind with thick slices of apples. The bread is thick and not soggy.

Super friendly owner too.

UNFORTUNATELY you have to give stars,  but if i mould i wouldn't give them any stars. This company is the worst.  Too expensive and the price keeps going up and the channels keep going away to a higher package price. The company's cs reps must hate heir jobs because I'm sure they only get negative comments and irate customers.  THE WORST!

The capuchino cake is really good, the cake is very light with perfect sweetness and coffee flavor. I had the coffee macaron it's very hard , not recommended. The green tea castella is really good too. Blueberry chiffon cake is yummy and light. The tiramisu is s basically filled with whipped cream, not a real tiramsu. Kanelle is good, crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside, not too sweet.

The last time I strolled into the champagne bar was a mere 20 minutes prior to breaking my elbow. My second experience is attached to less broken, more pleasurable memories

The bartenders have fantastic customer service, always making you feel welcome. In between sips of your fancy, expensive champagne, you can take 3 steps and purchase a $50 candle.

The $30 flight is an enjoyable conversation starter ;-) came here on a date because I knew we'd have to sip from the same glass.

Overall, a great experience. Nate was a fun and heart warming host in our experience.
Great event to try a lot of food from restaurants, bakeries, and food trucks. Plus enjoy the live music as well

This review is for the tiramisu. The lady fingers has great coffee flavor as signature tiramisu flavor. However there's more of whipping cream and barely taste the mascarpone. Overall it's a decent tiramisu.

Fast service, food is fresh. I had vegetable omelette with egg whites. Good portion. 

They have breakfast buffet for about $10 for weekends and there's omelette station, including waffles. It's worth it if you are hungry

Garlic knots are small but very airy and not doughy. They are not swimming in melted butter either. The Romano cheese on top is perfect complement, very light and you can get addicted  to popping them in your mouth  . Don't forget to dip them in marinara.

Veggie quesadilla has lots of veggies and not too cheesy. Very delicious.

Chicken Caesar wrap is loaded with chicken. It has lots of pepper in it and a little bit too salty for me.

Very small version of Target. Definitely not as complete as the big regular store and much smaller than the one on 19 and Chestnut. 


There is Starbucks at the end of the store. But at least it can meet your basic necessities.

I ordered from this place through Grubhub because of the discount.  Food arrived very fast.

Pan-fried pork soup bao: it's very delicious. It's a mini bao but with the fillings like pork soup dumpy. Perfect size to put the whole bao in your mouth, which in my opinion is the best way to enjoy it so that the broth doesn't burst out. Don't forget to dip it in the dumpling sauce provided. The sauce definitely alleviate the flavor because it has the balance of sweetness, acidity, and saltiness.

Roast pork bao: one order comes in 2 baos. The bao is fresh, perfect chewiness, not too doughy. Perfect proportion of the dough and the fillings. Roast pork has the signature sweetness.

Additionally, they use environmentally friendly paper container.

Definitely recommend both of them. I am looking forward to trying more.

Arrington vineyards has live jazz and food trucks on Friday evenings and tonight Pie Town Tacos BLEW MY MIND!!!! The Nashville hot fish taco was so good I had to have another! I don't eat catfish...ever! I would eat another one of these tacos anytime! I can't brag enough about how great they were!!!! I will def be visiting this restaurant very soon!

I always get the St Joseph cake here because I think it's the best. The pastry is very soft and moist filled with delicious Ricotta and mini chocolate chips and you bite it everything just melts in your mouth. The ricotta fillings isn't too sweet. 

You can get vanilla or chocolate filling also

Don't forget to get franoli which is donut filled with ricotta filling.

The donut is filled as you order: grape jelly, lemon, butter cream, or Italian cream.

Very nice and accommodating staff and owner.

I am in a mission to find the best birria tacos in the city. The posting of the birria tacos on Instagram every weekend made me want to try.

I placed my order over the phone and was told that my order would be ready in 15 minutes. When I got there my order was ready. I opened the styrofoam container and found three lamb birria tacos with a lot of meat in it. There's only one layer of tortilla, which made it not to be a heavy meal. However, I was expecting a crispier tortilla the way they were depicted in the Instagram. It's also missing slices of lime. They include green and red salsa. I'm not a big fan of the green salsa. The red salsa add the flavor to the tacos. It gives enough heat without overpowering the flavor. The consommé to my surprise has some rice and chickpeas in it. It's quite savory but a little bit greasy. You can see the grease floating on top of the consommé and it took a couple of hand wash to remove it from my hands as eating the tacos is a messy process. It's very hard to keep the tacos together because there's only one layer of tortilla. 

Overall it's a pretty good birria. It's doesn't have a strong gamy flavor from the lamb.

Cash or Venmo on Saturday and Sunday. 

Friendly service, pretty spacious area compared to the other famous Ramen in Chinatown. Menu has some cartoon backgrounds. 

I ordered mine to go. The girl recommended the spicy ramen and my husband loves it.

Definitely come back to try other dishes.

Awesome franoli: the donut is soft and moist and not greasy . The ricotta filling has perfect sweetness. It's a must have here.

During Easter they make Easter bread

Sfogliatelle has very crispy shell. A lot of fillings and not too sweet with a hint of orange. I wIsh the orange flavor is stronger.

Italian rum cake is super soft with layers of chocolate and vanilla custard. It's not a heavy dessert.

The schawarma fried is pretty good. It's not too greasy but still crispy and not dry. The schawarma seasoning on top gives a Mediterranean flare to it.

I recommend adding the soft pita for the salad. It's sliced in several pieces and you can stuff the soft falafel in it.
They offer quick, good service but it's not like they, or at least some staff members, are thrilled to see you. $40 for a 20 minute pedicure seems somewhat expensive.
We had this chicken I am sorry to say it was not worth the wait.  I have made better, I am not saying it wasn't good I am just saying the hype was disappointing.

The crew has changed since my last visit. I'm used to have a friendly and welcoming service from the elderly ladies there. This time I was served with cold staff who isn't so welcoming. I asked if there's any sample and one employee said no. One employee gave me a slice of fudge which was already prepared behind the girl who said no. How rude and awful service.

During Easter you can find a lot of cute Easter chocolate. 

I am disappointed that they didn't have my favorite coconut covered marshmallows.

It's a shame that the shopping atmosphere has changed.
Try the teriyaki seabass. It has great flavor, doesn't  have an overpowering teriyaki flavor but has perfect combination of sweet and sat.

The almond croissant is amazing. The almond filling I believe is homemade. The pastry is very crispy. Next time I will try chocolate almond. They have other croissants such as pistachio, hazelnut, berries. Their baguette is really good too especially when it just comes out from the oven. Cash only.

I had mice or rats eat the chocolate out of my backpack while I was sleeping. The next day reception was closed so I couldn't report the incident. Just that there was mice or rats in the building is disgusting! Especially because I was on the 4th floor! This ruined my trip to Philadelphia because all my clothes were ruined by the rats! Will never visit again. I couldn't hear the rats gnawing my chocolate and clothes because there was really loud construction across the street. I was terrified a rat would crawl on me while I slept.

If only I could give negative star for this review. I came in right after they are open to order summer rolls from the menu. I was told it took 15 minutes. 

While I was waiting I observed that the employees were doing meal preparation in the dining area which I don't think appropriate. One guy lit up incense for his beliefs right by the entrance door so I could smell the incense by the door.


After 20 minutes wait I asked where my order was and I was told that they didn't make it that morning and gave my money back.

That's the most horrible restaurant experience I've ever had. I would never go back again. It's very rude.

The dirtiest gym I have seen. It just gets worse. It doesn't matter how many people leave or complain. Cans always overflowing. Make sure you sanitize everything you touch. Parking lot always trashy. #dirty #outdatedfitnessclasses @lafitness #largo #florida #norecycling

If you want great croissants with a lot of fillings, you have to go here. Pistachio is my favorite. Peaches and cream has big slices of peach with creamy custard. 

Baguette doesn't have crunchy crust but moist and perfect chewiness, great for sandwich like banh mi. If you don't see the baguette you can ask the owner. He will get it from the back 

Super friendly owner too.

If you want fresh guacamole, you will like this place because it offers table-side guacamole so you can customize it based on your preference.

The restaurant is spacious, however the colorful lighting where I was sitting was not good for taking Instagram worthy pictures. My food pictures look blue.

Staff is friendly and attentive. Food came out fast. They provide complimentary chips and salsa. I enjoyed the salsa, not too spicy.

Tamales: it had minced pork, it's ok, not too much flavor, you can skip it.

Tostones is dry and the breading makes it hard.

Taco shrimp salad: it's my favorite. It's served is fried tortilla bowl. Shrimp is big and fresh.

Churros is a good choice for dessert. Crunchy and fresh with chocolate drizzle on top.

Fried ice cream: it's a big ball of vanilla ice cream with toasted shredded coconut around it served in a small fried tortilla bowl. I recommend sharing it because it's quite big.

If you are looking for a dessert place that make you feel like in a Downton Abbey scene, I recommend this place to enjoy an afternoon tea.

The teapot was warmed, with a beautiful tea set. I got oolong tea, very nice flavor.

My friend enjoyed the crepe cake

Multigrain bread: very soft and light.

Lemon cronut: it is amazing. Very crunchy pastry with refreshing lemon filling. Perfect summer dessert.

Bombolino: is filled with sweet chocolate chocolate cream filling. Verylight and perfect sweetness.

Walnut in chocolate bread: very delicious , the chocolate cake has perfect level of sweetness with smooth walnut paste filling

Pastry with boston cream and red bean has more of the sweet cream that burst and all over your hand, I was expecting more red bean filling. Very sweet.

Almond pastry has enough almond paste filling without overly sweet.

Chocolate ganache cake: very light cake between chocolate whipped cream.

I went to the insurance company next door, and as I was parking in the lot on the other end of this daycare, I heard a woman screaming at a whole table of 1-3 year olds. This woman, Kelsey, was bent over screaming at the child with her face about a foot away from the child's face. I drove over to the fence and told her that she shouldn't be treating someone else's kid that way. I told her that the ONLY reason the little boy was crying was because Kelsey was screaming in his face. A worker next to her in a red shirt proceeded to tell me that if I had an issue, I could leave or go talk to their director. I went in to discuss with the director that a whole table of 1-3 yr olds were crying while being screamed at in the face. The director said she would talk to them. Meanwhile, one of the agents in the office next door mentioned that he could hear an adult screaming from inside the office as well. Very unprofessional. I would never send my children to this daycare.
New item to try is the mochi donuts. It has some chewiness compared to regular donuts. All of the kinds are delicious .

I've been seeing their Instagram posts that enticed me to check it out.

This place is near the corner of 7 and chestnut. 

Upon entering you can find eating area, on the right you can find a freezer full of imported Italian dessert. So many options. On the left are prepared food such as salad, pasta, and other Italian dishes. On the opposite side of the fridge is the display of various pizzas that you can buy by the slice.

I bought margarita pizza and square upside down pizza (cheese is under the pizza sauce). The pizzas were reheated before serving. 

Margarita pizza: the crust is light crisp, so delicious.

Upside down pizza: the dough is thicker but still has a light crisp, strong garlic flavor with a touch of crushed red pepper, and melty cheese underneath the sauce. 

I enjoyed both. 

Highly recommended this place

We tried this place on a whim, knowing of its existence, but not always in the mood for mediterranean cuisine.  I am so glad that we did.  You might wait a bit to be served, but it's beyond worth it.  Our experience was consistent with other reviews where the owner (?) cooks, cleans, waits, and buses.  After he took our order, our appetizer (chickpeas in a yogurt sauce) was out in a couple minutes.  He was happy to select a Stella Artois for me when I asked for a light beer.  Our food quickly followed the appetizer, I got chopped gyro meat in hummus and fava bean puree, the gf got falafel.  Both were moan worthy, even the pita was perfect: warm, lightly grilled and fluffy.  

We took some dessert home - turtle cheesecake and baklava.  Do get some dessert if you decide to try this place!

The owner was so friendly and makes you want to come back, the food is amazing and gives any other mediterranean food in STL a run for its money.
Chapalas is the best Mexican restaurant in the Boise area- if you get out towards Caldwell I think there are some better ones. Too bad they closed the one downtown.
Do not come at lunch if you are on a limited time frame.  What a mess!!!! 15 min to order and 20 min to get food. Never again for me

I walked into Sultan Palace on a whim last night, just looking to get a takeout falafel sandwich.  I was informed that they just opened this past Monday, and they're still getting set up in the back.  The dining room is set up and very nicely remodeled.  For such a large space, they did a good job of making it decently cozy - I think the addition of some rugs on the walls and more pillows in the windows would warm things up a bit more in preparation for the coming chill.  
The place was empty (it was early) and the staff was around the register.  Everyone was very welcoming and helpful, I ordered my falafel and some baba ganoush to-go.  I was offered some hot tea which had a beautiful sage aroma and was already sweetened.  I was offered a seat in the dining room and sipped on my tea while my food was prepared.  My order was ready by the time I was done with my tea.
The baba ganoush was beautifully prepared - a little bit soupy with the perfect amount of garlic coming through and hitting you in the face.  The pitas (home made) are puffy and doughy - thicker than what I'm used to, but they worked well for dipping and even for the sandwich.  The falafel did not have a crunchy exterior, but the flavor was spot-on - the added tahini, lettuce, tomato and pickled veg (I think it was a pickled slaw) added the tang that I was looking for.  I have no doubt that the sandwich would have been even better had I eaten in. 
Here's the kicker - it's sooooo cheap!  I was astounded at how low the prices are - I paid less than $9 for that meal and was stuffed.  So if you find yourself in Dutchtown South, give Sultan's Palace a try.  I'm excited to go back and try more off their menu.

A forgettable lunch.

The bright spot was the staff who, other than not yelling RUN, did a great job.  This restaurant seems dated.

I had the smoked meat sandwich.  It was not great.  I have lived in Montreal and spent many days at Ben's and Schwartz's.  This sandwich was nowhere near that.  As well, the fries were not crisp.  A touch soggy and bland.  

These folks need to up their game.  Until then there are better choices.

My husband and I had a delicious breakfast at Panola's - the omelets are well prepared and come with grits and a biscuit/ toast. The crayfish ettouffe omelet was very good and the grits a good accompaniment. I'm not sure which was better. And the biscuit is one of the best in the city. Hot coffee regularly filled up made our breakfast a perfect meal. Kudos to our very nice server, Danielle.

My friend and I visited Dino's last night for happy hour--the drink specials are great--we had $5 glasses of wine. The appetizers were in the $10 range with $2 off for happy hour. We had flatbread, crab dip and parmesan fries. Everything was delicious! We ended up staying for the Snow Show! What a treat--a small venue, very talented singers, and a surprise ending to the show. I'm looking forward to going back! My parents also had multiple dinners here. A true gem to have in Glenside!

Ate here several years ago and it was amazing-- would've given it 5 stars then.  However, this time the food didn't even get close to expectations from previous dining here and at other Besh restaurants.  We did order the special August Coolinary menu, so maybe we were being punished for that!   Service, however, was excellent.

Made reservations for six on a Tuesday night.  The service was ok but the place was pretty empty and it was clear they did not want us to stay late.  The sushi was good, not great and the other dishes were nothing special. No beer on tap.  Probably would not visit this place again if I had the chance.

We had a nice dinner at Tommy's on Valentine Day.  The oysters Tommy were refreshingly light with a smokey taste, the avocado with crabmeat was good but definitely needed more crabmeat, and veal piccata was perfect to split for an entree.  The bananas foster bread pudding was delicious.  I love the ambience of Tommy's but the service was a little suspect.  We were seated at a table in the middle of the room ( kind of an afterthought table) and we asked for another table since there were lots of available ones.  They said they were reserved. After I pointed out that we reserved a table as well, they managed to find us a better table.  Also, instead of explaining  the specials to just our table, our waitress combined us with another table and told us both what the specials were - good thing we have good hearing.

The lunch special is great with extra fast service! It's about $8 for a noodle entree with tofu. It comes with an appetizer (spring roll) and a bowl of soup. The pad se ew was really good. Order it mild if you're not a spice fan because medium was over the top. I'm a fan of peanut sauce, but really can't get into it from here.

I've been wanting to try this restaurant and I was not disappointed!! This is a small restaurant so I would recommend having a reservation, thankfully they were able to seat us right away! I ordered the Godzilla roll because it was super unique! It has shrimp, tempura, eel, avocado and it was topped with strawberries, crushed macadamias nuts and honey. Sounds kinda weird but it was sooo good!!!!!! I like trying unique sushi and I've never had strawberry in my sushi that's for sure! The second roll I ordered was the 4-8-15-16-23-42 roll, which was also delicious!!! It was wrapped in a pickled daikon, which I've never had before. And there was tuna, salmon, yellowtail, avocado and mango! I love when sushi rolls have mango! The fish was super fresh and it was so delicious!! I would absolutely come here again to try more rolls!!!!!!

Love this place... the food is spot on and very affordable.  Owner and staff were friendly and helpful.  Excited to have a place like this in my neighborhood.  I recommend any of the Pho dishes, Hot Pot, Bahn Mi.

The mango mille crepes is awesome. Definitely get this. It's served with chunks of fresh and sweet mango. Really refreshing. The matcha one is ok, you can pass on this one. We were around 2, I wanted the motchi but I was told it is available at 3. I also wanted the black sesame paste dessert but it's not available. Very disappointed .

The mango pocket is basically abig chunk of mango and whipped cream wrapped in a crepe. It's ok, nothing special.

Next time I want to try the shaved ice.

We had a delicious meal tonight celebrating a friend's birthday.  They first served us complimentary crabmeat ravioli appetizers. The crab salad was thoroughly enjoyed. as were the fish entrees- my pompano was very good with crabmeat on top.  They very kindly split it in half in the kitchen for two of us to eat - a perfect size for light eaters.  The birthday boy was served  doberge cake with a candle for dessert and was also given a gift certificate.  It was a great place to celebrate a birthday!

This joint has the best take out hoagies, cheesesteaks and pies around. 
They do all the old world style sammies with the seeded rolls. Even the wings are super which usually you get one or the other. They know what's up at this place!

They even wrap everything up just right  so you can reheat right in the oven, and delivery is quick. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is because I've never actually been inside the spot.
Great dim sum, highly recommended. Very crowded on Sunday afternoon. Fortunately I made reservation online.

GREAT food and service!!! Always a pleasant experience dining here!  One of my favorite restaurants in Manayunk by far!  The food choices change with the season and the beer choices change often.  The staff is always pleasant and the service is quick.  Definitely recommend if you are looking for a quick, moderately priced meal!
Friendly staff. Knowledgeable. Large variety of trees, plants, pottery, garden fare available.  Nice to see that some things don't change...  still as reliable as when they first opened!

Arturo runs a wonderful  restaurant; he is a "keeper!" 
The service was excellent, as was the food !
I have heard the happy hours are great, as well!  Bob and Donna will be back!

Amazing dinner. Truly Iron Chef quality food. Beth our waitress is very knowledgeable in describing the menu.
Appetizers: wagyu dumplings. The meat melts in your mouth. The broth is perfect. Definitely get this. Also tofu made right at the table. It started with soy milk mixed with salt water. After covered for 10 minutes, voila, you get tofu served with very tasty sauce.
Soup: ramen. The noodles is very silky.
Main course: black cod. Very delicious. The meat is firm but very smooth. The miso sauce is amazing. I could really lick the plate clean. Highly recommend.
Desert: definitely get the fiery chocolate. The chocolate ball is lit up and melts it. Very high quality chocolates.
A great latte!  Plus, the interior of this new location is bright and inviting.  Fans of mid century modern will appreciate the vintage décor.

Amazing burgers and fries and a really cute outdoor patio.  The service is excellent, but I wish they had paper menus.  If you're out on the patio, you have to go hover over other people's tables and squint at the blackboards to see what's available.  That can't be fun if you're the one at those tables, trying to eat.

I'll definitely be back.

Been here a few times it was great at first, love the food on the weekends with the sashimi, snow crab legs, and the Peking duck ( this one is harder to refill and get you have to wait a while). Wish they would change the menu or change up how they make the food it's been the same menu for so long in which you will get tired of even when you only come once in a while. But good service, but I feel the food tastes the best on Saturday might be a diff cook or when they get their ingredients.

My girlfriend bought a used MDX here on her first vist. Sung was very helpfull sales rep and she was able to drive the car home that day. There was some corner damage that they said they would take care of when we set up an appointment. We then discovered the Blue Tooth was not working right before leaving the lot and were assured it would be taken care of. To my girlfriends delight, they have taken care of everything they said they would, and she is now going to pick her car back up. Great cars and great staff!

Another CWE mainstay, The Scottish Arms is a very easy stroll down the block.  They get busy, but if you go early on a Fri or Sat, you should be fine.  The chef is always doing cool stuff like buying a whole hog and using it in specials throughout the week.  They're currently transitioning to the winter menu and it's looking good!  I had a filet wrapped in pancetta from Salume Beddu, rubbed with KaKao chocolate.  Served with mashies and sauteed spinach and onions.  

FANTASTIC.

Our dining experience was a real trip down memory lane.  I loved seeing the old ( and new ) artwork in the foyer, bar and dining room.  The ambience and service ( Brett) was wonderful.  The food reminded me of other local restaurants ( I guess John Besh)-- the Parkerhouse rolls with sea salt, the lightly fried oysters, and the stuffed squash blossoms with pickled vegetables (mmm - delicious). The crab remick was a Pontchartrain throwback- very good as well as the Mile High Pie.  While the pie as good, it would be even better if it was more like the original - a regular pie crust and much more meringue. The pecan pie was only ok.  The restaurant needs its distinctive cuisine- maybe it could be an old fashioned Creole restaurant ( similar to Galatoire's) with a few of the former Caribbean Room's key dishes such as Mile High Pie.

This place is a MUST if you visit Nashville. If you come here, you absolutely MUST try their ribs, they are a staple of this place. Smoky taste and just melts in your mouth. It's a shame that BBQ places down in Tampa where I live cannot make their ribs this good. I will most definitely be back for more!
Brooke was a great waitress. If you get a good waitress here its really good, if not then you're going to have a bad time. I come for the Daytona Beach wings, which are great.
A bit overpriced for what you get but at least it's not chef Boyardee like you get somewhere like olive garden.

This place is amazing! I went here on my birthday and the waitress was so nice and funny! She really made us feel right at home.

I ordered the spring rolls, which were so amazing I ordered another round of them! I also got the pad thai noodles which were so delicious!! I would absolutely come back and order again! It's also great that the restaurant is BYOB!!

Great bar.  I've gone multiple times and the service has always been good.  One of the times there it took the servers some time to realize that we had not been served, but once they realized they were very apologetic and served us very well the rest of the night.  I really enjoy Wednesday night trivia.

Decor is great but that's not why you come to a nail salon, you come for the experience and relaxation. Seems that is forgotten here. I timed my pedicure from start to finish and it was 18 minutes long. Maybe I'm spoiled in the city but every place I go to is 30-35 MIN with many other extras! (Great leg massage, back massage, drinks etc). The entire thing felt rushed and I was not relaxed whatsoever. Thank you but I will take my business elsewhere on the Main Line and JC Fancy when in Center City!

As soon as we walked in, we were greeted by several smiling faces. Got a table on the patio, which is beautiful! The food was amazing, and our server Lauren was the absolute sweetest. She was the perfect mix between professional and fun. She was very knowledgeable of the menu and an absolute delight overall. The entire experience was flawless. The staff, atmosphere, and food was amazing. Keep up the good work. I will definitely be returning. Lauren is a great asset to your team!

All our food was really cold and this kid couldn't wrap a burrito and the chips were really salted. Chipotle is better. The girl offer queso and when she close the lid, she leak her fingers. That's unhealthy. I will never go back here.
The lettuce wraps are bomb. I mean, they should be good with the 900% increase in price. I would also recommend the blueberry sangria because a daily serving of fruit is important.

Good service, good location, good food.

We lunched there.  The duck fat tater tots are a great appetizer.  A full order was plenty for four.  

The jambalaya was very good, as was the corn chowder.  The presentation of all dishes was excellent.

Merchants is worth a try.
This supermarket is at the basement level. Not as complete as the big Asian supermarket. Lack of varieties of baked buns. However I like the Chinese medicine section near the register.

Had a great experience at the KOP location. 

Walked in with no idea what to expect and ended up having a blast! We had a group of 6 people, all first timers. Our axe man, Rob, was excellent and showed us the ropes. Only bummer was we had to wait for another group to show up to start the training, but that's not on them. 

BYO food and drink is awesome, as they have picnic tables for you to set up on. 

Great activity to kill a couple hours on a rainy Saturday. Don't forget to tip your axe man - they deserve it!

A nice surprise. 

I was in the neighbourhood and dropped in for lunch. It was fairly quiet inside but the patio was crowded.  Best to make reservations for the patio. 

The servers were friendly and efficient.  

I ordered a Caesar salad with chicken.  This is a go to lunch dish that can range anywhere from ho-hum to exceptional.  

This one was quite good. It was fresh and tasty.  Cajun chicken would have been a nice option, but the chicken provided was fine.  

If I am back this way I will try it again.

Nothing special. Believe me when I tell you, I know good Chinese food. And to me, what makes Chinese food good is not using the chicken fat for every chicken meal. Ordered orange chicken from here, it's all chicken fat. Sauce was pretty good but the chicken was soggy, almost like it being microwaved, and like I said, all chicken fat. 

The BEST Chinese place is literally a half mile away, the problem is, they don't deliver. 

I don't want to say this place is BAD, it's your typical Chinese place. And it's open pretty late for delivery, so I get it at least once a month. But if I was driving, I'd go to the other place, strictly because they use actual chicken beast white meat in their dishes.
Great value for a sit down restaurant.  Food is tasty and well priced.  Give the margaritas a try, another great deal at happy hour.

They improved the dessert section by putting a glass display for the cookies. They look very enticing. 

You can find great Italian bread and rolls here. My favorite is either Aversa or Liscio. 

There's manager's special at the back to find discounted products including dessert.

There are 6 self checkout stations too. Everybody who works here is very friendly
One of my favorite go to bars for drinks and great bar food. Good service and nice selection of alcohol.

1 buck shuck happy hour 5 stars.
Only delaware bays for one buck shuck, 3 stars. They were super fresh just not my favorite, not briny, just meh.
Good priced beer 4 stars.

Pretty cool place for happy hour.

You really can't beat this place.  They're always on-point, putting out awesome food day after day.  I frequent Tortillaria because of it's proximity to home - I've never had a bad meal there.  I HIGHLY recommend the Black Bean Empanadas and the Guacamole Burrito.  Also, the Baja Fish Tacos (grilled, get the Originals for fried) are the best in STL.  Do go up to the salsa bar, they're regular salsa is good, but they have some really good flavors at the bar.

Do not come at lunch if you are on a limited time frame.  What a mess!!!! 15 min to order and 20 min to get food. Never again for me

Well, 9 Months later I tried-to give this place another chance.  So I ordered carry out, online what a mess, order was canceled due them being out of tuna salad, they charged me twice. The food I did Oder was incorrect.  I had to ask 3 times for a glass of water.  There is not enough staff for this business model.  It is a mess and shame on me for going back!!!!

Great customer service. The staff is really helpful and patient with me, who is a newbie using their service. Everybody is welcomed warmly. I took one star down because I had to wait quite some time to get assistance. There should be more people working there because it is near the Convention Center and hotels so you would think that there are a lot of people using their service.
Very attentive staff. Great mani/pedi! Very clean and relaxing!

I like staying at the Springhill Suites because they're a touch nice than other hotels. This one isn't as nice as others in this chain. Service and the people were very friendly and welcoming, just thought the hotel  could be nicer. The location is about off the freeway as well. I'd stay here again...

Best sushi in Philadelphia. Went with the Vampire and White Forest roll and split with a group of two others who also got 2 special rolls. Absolutely delicious. Go with a group and get a big plate to share. Start off with a Miso soup and green salad with ginger dressing.

The food was good - my nephew had a well done steak and it should have been medium rare - easy fix - the problem was our server , Carrie was insulting ,and unprofessional  - it was pretty much a fun family get together that was completely ruined by the actions of a staff member . 
Someone contacted me -asked me to reach out to them , I did reply then nothing - seems like the servers attitude runs through the establishment-

Very professional and very effective.  They were quick to respond which meant our situation didn't worsen and after following their treatment recommendation we had complete success.  Luckily it hasn't happened again, but if it did, I know who to call!

Had lunch at Adobe Red's today.  Everything was excellent!  The chips are just salty enough and the salsa has a tang to it.  I had the salmon wrap - it had arugula and watercress in it and Adobe Red's honey vinaigrette.  It was nicely done.  The mango salsa and the slaw are very good, too.  If you don't want those, you can get steak fries here.  

I've had the B.L.A.T (BLT with Avacado) before and was very happy with that, too.  While I was sad to see The U go, I'm glad that Adobe Reds came in to keep making good food.

I've been a LA|Fitness Collegeville member since before opening day. The overall experience improvements since site manager Justin arrived have been REMARKABLE.  Are things perfect? No. No business is ever perfect. What counts is how management reacts and solves reported issues.  And that is what has improved to the point that I'll give'em four stars.

 I recently experienced a financial/bookkeeping issue with the company that, with Justin's intervention, was resolved to my satisfaction very quickly. In response to some of the other postings -- I've learned classes are taught by an outside firm, outside of the site's control.  I have  noticed better interactions between front desk personnel and members. And yes, there is a HELP-WANTED sign looking for a new cleaning staffer posted in the ladies Locker room. BTW. I did visit the Pottstown facility a few times when the Collegeville's pool was out of commission due to the discovery of broken glass -- and was most happy to return to Collegeville.  

Yeah, I'm a fan. I've lost 32 pounds since January, due in large part to my almost daily workouts (swimming+pilates+weights/machines+racquetball+water aerobics) at this LA|Fitness.

I've been to Sauce in Tucson and Phx for years. I'm smitten with the fresh tasty salads- crisp healthy simplicity! Finally convinced the folks to tag along. They prefer pizza leaning more toward the sicilian 'sigi' style than thin or hand-tossed, but they obliged and Sauce won! 
We ordered two salads, a cup of soup, and two pizzas to share. Shortly after ordering, the manager, Erin, greeted us, tableside, to inform us that the salmon was actually unavailable - as it was cooking- and would not be ready- so she apologized and asked if she could offer a different entree; we switched for a different salad... i jokingly mentioned it was their first time to sauce and she was surprised... 
needless to say, the folks evidently made a big impression (as always) and for the remainder of our dining experience we felt as if we were the only table in the restaurant- royal treatment! Checking in, refilling drinks, saying goodbye, even holding the door when leaving.... it's those little things, that only take a minute... that matter...  Great food, Great Service! Kudos, to Erin and the staff, you definitely know how to get repeat customers!

It's a good place to have build-your-own pizza. The crust is thin and crispy but don't expect to have an authentic traditional Italian pizza because it's missing the chewiness of the dough. I think it's more like a thin crispy flat bread.

The website has a calculator for nutrition facts depending on what you have.

I'm really into this pizza joint. 

I'm willing to say it's one of the best in Philadelphia. 

You walk in, there's pizza under the glass. You can grab a slice or order a whole pie. I've only ever had the pizza and mozz sticks so I can't attest to anything else on the menu, but my mouth is legit watering thinking about it/ writing this post. 

The staff seems friendly. I've never had a problem. You can get delivery if you live in the area, just check out their website for delivery options. 
* they even save your login info for future pizza reorders. 

It's not fancy but you're welcome to dine in. They offer all the great additional toppings for that slice your about to get ie. Parm, chili flakes, garlic, salt, pepper.... you know the classics. 

you should try this place out. Plus added bonus for warmer months there's ice cream right next door.

Chicken burrito is delicious. The alfajores is a must have here although mine is a little bit crumbly but perfect caramel flavor not too sweet.

Friendly and helpful staff
Too dark and loud and food was ok. Great location but too loud to have a conversation at the table.

We had lunch here and watched Liverpool game. Nice place to watch because there are a lot of TV. There's bar area and further back there are big tables for larger crowd. 

Appetizer: hummus with pita. It comes with big olives too. The hummus isn't thick, not too salty but lack of the chickpea flavor . However, the grilled pita bread complensates it because it's warm and soft, soo good.

Crunchy salad with pear vinaigrette. The salad is fresh and the walnut gives the crunchy texture. The sliced apples are a nice refreshing flavor to the salad. I ordered salmon and asked for medium. It comes well done and a little bit dry and greasy.

Shrimp tacos. Comes in 2 tacos with rice pilaf. The rice pilaf isn't necessary at all and doesn't complement the tacos. My husband said they were just okay.

Fries: skinny potatoes, not many, but pretty good.

They have dessert menu too from the brazilian restaurant next to it.

Every time I bring my car here for the free oil changes offered under my extended warranty I get so nervous that I'm going to get my car back and something will be wrong with it that wasn't wrong before I brought it in,as it has happened before. I once left this dealership after a simple oil change with my car making a terrible sound that it wasn't making prior to being there. I paid over $200 in repairs that I didn't need, while the services I did need were actually covered under my warranty. They just refused to tell me about the covered repairs until they took my money. I have nothing good to say about this place. Suzanne seems to be running the service center and her terrible attitude doesn't come to light until you ask her questions that she either doesn't like or doesn't want to answer. Everything about this place is awful. If you have an extended warranty take your car elsewhere and pay the $100 deductible to have it fixed. You'll probably save a ton of money and a headache.

It's shake shack so obviously it's amazing. 


The staff is always very friendly and the line goes relatively quick (if there is one) 

The space is a decent size, they have a lot of tables outside and a communal table along with several booths inside. 

Condiments are easily accessible. 

If you just want water there's a free tap in the back. 


Definitely great quality for it being a fast food restaurant. 100% affordable.  

Shack sauce is delicious. I typically get the shack burger which I always feel like I could eat two. 

They do offer gluten free buns which is Pretty cool honestly.

In my opinion it's a little bit to salty, it's not watery and they always have different tipping. 

The pita is very fresh, light, and soft

To say my meal and the service was very disappointing would be an understatement.  I ordered the Beef Medallions Bordelaise from the "gluten sensitive" menu.  The server brought me my meal without the Bordelaise sauce telling me the sauce has flour in it.  She said it in a nonchalant, matter-of-fact kind of way.  Really?
