The sauce was the only reason (and I mean only reason) I got this dish.  There are a few things wrong here.  First, why would you put a dish on a gluten sensitive menu that had flour in it?  Second, why wouldn't you tell me that it had flour in it *before* I ordered?  Third, why would you bring me the dish expecting me to be okay with dried up beef cubes and a side of sauteed spinach and mushrooms for $30?  It was a Bordelaise dish without the Bordelaise.  I was shocked and speechless at the lack of insight and consideration. The cook was really okay with sending out a Bordelaise dish without the Bordelaise?  And the server, not telling me ahead of time, delivered the dish without compunction, really? What a huge waste of money.

You place your order through a touch screen and grab a buzzer to let you know when the food is ready. I had salad bowl with chicken, eggplants, beets, shredded carrots and beans. Amazing flavor and very filling. I definitely taste the Mediterranean flavor. Several hummus options and baba ganoush. The Tim's hummus is too salty. If you order sides of hummus you can grab it yourself in the fridge. The chicken is very tender and enough flavor.

I took a star down because the pita isn't fresh at all. It's thin and dry. Wrapped in plastic wrap on the counter. Also I found a hair in my dish.

This famous cafe lived up to its standards. The service was amazing and the food was great. Also, if you like sweet tea and homemade biscuits this is the place to go. The prices were not too bad for the size of the portions. It was nice to walk around after dinner a explore the little shops.

Professional, caring, quality care. We used them last year for a complicated surgery for our dog. We sadly just used them again to have him put down after a sudden turn. The surgery gave him a great last year. When I brought him for euthanasia they were nothing but kind and caring. It was a peaceful and special departure for our beloved buddy.

This place is a joke. They charged me $900 to fix my bumper. Not only did they tell me the part didn't exist (which I found online for $50) they asked me to pay an extra $100 to put the wrong part on. They covered up my dent and simply put on a $50 bumper which is now falling off. So they charged me $900 to put on a cheap plastic bumper to cover up my dent. This place is an absolute joke. Please do not go here unless you want to be ripped off and made a fool of.

This is my place!! It's such a nice environment, very clean, very relaxing. Everyone is great I'm sure but I had Tom do my nails once and haven't gone to anyone else since because he does such a precise job. I get powder dip and finally have long strong nails that last.

I ordered salad with barbacoa. The salad is served in a big bowl but there's not much salad in it. The shredded beef really lacks flavor. I could only taste salt and a little bit of spicy kick. Not worth the money.

You place the order at the counter and you are given a number. Your order will be delivered to your table.

My husband had spicy shrimp tacos and he said it's pretty good. Each taco is wrapped.

There's salsa station where you can pick your own depending on the heat preference. If you want habanero you have to ask.

There's an employee who walks around passing the menu and explain the ordering process and answer questions. The manager walks around to check the customer.

They make seasonal pastries so I recommend follow it on  Instagram to see what they have.

Because of the rain, I called ahead to secure my goodies. Upon arriving I was greeted by a friendly  gentleman. There are several tables to eat in. My order was ready in the box. 

Cherry coffee chocolate Tarte is really good. The chocolate filling is smooth not overly sweet.

Lemon meringue Tarte: delicious tangy and sour lemon balanced wit very sweet meringue.

Almond croissant is sliced in have with a thin  layer of almond frangipane. Very crunchy exterior but moist inside. However I  didn't taste any almond at all.


Service is  great. Very helpful, friendly, and courteous. I felt very welcomed.

They have loyalty program too by using your phone number

Please bring it up a notch!  

I write this review, know I am a spoiled foodie.. but when you are shopping at Whole Foods you don't expect a ghetto Safeway.  Sure it looks nice.  It is a small store, so there may be challenges to getting in variety of products.  My main complaint:  Nothing in the deli looked fresh the day I was there.  We are talking At Least day old salads, everything looked dried out or slimy.  Eatable? Probably but this ain't no soup kitchen.   Also saw two bratty boys running their hands through all the bulk food bins, while their parents check their lists twice.  Sweet! :(

Tomato walnut hummus is really good. Staff is super friendly and helpful.

They always gave special toppings so you want to keep in coming back to check out new menu.

Service is fast. You get a number for your order

I eat at airports pretty often and have been to some great airport restaurants like Root Down in Denver and Barrio Cafe in Phoenix. This restaurant is not in that category... 

I ordered the Carnita Street Tacos upon the recommendation of the server. I'm a big taco fan so I jumped at the suggestion. I was very disappointed in the dish. The meat was dry and tough, as if it came right from the microwave. Carnitas are typically fried so they have some moisture to them, so I was upset when I had to drink water to get them down after my first bite. The tacos come with shredded cheese, tomato, and a slice of avocado, don't really have anything to say about those. The tortilla was stale and not even warm. Felt like it came straight from the bag. Overall the taco was very dry and lacked any flavor. It looked and felt pretty sloppy-ly put together. Would not order that again. 

Service was mediocre as well. It took about 15 minutes before anyone even took my order, and another 30 minutes to get my food.  That's a long time to wait, especially for an airport restaurant. Wouldn't be surprised if they've had people just walk out. I don't think I'll be eating at this Chili's again. I rarely give 1-star ratings, but I was so let down by this place that I truly think it merits it.

Great Classico cake which is chocolate cake with NY style cheesecake. They also carry Frangelli's amazing donuts. There's also local sweets too such as Shane candy. There's bread by Lost Bread Co. the foccaccia bread is very moist and chewy. Great selections of cheese. Sometimes they have samples too. Get pecan covered with cinnamon and chocolate. Very addicting

Love love love Banana Blossom! It's such a beautiful establish, and the food is incredible here. This is my hands down favorite restaurant in the Greater New Orleans area. Their fried rice and roti is amazing, nothing tops it. My fiance ends up trying a new dish every time we go and is never disappointed! Y'all rock :)

The steel cut oatmeal with dried cherries and granola is amazing. Perfect sweetness from the granola, the oatmeal itself is served warm. I ordered Rittenhouse breakfast with scrambled eggs. Instead of home fries, I substituted it with High Street bread. That meal comes with a choice of a side order and I chose roasted escarole. 

Scrambled eggs: it has a creamy texture and basically melts in your mouth. 

Bread: very light and moist. It's a potato sourdough bread from their sister store High Street. I asked mine untoasted. I believe it's better because I noticed there's burnt grilled marks on others. It's served in 4 slices, which are more than enough.

Roasted escarole. It's greasy and spicy, so it's not a perfect accompaniment for my breakfast. That's why I took down one star.

Home fries: I had a bite of my husband's. It's very crispy with herb seasoning. Very good. 

I recommend making reservations especially for weekends because it can be crowded.

Service: great service. The chef and waitress gave me good explanation on the menu item. Very friendly.

This is my go to sushi restaurant, it's my absolute favorite!! Me and my roommate order from here pretty much every week! I'm obsessed with their spicy salmon rolls! Their sushi is so fresh and tasty! Definitely the best sushi place around, I would highly recommend! :)

If you want to get all of the donuts options that they have, you have to come early.

I arrived around 7:15 and there were already 6 people ahead of me. Two were bringing folding chairs as if they were tailgating. Later on I found out that some had been waiting since 6:45.

There's only one gentleman helping me with the order. He explained each kind of the donuts. I learned that there are at least five dough varieties of the donuts. Every week the flavors are different. Just like the name implies, you are curious about the flavors they come up with.

Each donut has a nice crunch when you bite it.

This time my favorite one is eggnog donut. Strong nutmeg flavor. By the time I finished my order, there's only one vanilla donut left. They always sold out.
Great beer to end a long vacation day on the beach ...enjoying family time. Fire in from Scottsdale and brewery hopping. Friendly and cute bartender. I'm going to hate my  bikini tomorrow!

The hummus is super creamy and smooth. I had hummus chicken. The chicken is a little bit too salty but full of flavor, reminds me of chicken schwarma 

Friendly staff and fast service

I sampled the cheesecake. It's smooth and melts in your mouth.

The mojito pastry is a perfect combination of sweet and sour.

The s'mores pastry has a nice torches meringue with crunchy graha

This vegan store is at the corner of 15 and Hicks. Super friendly owner. Follow the Instagram account for special events.

They can explain really well all of the products.

Vegan cannoli: it's small and the shell is really crunchy. Filling is pretty good. Overall it's a delicious dessert. 

Tiramisu is a disappointment because I cannot taste the coffee flavor. I don't recommend it.

Upon arriving we were greeted by friendly staff. Our waiter was really nice. He made sure our food was ok. However I didn't get any refill on my water. That's why I took a star down.

Lobster Mac and cheese is very good. There are chunks of lobster in it. What is unique about it is that it uses orzo instead of elbow pasta. Not too cheesy but enough so that it doesn't become a heavy meal.

Tuna with mushroom risotto is really good. It's a medium size meal. Tuna is crusted with sesame rare in the middle. Risotto is perfectly cooked with balanced flavor of soy sauce underneath it.

Calamari salad is huge. Calamari I lightly breaded. Perfectly cooked, tender, and not rubbery at all.

Overall there's nothing negative I can say about the food

I came for brunch and it was great! I had the eggs, sausage and French toast. Eggs were made perfectly as was the sausage. The French toast was amazing! It was sweet and savory! I love the outdoor seating it was perfect for me and my dog. There were also other dogs there and they brought out water for them. The little waterfall/ brook is super cute and relaxing. The waitress was very friendly as was the hostess. I would definitely come back!

My husband and I came here in a cold Saturday morning. Fortunately they have outdoor heaters. Our waiter was nice and helpful.

Oysters are fresh. Tuna poke is served with black rice.  There's not much rice in it so it's not a heavy meal. Tuna is fresh. I ordered mustard green salad with grilled salmon. There are charred grill marks which creates bitter taste to my fish. Maybe next time I need to ask for medium rare. Salad is served with shaved cheddar cheese and pecans and not drenched with dressing. The size of the salad is small. Overall the salad itself blends well. 

My husband enjoyed his Bloody Mary

Came here with a group of about 15 people. I think this was a first time I had a lobster. After some waiting we have got quite lot of them and they were pretty good. Then an icecream with flambeed bananas. I do not remember any other food so it probably was not anything spectacular. 4 stars for the originality.

One star because every time I took the last sip of my glass of water, the wait staff hurried another over. Another star because the ambiance was nice and the last star because the buffalo cauliflower was delicious. Not really vegetarian friendly. The flat bread wasn't very good and the chips were tasteless.

I'm soooo glad I found the Everly! I feel like I live at a resort. The pool, the clubhouse (and free coffee ), super nice 24/7 gym, my apartment, I'm really happy here. Michael helped me figure out which apartment would be best for me and helped make sure everything went smoothly as I moved in. He is the best!!

This review is for the pop ups by the baklava lady and conscious culture. I sampled the dairy free Brie, mozzarella, and Pate made from mushroom. Everything is delicious. Super friendly owner who explained the products well.

The baklava by the baklava lady is amazing. Everything is delicious. Phyllo is crispy and filled with generous nuts. She comes once a month. Make sure you follow her on Instagram to see her pop up schedule

This review is for the pad Thai. It's very delicious. The noodles are al dente and doesn't stick together. The flavor is well balanced with some freshness of the lime. the had mine with chicken which is tender and fresh. The fried tofu really completes the the meal. Definitely recommend it

When you have cravings of strawberry shortcake, a slice of the cake from this place is more than enough because it's huge. There are several slices of the chocolate version. It's not too sweet with thick chocolate whipped cream and chopped strawberries in between. They also have mini pies, muffins, and sometimes slices of chocolate cakes . For Valentine's Day they have heart-shaped strawberry shortcake.

Mixed.  I've stayed here a few times over three years because it was pet friendly.

This place had a cute charm to the courtyards and the rooms like a relaxed family California place.  Unfortunately this year, I learned first hand that the new owners are very abrasive and rude.  It is looking rundown.  

The bathrooms are remodeled (by previous owner) and nice.

During the week the rate was reasonable at least around $89-$99.  Since I didn't want to move locations during a 6 day stay, I continued to booked the higher $179 weekend rate for Friday and Saturday.  I noticed the Westin overlooking the ocean was available for $159 for the same nights.  

I was yelled at by a lady the morning of check out regarding having my dog.  She berated me and was very hostile.  It turns out this is the owner or owners wife.  She claimed dogs are not allowed.

Yet I had paid $120 for 6 nights to keep my dog in the room, at check in, as I had last 3 years.  I told her I had declared and paid for my dog.  She gave me a dirty look and ran off to the office to check.  She came back a few minutes later and didn't say a word to me but started yelling at my neighbor for leaving a beach towel to dry in the sun.

Bad vibes.  Sad, this place used to be cool. ;(

Not terrible place, but I probably won't stay here again.

Parking is tight.

Great hummus, baba ganoush, and tabouleh. I ordered the platter with those three items plus chicken. Great flavor, perfect creaminess of the hummus. The baba is light and perfect flavorings. The chicken is grilled and not dry but it's not a big size.

The desserts are delicious and fresh too. You don't want to skip it.

The pita is fresh and moist. Perfect for dipping the hummus.

Great service and very helpful in fixing my order due to some misunderstanding.
Nice atmosphere, great food, excellent service consistently provided. Also right across the street is the Gulf of Mexico for beautiful sunsets after dinner!

This review is for the red velvet strawberry shortcake. 
The cake has thick two layers with fresh chunks of strawberry in the middle. The top of the cake is decorated with big fresh strawberries.

The cake isn't too sweet and very moist. Highly recommend.

Make sure you order it ahead of time at least 6 pm the day before because I don't think they carry it at the store.

There are sliced cakes, cupcakes, cookies, and breakfast items too.

For the holiday, they have special opening dates, Wednesday Dec 23 and Thursday Dec 24 because they are closed on Christmas weekend. 

Arrived at the store at 7 AM and was the first in line. A couple minutes later another fellow joined me in line and we had a nice conversation. The crowd was definitely not as crazy as weekends. 

My favorite donut today is the chocolate curlers because it has chocolate fillings in it. 

The s'more has a big square of fresh pillowy marshmallow. The Instagram pictures definitely entice you to come here. 


The chocolate donuts never disappoint also.

So we are at the beach and thought we would patronize one of the take out businesses that are staying open even when the beach is closed. I assumed that the food establishments, especially in a beach area, would be more environmentally friendly. Sad to see styrofoam, plastic bags, and plastic utensils wrapped in plastic. I think they should be more responsible. The staff was very nice though.

Have been here a few times now after recently moving upstairs. Surprisingly good food for a "bar". Their martinis are very good and they have about 50-60 beers on tap. Only down aide is they never have a list of beers on tap. With that many taps it could be useful. They've been consistent with both service and quality.

The review is for Hershey kitchen at the back. It has Hershey related souvenirs and candy and chocolate themed Philadelphia related souvenirs such as Ben Franklin eating chocolate. There's fridge area to get prepared salad and sandwiches. 

The cookies are huge. You can get hot gooey s'mores made there with chocolate options : milk , dark, or Reese's. Staff is friendly except one lady doesn't smile at all
A very good place to try.  You will certainly love the good and the cozy atmosphere.  The service was quick and friendly.
The strawberry shortcake is the best. 8 inches cake is $30 and 9 inches one is $39.95 So fresh, moist, and light.

$3 for basic car wash. Convenient by Broad St. Fast service and friendly.

You pay at the entrance of the wash.

What time is it 10pm
I had a vegetable pizza and it was delicious.  I suggest that you try there pizza and cheesesteak

I came here for the promotion of buy one get one free, actually the giveaways were either the match'a latte or matcha drink.

I ordered matcha lemon , very refreshing especially for a hot summer day. Staff was super friendly and helpful, she offered me a carrier for my two matcha drinks.

It was very crowded, menu is available on a display but you can scan the QR code.

Definitely come back to try different options

I had the realization recently that I've never eaten in a "fancy" restaurant. Sure, I've had a birthday dinner at Olive Garden and have visited the Cheesecake Factory few times - but I've never been to a restaurant where you felt rich~ in. You know what I mean? I'm talking about restaurants with a dress code. No flip-flops, shirt required type of deal.

Anyhow, as Valentine's Day was approaching, I was lucky enough to receive an invite from a fine honey to Il Ritorno for an upscale, allegedly vegan dinner. Upon gazing over the menu on the website each day for the two weeks prior, I didn't really see much that was vegan - you know how it be. Would I settle for a side of potatoes, salad and a glass of wine? You bet. But, when I arrived, I was in complete shock as the server handed me a menu and stated, "here's the full vegan menu!" What do you mean... a full... vegan... menu? As in, I don't have to eat lettuce and french fries? "WE LOVE VEGANS!" he screamed. (Kidding, but they do love vegans if they offer a WHOLE FRICKEN VEGAN MENU!!!!!)

Ambiance? Perfect. Dimly lit, not too big or overwhelming. Our server was amazing, and this was truly a one of a kind experience. I had the mushroom spaghetti, which you could tell was very fresh and made in house. The potatoes were also delicious. There were so many options for the main course, which was extremely refreshing and exciting! But let me tell you what the star of the show was... the Brussel sprouts. They were out of this world, absolutely intergalactic. Full disclosure, I love b-sprouts, but now I only love THESE b-sprouts. They were crispy, tangy, garlicky, perfect. I regret not getting the rigatoni as my main dish, because you already know what comes on that thing! Ended the date with a shot of espresso, and I cannot wait to go back.

5 stars for a beautiful experience from start to finish.

I'm updating my review  to 2 stars due to the owner reaching out to refund us. I do not believe a refund constitutes the removal of my original review as it details the experience we had at Royal Thai Massage, which I believe to still be valid. Especially since we had to experience the things below and share them via Yelp to point out the lack of communication throughout the massage experience causing many of the issues shared. 

However, I will say that Vicky (owner) was very understanding and apologetic in response to my original review and refunded us the full amount.

I would never go back to this place ever again. Food was awful and pricy. Service was even worst. Ordered the special that the waiter highly recommended without telling how much it was and the bill came out as $134 for a steak that didn't even taste good. Waited so long for our food and when the food finally came it started to rain, the waiters told us there's nothing they could do abt that however, we were the only table that didn't have an umbrella. Ate the food in the rain. Had to check out on our phone, and there was $40 unknown payment left out after everything was paid for. The restaurant did not even bother to answer what that charge was and just told us they didn't know what that was for because everything we ordered was paid. But we still had to pay for that unknown $40. This restaurant is such a scam

The restaurant is managed very poorly. I am not only blaming the servers also management for their lack of organization. I went in today, fully aware of and understood that it's a busy day and that they were short staffed. I patiently waited in line forever an 1 hour and 15 minutes without being greeted, or even asked how many people were in my party. I watched as tables sat dirty for 20+ minutes and the line got longer and longer. There wasn't even a list were people could put their name and wait to be called, their phones were also turned off, as I tried calling multiple times before going in. At one point one of the servers went behind the bar and checked her personal phone and stood there as people were sat without a server even coming to greet them. The servers seemed to be unbothered and in no hurry to help their tables. I still tried to be understanding. When I was finally sat I waited 20 minutes before our server came. When she finally came the first thing she said was that she had just been told we were her table and bluntly said "I just want to tell you that you will have to wait another hour to get your food because we have too many tickets, we don't have empanadas, we don't have rice, we don't have New York steak and we don't have chips" among several other things. We know things happen and it's not her fault so my mother asked if something else would be substituted in for the rice in the plate she wanted and she was told she would get more "salad" to make up for the rice. She asked what type of salad and the server said "plain lettuce". Her attitude during this conversation was very much "I'm telling you ahead of time so deal with it". I became upset and asked the server why we weren't told that half of their menu was unavailable or that we would have to wait an additional hour for food to be served while we were still in line. And her sarcastic response was "mija I can't skip you guys, my table, to go tell the line first, can I?" It was very disappointing because this was my first time here, there was no structure to how the servers took tables or even cleaned them, and absolutely no warm welcoming.

The staff is very friendly and welcoming.

Horseradish potato salad is unique. The horseradish isn't overpowering, enough to give you some zing taste.

They carry Stock's pound cake in slices or the whole loaf. It's so convenient so that you don't have to go to Northeast Philadelphia.

Italian hoagie is pretty good with the roasted peppers.

Corned beef sandwich has really good cole slaw. 

Hummus is the least favorite because it's very dense.

This eatery just opened at Reading Terminal Market near Kamal's middle Eastern food.

I ordered curry chicken. It comes with plantains, cabbage, and rice and beans. I was able to substitute the rice with veggies.

The food is served in styrofoam container and the broth is leaking to the bag. They don't have rum cake although it's printed on the menu. That was disappointing. That's why I took a star down.

Chicken is so tender and fall off the bones. Plantains are perfectly cooked, not greasy. The veggies has some kick to it. Overall the flavor is on point. Be careful with the bone pieces.

Awesome Puerto Rican bread.

Pan Sobao aka sweet bread. Very soft, moist, and sweet. Pretty big and addictive. It's similar to Hawaiian sweet bread 

Pan de Agua. It is similar to Italian bread but with softer texture on the inside. It is crustier on the outside compared to the sweet bread but not as hard as a baguette. The inside is still soft and moist. It's good for a sandwich. It's much bigger than the sweet bread.

Both bread is super soft like pillows.


Guava pastry: filled with sweet guava. Pretty generous on the fillings. Fresh and crispy pastry.

Flan is really good. Not too dense and the sweetness is not overwhelming.

The fried sweet plantain is a little bit burnt and too greasy for me. 

I will try their other food again.

Mofongo with pernil: the pork is perfectly cooked and seasoned. Not too salty. The mofongo is dense with subtle seasoning.  I ate them separately. I think if it's eaten together the flavor will blend. There's about a scoop of salad but there's big puddle of grease at the bottom and it leaked through the container. Maybe it's from the pork.

Alcapuria is small with good amount of fillings. It's very greasy.

Pastellillo with crabmeat is awesome. It has a decent size with good amount of perfectly seasoned crab meat. Highly recommend

Tornillos: it's very delicious. Filled with sweet and creamy vanilla filling that burst in your mouth because it's filled with the custard. Highly recommended.

Mallorca is very dry. Pretty disappointed

Delicious authentic Caribbean food.

Jerk chicken: perfect seasoning, very tender and moist. Fried plantain is not overly fried but it's not sweet. 

Bbq jerk chicken: delicious barbecue seasoning. I ordered take out and the sauce can spill over so be careful.

The steamed cabbage has some kick of spice.
Loved the food and great atmosphere. Menu is updated regularly and there always seems to be some sort of surprise to look forward to.

This place was a really nice found we had already begin to tell friends about this place.  It was a nice change of taste for brunch.  The place was very charming and very small.  They do have outside seating.  They do followed the rules of the CDC about the pandemic.

This place has a lot of varieties of Vietnamese dishes. There was a crowd waiting for the banh mi order. The summer rolls are big. The sesame balls are fresh and has perfect chewiness.

I took a star down because It's a bit too crowded for current pandemic condition and it's hard to be six feet apart I was so anxious about the crowd and couldn't wait to get out of the store.
Food was very good, service quick and pleasant.  The place was airy and clean.  I would highly recommend this place. Great atmosphere

I've strayed from Cider Press for many years, completely due to the fact that I was under the impression that this establishment was raw (or healthy) vegan food. I like a good salad every once in awhile, but.. yeah. To my surprise, sometime within the last year I had the pleasure of finding out exactly what was going on inside the walls nestled on the corner of Central Ave.

Cider Press was no longer the Cider Press in my memories, but that of my dreams. Vegan French dip sandwich? Yes. They have it. A Buffalo chicken sandwich? They have that too. From brunch to dinner, this is a one stop shop for my vegans and plant based enthusiasts. While the opportunity to photograph all of the wonderful meals I've had here lately has come and gone, my most recent experience includes the bang bang shrimp. 10/10 delicious.

There's an outdoor area with plenty of seating, bar seating and a dining room. Bring your kids, bring your dogs, bring your Bumble dates - whoever you bring will be sure to have a good time. Enjoy a fresh squeezed juice or a mimosa, whatever you're in the mood for - but don't sleep on this restaurant! It's not very loud at all and the atmosphere is very chill and enjoyable. I love this place!

Decent prices too~ what more could a girl want!
I ordered a 6 piece chicken tender box and got 4 good pieces and 2 pieces that were smaller than a chicken nugget and had no chicken. Not worth $7 at all.

The first time I arrived here was at 7:45 and the line was already a half block long. Therefore today I arrived 7:15 and became the first person in line.

As I was looking at the store window, the donuts were already sitting on the counter ready to be devoured.

The gentleman who helped me with my order was very helpful and friendly. He knows each kind of the donuts. It will be helpful if there are signs describing each kind. There are 16 varieties including curlers and vegan. After you get the donuts you go to the room next door to pay and to get coffee. You can have your coffee spiked too with several options of alcohol on the table.

The donuts are delicious, some has the texture of cake donuts. All of them are very moist and soft. The regular glazed are ok, you can skip them. The flavored glazed are better, not overly sweet. The curlers are very light and hallow.

It's definitely a bigger store. Very spacious so you don't bump into each other. Staff is super friendly. I took a star down because there's a sign that prohibits taking pictures. Thus I cannot post any pictures on my review

Initially attending PMI I had a great experience. Great instructors and amazing friends. Due to an unexpected move I had to withdraw from PMI. Little did I know they would be demanding of their money and offer no reasonable payment plans or a grace period to start making payments. I almost immediately started getting notices of "late payments" and them wanting their money in the full amount. Upon finally getting in contact with someone from PMI I was informed my financial advisor was no longer there and the emails I've been sending for weeks about obtaining a payment plan were going nowhere. They offered me a "deal" to pay off a nearly $15k debt (for two semesters) (books were $1k+) over the next two years at $600+ a month. As a full time worker and soon to be full time student I felt that was asking for too much. If I could go back and decide to attend a regular community college I would have chosen that route instead of a $36k program that would only get me an associates degree. I would definitely recommend anyone considering going to PMI to really sit down and think about what you are paying for and how far it's really going to get you.
Super cute and COMFY spot that was a perfect breakfast retreat, and TASTY. We loved it!

My husband and I came here on a whim and made same day appointments. 

Summary of our experiences:
 - there was no conversation prior to the massage starting so neither of us were able to communicate preferences and concerns (I'm postpartum from a c-section and breastfeeding..had to stop a lot of things in the middle of the massage which made me feel like I didn't get the full experience from the massage..)
- both of us were left multiple times in the middle of our massage for 2-10 min at a time with no communication 
- we both had at least one other person come in for a portion of our massage with no communication 
- we did not receive a full 90 minute massage (even with all the leaving, it ended a full 15-20 min before 90 min mark)
- the massage was not the classic version of relaxing

We love Thai massages, but didn't feel this was the right experience for it. We paid full price but didn't receive the full time or experience. Also, upon further Inspection we are both riddled with bruises less than an hour after the massage...We Wouldn't recommend, save your money and find another place.

Have been here a few times now after recently moving in upstairs. AWESOME martinis. Great food which is unexpected from a "bar". Today we had Masha as our server. Ask for her, she's awesome. Consistently good drinks and food. Our new regular spot.

We came here with some friends to watch Liverpool game. The inside is small so it's hard to accommodate a lot of people so some of us had to stand. Service was great. Our food and drink orders came out fast and correct. My husband enjoyed the Bloody Mary.

Hummus: fresh and not runny. Served with pita bread and grilled zucchini and carrots. Highly recommended.

Cheesesteak spring rolls were delicious too, not too greasy and had a nice crunch .

Salad: my mixed green salad was served with goat cheese and candied walnuts with beets. Good portion size.
I always come here for the shredding service, 99 cents per pound. The gentleman who helped me was super courteous and very helpful with the customers.

The space is giant and gets pretty packed on game days and special events. Something to note that they won't let you be seated if your entire party isn't with you. 

There are several TVs and you can basically see them all from wherever you're sitting so you're not straining your neck to see the big play. 

The food is pretty good for bar food. But the service is hit or miss. Especially on big event days I find that the service sort of goes out the window. The wait staff is always friendly, just not consistent. 

It's pretty much an escalated dive bar. I've been here to watch nova games or election results.  Actually one of the best times was when nova won the tournament in an epic buzzer beater shot. The energy then was pretty wild. But I would say typically the crowd is your average sips crew (bros)  

I would recommend this place if you want to see the game. 

They have some good happy hour deals and a pretty decent beer list.

My favorite is the cheese ravioli. It retains its form and doesn't easily falls apart.

The gnocchis are pretty good too. 

There are a lot of other frozen pasta to choose from. There are fresh pasta too being cut fresh for you. Look for their special price. 

They also have cheese and antipasti. The marinated artichoke is pretty good. Different kind of Italian bread are available.

Ordered pad see ew aka kwetiaw through Grubhub. Food was delivered on time and still piping hot. Noodles are soft and don't stick together with some light sauce but not soupy at all. Chicken is tender with some greens I believe it's Chinese broccoli. The greens is fresh and not overcooked. Decent and light flavor not heavy in soy sauce.

My criticism here is the noodles are broken into small pieces and I wish there are more veggies 
The portion is huge. The picture that I took is only half. I made 2 meals out of it.
My workplace ordered empanadas, I tried the chicken and ground beef. Not too greasy. A lot of fillings, nice crunch, very tasty

Rellenos de papa: the potato has smooth mashed potatoe consistency so it's very soft. There's not much filling but the flavor on point.

Pastellitos de camarones has several small shrimps with tomato sauce. The sauce is great but I wish there are more shrimps.

My coworkers order sandwiches and they flip flopped the label

If you want to get good drinks without spending too much , come here Monday- Friday before 6 for happy hour. I had mojito and it's perfectly refreshing. Staff was very attentive and helpful. Good and spicy red salsa served with chips.

Guacamole is ok. Carnitas burrito is mediocre. Had little pieces of pork mostly fat.

I ordered salad with shrimp. They asked me how many shrimps I wanted. Shrimps are big and perfectly cooked 

In summary, I recommend the drinks but not the food.
What a dumpster fire, wait 30 min for my food and it was cold, and then they Charged me $9 for a beer.  I had to run to catch a flight.  Most people were waiting on food.  Place is a disaster

Seating attendant was so incredibly rude put us at the very first seat and basically threw our menus on the table and walked away. I asked her if we could sit some where else for a bit more privacy instead of sitting right next to the waiting area and having people stare at us while we eat. She was so put off by the whole thing and again found us another table get this..one table away from the original. Then I was told my waitress could TRY to get my home fries well done but the cooks give her a hard time about it. Oh really cause the last time I checked when I go to a diner and pay money for food it gets cooked the way I asked it to. I'm so done with this snobby establishment. Harrison House in Mullica Hill or Angelos, and PB's in Glassboro are a better choice.

I wouldn't even give this salon one star. I was unfortunately on this side of town and needed to get my nails fixed before the holidays. Not only did I wait over half an hour but then the male who works there complained about how he had to come into work. He proceeded to rush through my manicure which was sloppy and messy, to the point where I was telling him to clean them up. He didn't want to put a top coat on my nails and tried to use a different color instead of using the one I asked him to. My cuticles were cut up and he took my skin off on the sides of my nails. And to top it all off there were dead bees and flies all over the salon and a broken nail polish that they just left laying there.

The Cha Gio here is too amazing for words. Order some Cha Gio, put some chili paste in the fish sauce, order a little "Pesi Soda" to wash it down and you will immidiately have 10 orgasms. Honestly too good for words. My favorite dish I've ever had at a restaurant- period.

My husband brought my car here for a routine oil change and tire rotation. They didn't even do the tire rotation and yet charged for it. I knew something was up because my car tells me the tire pressure and it was on the low side to begin with the left back passenger tire being lower than the others due to a hole it had. I knew something was up when they hadn't changed, but it was confirmed once we took my car in for a recall at the dealership and they told me I needed a tire rotation 1k miles later. We will be contacting for a refund and never returning.
Chocolate cinnamon babka is very gooey when it's just came out from the oven. Very good and not too sweet. The fig almond is ok. They have a loaf of blueberry cream cheese babka which is pretty good.

I regularly go to The Dubliner for drinks on most Tuesdays (Tenacious Trivia) and some weekends.  It's normally loud on Fri/Sat night, I prefer the upper bar (up the stairs in the back); it takes a while to fill up.  
For drinking, Dubliner serves its purpose, though it could be a little cheaper and a bit quieter.  
I came for dinner before trivia last week, never having really looked at the menu closely.  I was largely underwhelmed by the options.  I settled on a chicken salad sandwich, which was quite good.  I opted for coleslaw instead of fries: not a great choice.  A full cup of the vinegar based slaw is a bit sour for anyone's tastes.  
I have tried the fries and the charcuterie platter here also.  The charcuterie is house-made which is highly respectable.  On 8/30/11 they were serving two pork pates and a chorizo.  There were two cheeses served with the meats, too.  I was not informed as to what was in front of me, but both were hard cheeses - one with a very mild smokey flavor and one with a mild 'tangyness'.  
I was pleased with the charcuterie platter which was served with day old sliced baguette and very happy with the 'chips' (fries) which are accompanied by two flavorful aiolies.  

It's good, not great.  I don't agree with Douglas' assertion that it isn't clean.  I've seen the floors mopped, and the epoxy on the tables commonly feels 'sticky', even when clean.  Come here for the beers and not the eats.  And because I care about this kind of stuff - the vegetarian options are lacking, at best.
Several flavors of fortune cookies such as coffee, strawberry, and original. Very good and crispy. You can buy a bag or buy individually for 15 cents each.
Very convenient to pick up my order at Amazon locker. I found varieties of protein and snack bars

The grilled calamari is perfectly cooked, not chewy at all. Gnocchi and penne with peas and pancetta in vodka sauce are very good. For entree the veal with shrimp and crab meat is delicious. They have homemade tiramisu with mascarpone, not whipped cream, highly recommend. Tartufo, which is basically ice cream with chocolate shell is very good to. Overall, great dining experience.

Complete scam...no wonder why they won't let you see a physical copy of the forms you are signing!!! The free trial is not risk free!! 100$ cancellation fee! I've never, in all my years of going to gyms,  heard of a cancellation fee. I also have never felt like I was signing up for a year contract when I was signing up for a gym. I needed a place to work out for 4 months while I live in the city, at their price, including their cancellation fees, it is not worth it! Plus it has a nasty odor in there!

All in all, I would not recommend.

Very good bagels. The cinnamon crunch is the best because it has crunchy cinnamon sugar on the outside especially after being toasted. The orange scone is highly recommended. The cinnamon bun is huge and very inviting

This place was a lot better than most of the La Quinta's I have stayed at.  It's got good sized rooms and bathrooms that are neat and tidy when you arrive.  No surprises here. 

Breakfast is included and they have waffles, cereal, name brand yogurt, etc.  Pretty good for what it is.  

I'd come back again.  

Valet parking was on par with other hotels in the area.. I think it was around $25-30 or so a night.   

oh, free wifi throughout the building with no password.  easy.

Can you say overrated?  I had the butcher's cut (med-rare) because of the accolades it received from other Yelp reviews.  It did not live up to the hype.  My wife had the 8 oz tenderloin (med-rare), and a good 3 ounces of it was sinew and fat.  Really?  So disappointing.  Save your money -- there are so many amazing places to eat in New Orleans.  This is not one of them.

We had a first at this restaurant, but it wasn't a good first.  After a relatively nice meal and good wine and ok service, we were told we needed to leave because there were other people waiting for the table.  I can see rushing people out when it's a diner, but when you're spending $200+ on a meal,  I think you can have a second cup of coffee while waiting for the bill.  It kind of ruined the experience.  We got to the restaurant promptly for our reservation, but had to wait for our wine.  The roasted beet salad was delicious, the gnocchi somewhat overrated, the fish of the day bland, and the bread pudding and snickers dessert not worth the calories, but the coffee was good and the ambience of the restaurant fun and upbeat.

Well worthwhile.

I have only been once, but will be going back.  The restaurant sits about 40 or so, and seems to work best with a reservation.  I did not have one, but got seated anyway.  The wait staff were excellent, knew the menu, made recommendations, and provided first rate service.

I had dropped in for a quick bite, and ordered the "Tagliatelle, Chicken, Pancetta & Porcini Ragu Toscano, Parmigiano, Borgo de Medici Olive Oil" for $25.  

Let me context my expectations before providing comment on this dish.  I quite like Italian food, and thanks to a close Italian friend I have enjoyed far too many Italian meals - both homemade and in restaurants in a number of countries, including Italy.  Many, if not most, restaurant pasta dishes are poorly prepared and presented.  Pasta cooked and served properly - with love - is perhaps the best dish one can hope for.

All of that said, I was quite smitten with the Tagliatelle.  First, the presentation was flawless.  The dish looked like it belonged in a magazine article.  Second, the pasta was cooked perfectly.  Third, and perhaps most importantly, the taste was exquisite.  

I have provided a 4 star rating, but I fully anticipate that when I return that will be upgraded to 5 stars.  These guys are good!

I am shocked that I have never written a review for this place as I am here at least 3 times a week for lunch or breakfast. The food is consistently fresh and delicious. The staff is just as amazing as the food. So friendly and they always do their best to get your order up quickly. I'm always looking for healthy organic alternatives and this place is dedicated to providing grass fed beef, free range chicken and local organic produce. Proud to support them. Wish there were more locations around the city. My favorites are the border salad with beef, chicken and guacamole burrito and I love love love their MD smoothie minus the Bannana and kiwi to keep the sugar content low. Healthy delicious food!!!

I went to Treehouse for the first time on Saturday for brunch: best decision of my life!  I was happy to be the first customer to try their homemade Bloody Mary - the best I've had in STL.  Most other bloodies that I've had in the Lou taste watered down and are lacking in body; this was a flavor sensation... it had some nice heat and really good tomato flavor, probably from the addition of fresh tomato juice!

I had the vegan biscuits and gravy, something that I've been searching for since Local Harvest stopped making their mushroom gravy.  The gravy had bits of vegan sausage and was super creamy: definitely something to return for.  

I will be returning soon for both brunch and dinner.
My review is for dim sum which is pretty decent. You can select different kinds at the back of the store.

There's a reason Anna Marie's can close so early in the day, and it's because they have a line out the door even in the dead of winter. The reason they have a line out the door is their absolutely delicious food.

With rotating specialties like white chocolate stuffed french toast and regulars like their enormous pancakes and goat cheese omelets, it's usually difficult to decide what you want.

Oddly, some of the places they're weakest is in their most basic foods. I found their bacon overly cooked and their cinnamon rolls kind of bland, but let's be honest, you're probably not going to Annamarie's for something as simple as bacon.

Bring cash (they only accept cash and although there's an ATM inside, everybody likes avoiding fees.)

If you're deterred by the appearance of this small ice cream shop, don't be. I order the half sandwich (grilled cheese) with soup special every time I go. The grilled cheese is made on fresh homemade bread, and you have several options for cheese. The tomato soup is the best tomato soup in the entire galaxy. It comes with homemade croutons on top, and it's my favorite part of the meal. I think the soup is made with the tears of Zeus or something. I haven't tried many deserts, but the raspberry cheesecake bites were mediocre. There was an entire frozen raspberry inside the "truffle," which I wasn't expecting.

If you've followed Gary Vaynerchuck for any period of time, you probably have heard the term QPR, or Quality to Price Ratio.  At Liluma's Side Door that ratio is approaching infinity, i.e. high quality divided by astonishingly low prices.  I think I'm pretty good at tracking down some of the most brilliant deals in STL, and when you don't need a groupon - it feels great!  I found out about Side Door yesterday through Sauce, of course.  It is totally chill in there - feel comfortable wearing jeans, or shorts in the summer - I probably wouldn't walk in with a tee-shirt, though.  One of the best things about Side Door, that you will notice when you sit down is that they are offering an awesome selection of vino for max - $16 / bottle!!!  You'll also note that nothing on the menu is over $10.  This is truly a small plate style service which allows you to try some truly amazing food and a lot of different things all in one sitting.  

We tried the crunchy gnocci with brussels sprouts (they melted in my mouth), roasted MO mushrooms which had a brilliant earthy flavor and the ducks in a lake which is a bowl of about 6 raviolis (filled with almost creamy duck confit) floating in a pool of duck broth.  Our waiter, without asking, brought us extra bread to dunk in the left over broth - I think the term I used last night was heavenly.  
Our second round consisted of the vichyssoice raviolis (everything in the pillows portion of the menu is a ravioli) and the surf n' turf with scallops and cauliflower.  The ravs were creamy as all hell and the scallops went so well with the maple gravy that covered the caramelized cauliflower.  

We rounded out our meal with the baked potato - yes, it looks exactly like a baked potato, but it's vanilla bean ice cream (covered with real bacon)... If you're unsure about bacon with dessert, I recommend you give it a go - Chef Michael Symon has been doing it for years.  It's bacon! how can you go wrong?!  And the doughnut which is actually three pieces of brioche cut out like glazed doughnuts.  That whole dish was out-of-this-world.  

Bottom line: go here and order what you want.  You will fill up, you will drink plenty of wine, and your bill will absolutely surprise you (in a good way).  This is one of the best deals in STL and another place I'll frequent in the CWE.

I've lived in Delaware for a while and when my family first moved here, it was really hard to find Asian imports. My mom's half Japanese & we had previously lived in NYC and California so it was a lot easier to find these things....the  Newark Farmers Market was the first place in Delaware where we were able to find some more traditional foods and they've steadily been growing their selections. Now it has a lot to choose from and many options for Asian Americans in Delaware. The only downside is that it's always packed, but they usually have a lot of cashiers open and so the wait time in line is never bad. I really enjoy this market and am glad it's open 7 days a week.

These guys know what they are doing. 

I am in Edmonton on business often and Fat Frank's has a food cart nearby.  I have been there a few times. The food is fresh and well prepared.  I typically grab the spicy Italian sausage and it is great.  

There is seating by way of park benches and cement flower boxes nearby.   There are also other food trucks in the area.  

On my A list.

Solid food and drink.  You could take your wealthy conservative relatives here and they will be happy.  It was good, but nothing blew me away with flavor.

Service was solid, if you like fine dining attentive style.  No complaints.  The man earns his tip.

Ambiance nice, could hear ocean waves.  Casual dining area, but nice.

For the price-point, I prefer food with more flair.  I'd go again in the right company, but not simply for the food.

Worst Mexican food I've ever had. Taco bell is better than this. If you good TeX mex in Newark go to border cafe. The all you can eat enchiladas were the absolutely gross. Service was mediocre. Second time here, first and last.

Sonoran hot dogs!

Start with a bacon wrapped dog and go from there.  Not fancy but it is tasty.  

A few other dishes so will have to go back....

A nice neighborhood restaurant which is very popular with the locals - a little loud however.  We had fried eggplant ( not as good as usual) and fried oysters and Brie ( excellent) as appetizers.  We had a nice leek and fried oyster soup which was very tasty.  The crabmeat salad was fairly good but had a little too much salad dressing.  My husband's grilled pompano was okay but the drum with crayfish looked good.  Two outstanding aspects of the meal - the delicious fresh bread and the desserts.  We were fighting over our shared peppermint ice cream and chocolate sauce, salted caramel pudding and lemon ice box pie.  The service was fair.  Although we're locals, we're not regulars and were treated as such.  It took forever to get one cocktail and the waiter, after we ordered our appetizers, asked us what we wanted for dinner without even telling us the specials.  I highly recommend anyone who is not local and who wants to try this restaurant ( which is good) to familiarize yourself with the recommended favorite dishes and comments before coming.

I could not be more happier. I had to re-skin my 2 front seats in my Acura TL due to the intense Florida heat, and unfortunately the year and make of my car is notorious for using sub-par quality leather, I have read on message boards of all the complaints of the perforated leather drying up and cracking easily and my car was no exception. John took care of me and went well and above my expectations, and my car feels like I'm driving a brand new car. Thanks so much!
Had grass fed sirloin with roasted broccoli and broccoli sprouts. Very tasty. However it's a little bit greasy

Apolline has a wonderful ambience - it's located in an old house that has been renovated.  They painted it a light color so it is open and airy but still has brick columns interspersed in the room so you feel there are intimate nooks in the spacious room. We had the shrimp and grits ( a bit too rich for my taste) and crabmeat Mac and cheese - delicious! We had the pork chop which was very flavorful and the brioche bread pudding for dessert - very good! The menu was somewhat small and didn't have a lot of options.

Service was great. Very friendly and food came out fast. We had chicken satay for appetizer with peanut sauce. The chicken is tender and moist with very tasty sauce. Wonton soup is ok and tends to fall apart. I had the veggie noodle soup with chicken and mushrooms. It's on the salty side and the flavoring is similar to instant-ramown seasoning and I could taste white pepper. The flat noodle (kwetiaw siram) had again dominated by white pepper also the stir fry version of it (kwetiaw goreng). We had ropang for dessert which was amazing. It's a toasted bread with chocolate, cheese, and ham filling topped with shredded cheese and sprinkles. This place is cash only.
Love banking here. Clayton and Jessi have been really helpful and there's typically not a line.

Went there on a Saturday evening before peak hours. This is the best pizza we've had here, period. We got the Tyrannosaurus rex and it had a great balance of toppings vs cheese vs sauce and crust. The sauce is clearly made in house. Garlic knots are excellent and quite large. Having lived in NYC before I grew somewhat snobbish about what good pizza should be. This is absolutely the closest I've found here in TN.

The food.. was unbelievable... we could see the chef making sure everything was too perfection before he plated it. We had the broccoli rabe ravioli and Surf n Turf. The service ( one waitress for a packed restaurant by the way) was impeccable. Not one time were we waiting for something. I would highly recommend coming here just ensure you make reservations and bring a great bottle of wine to accompany your meal.

Keep doing what you're doing Entree BYOB!

My wife and I ate here a few nights ago and had an awesome experience.  The drinks, food, service and ambiance are all top notch.  Not cheap, but certainly not overpriced given the experience.

Try the deviled egg appetizers - they're awesome.  Also take a look through their cocktail list - they're strong and not overly sugary.

Very sweet ladies at the store. The waffle is good but very sweet and not too crunchy. I had original and chocolate. The chocolate had some chocolate inside. The buns are OK. They sell raw ho fun  and a lot of other goodies

Overall our experience was "okay"! The food was nothing special, we will not he going back. What really upset me was, they add 18% to the bill for a party of 6 or more. And under most circumstances that's fine. But, this time the 6th person was my 9 month old son. The service was BAD and I wouldn't have tip 15%, let alone 18%! Keep in mind the waitress did NOTHING to help my son. He did not eat any of the food and we had our own high chair.

Came here around 2am on a Thursday night. The only place that was open around this time. Got seated quickly. Our waitress seemed to be really frazzled and in a rush to get our orders. The meal was below average. I went with a cheese omelette and a side of home fries with wheat toast. I could have made a better omelette at home. The toast was burnt. The home fries tasted undercooked. The two stars are for the fact that it's open 24/7 and that it's inexpensive (~$10 for the meal above).

When you go to this place, you definitely need to order the Peking Duck. I would recommend eat it with a the bun instead of the pancake which is a tortilla. The dim sum is ok. Har Gaw is too soft and falls off. The sup dumplings is not recommended. You better off go to Dim Sum Garden. The shio may is pretty good. I had the steamed flounder. It's on the greasy side.

This place is very nice right across Reading Terminal Market and convention hall. There are 4 stations to place your order to avoid the line if you are not paying in cash. There's pager that you pick up to let you know that your order is ready. I got mine in a matter of minute. The cinnamon crunch is the best you cannot get it anywhere else.

I love this place! I have pretty much stopped getting meat anywhere else. Their marinated steak tips are the absolute best. The Steak House ones are my favorite, though I've tried the butter garlic and the teriyaki and they were both really good too. I also got a prime rib for Christmas dinner last year and was not disappointed. It was amazing and everyone loved it. Everyone that works there is super nice and friendly plus they have a pretty great rewards program. I highly recommend, especially if you're tired of mediocre supermarket meats.
The Italian bread is dry. I had chicken which was juicy but greasy and salty. I don't care for it. My other guests dish seemed better and they enjoyed it. I would give another try.

I have ordered 2 pies from Tonito's and had two very different experiences. The first was a solid pizza. Not great, but good. The second was just bad. Dripping with grease and the cheese was all over the place. 

I had high hopes as Exton NEEDS some good pizza and I live right down the street. I will probably give them another shot, but if they come up short again, I will be back on the search for the perfect pie. 

2.5 stars

As with other yelpers the ambiance is null same with the service.. It didn't help that where they sat us was where another family was with there little boy.. He was screaming and banging his fork and running all over the Restaurant!!! The food was wonderful we had the chili chicken, won tons in chili oil, Dan Dan noodles the food was amazing I have never tasted any food as good as theirs. Next time I think we will get ours to go.. The kid ruined the experience but overall I will be going back the food is way too good not to.
They had us pay $15 (without tip) for 2 coffees and 1 piece of banana bread this morning. Seriously?
Very nice supermarket. The price was a reasonable. The line can be long when it's crowded. There are 6 self checkouts. Deli can be a long wait too.

They have pretty much their popular goodies such as the famous ricotta cannoli, cupcakes, cake, cookies, and biscotti. The ricotta cannoli is not watery, perfect sweetness with mini chocolate chip filled for your order so that you can taste the crunchiness of the shell. Best eaten right away to avoid sogginess.

The chocolate covered banana is their specialty too. It's banana on an almond pastry with some cream and banana fillings.

Their shoe horn is great too. It's basically an almond pastry with some almond paste. Its a must for almond lovers.

The fig bar is filled with fig covered in a thin pastry.

Another Italian pastry to try is sfogiatelle. The shell i a crunchy and layered pastry filled with ricotta andd a hint of citrus flavor that brings a fresh taste.

For cookies, my favorite is the amaretti and pignoli. The cookie is very moist with almond paste.

Toma is our favorite restaurant in Santa Barbara - by a long shot.  My wife and I live in the bay area and come down to Santa Barbara once a month or so and recently discovered Toma.  Service, quality of food, ambiance and drinks are out of this world incredible.

Definitely try their bone marrow dish.  Unlike other restaurants that serve this dish, their portions are adequate and the taste is to die for.  The owner is often working and it shows through the quality and overall dining experience.  Definitely a go-to place and hope they dont change a thing in years to come.

Took 23 minutes to make three subs for Cary out. Unbelievably slow. 

The meatball sub had no flavor and needed more cheese. The Gyro had a ton of meat yet very little tzatziki dressing. The other sub was average. I really wanted to like this place but the bland taste and ridiculous wait time will not result in a return trip

The ambience of Bywater Bistro was lovely, particularly with all the Michalopoulos paintings on the walls. The food was very avant-garde but interesting and the presentations were fun. We started out with cocktails- I had the Wanderlust which was delicious and refreshing, then pumpkin soup which was extremely spicy but had sherbet on top to cool the palate.  I never would have the paired the two, but it was interesting.  The poached red snapper was very fresh and moist but I didn't really like the whipped hollandaise on top-- I guess I'm just used to richer sauces.  The desserts were my favorite even though they were quirky and different and not that sweet.  We had the rice pudding, crepe brûlée and something chocolatey.  Everything was good about the restaurant except our waitress and it was just directed at me.  Something upset her and from then on, she literally ignored me. It was pretty bizarre, very rude and definitely took away from the overall enjoyment of the restaurant.

I had an excellent meal at Franco the other night.  The wine by the glass list is versatile with a number of french wine choices.  A beautiful duck mousse with melons appetizer was a special that night, the sweetness of the fruit nicely complemented the savory mousse.  When we asked the waitress to include some toast points, she was MORE than happy to provide them for us.  

The homemade warm bread and butter was AMAZING!!!  The butter was perfect, sweet and creamy.  
My entree was the Mussels and Frites.  The mussels were served in a spicy corn chowder that was unexpected, but very nice.  The frites were heavily seasoned and perfectly cooked.  They were served with a flavorful pesto aeoli.  

Dessert was a must with a number of different options.  We were enticed by the chocolate pot de creme which did not disappoint.
One of my favorite ramen place in Philly. I go there a lot with my friends. Their sushi bar's really good too. Highly recommend you guy to try it!!

There is always a line during lunch time rush hour. That tells you about the quality of the food. 
The greens is fresh. You can have warm ingredients such as warm quinoa or brown rice. When you order warm ingredient, they will prepare it in paper bowl, but if it's just salad, it will be served in plastic bowl.

There are many fillings that you can add on, my sweet potato is very tasty, the corn is really sweet. Don't expect much of the sweet potato, I got only several thin slices of it

For dressing I had tahini yogurt. Very flavorful and brings some freshness to the salad. Each order comes with a nice slice of bread. 

Although the line is long, it moves pretty fast.

Highly recommended.

Very friendly staff and accommodating to my order.

My reviews are for the sweet martabak.

Original with peanut and Nutella. My favorite and reminds me of my childhood. It's filled with generous amount of crunchy peanuts. I wish they put more Nutella.

Pandan with corn: it's good and the corn is sweet.

Taro with peanut and chocolate sprinkles. Also filled with generous amount of crunchy peanuts.  You cannot taste the taro . 

You can bought Ovomaltine there too for breakfast spread. Next time I will try this kind for my martabak.

Got free pretzel for the 10 anniversary. I got there 8 am and got hot and fresh pretzel.

The dough is light and airy compared to soft philly pretzel company so it's not too filling. Perfect light breakfast or snacks.

They have cinnamon sugar version and different kinds of stuffed pretzels.

Fabulous food. Wonderful wait staff. 

However, during tonight's visit, neither a nearby table's waiter nor restaurant management ever asked parents who were ignoring and distracting their two-year-old with a LOUD video game to turn down the volume or turn off the OBNOXIOUS device entirely. If I wanted to hear tinny game music while I ate, I would have stayed home. The parents and their table guests were OBLIVIOUS to anyone other than themselves.

When I complained to the MANAGER on my way out the door, her response was to say "sorry" a dozen times and to blame ME for not asking to for my husband and I to be moved elsewhere earlier in the evening. REALLY? Just move me and my husband and let the other guests putting up with the unacceptable noise fend for themselves? 

Fabulous food. Wonderful wait staff. 

POOR MANAGEMENT CUSTOMER SERVICE POLICIES......

STAY AWAY !!!!!!
Always wonderful to stop in to see the latest katsinas, admire the stones nd silverwork. Fine representation of Southwestern artists...
The white tuna is the best. Salmon is really fresh. The salad dressing is really refreshing. Food came out fast. The udon is bland, not recommended

Arrived around 6:30 and had to wait 15 minutes. Just made it before a line started to build up. I recommend arriving around 6 PM. 

Waited a while before we gave our list. They need to add more staff. Cooked food came out fast but the sushi was slow and although the staff was nice to make sure our orders were okay, it took a while to get an attention.

Appetizer: gyoza. I asked for steamed and they complied. There's not much flavor in t and salty.

Spring rolls: very crispy but not much fillings 90 percent was cabbage and five strands of shredded carrots.

Salmon and chicken teriyaki: enjoyable wit a lot of onions.

I recommend skipping appetizer except salad because it's fresh.

Disappointed because there's no eel sashimi. I hope it will come back.

The squid is very sweet, it's chewy but not hard. All sashimi is very fresh.

Volcano rolls: very good with spicy mayo and crispy tempura on the outside.
My new favorite Thai place. The food was prepared very well . The atmosphere is excellent and the flavor of the food was terrific. Also, the wait staff was really nice. I will be back.

BBE has a vast variety of beers and ciders. It's a great selection honestly. They also offer some inventive specialty cocktails. The bartenders are both friendly and knowledgeable. If you're looking for something that's not on the menu, they are able to Offer some great suggestions. The "new" chef has created a great menu....serving up some great eats that definitely cater to the area. The space is big enough but not overwhelming, and the visitors are "generally" fun and welcoming. Plus they have a giant tv that usually sports oldie movies. If you're 
Looking for a casual place you should definitely check this one out. It's in a great area so be sure to bar hop when you're good and ready!

It's a build your own meal Mediterranean style. I arrived 11:30 and half hour later more customers came in.

Service was quick. You can have grain, greens or half grain half greens.

Spread: Hummus is the best compared to other options. My second favorite is roasted red pepper. The egg plant has weird taste. I thought it will taste like baba ganoush. It's not even close to it. I asked my spread to be on the side and it was not a lot. It's like a drop not a dollop. That's why I took a star down. Another reason for 4 instead of five stars is because the pita wasn't warm at all. It's an okay pita.

The roasted veggie was perfectly cooked and had balanced flavor. It's still has crunchiness. 

Download the app for points and advanced orders and easy payments.

The container is environmentally friendly. You can buy hummus there. 

The website has nutritional calculator for your customized order.

If you're looking for authentic, halal (zabiha) Pakistani food, Kabobeesh is definitely a must. Third time visiting and I got the same dish : tandoori chicken served as meal. Pick a meat (chicken, lamb, beef) and choose a side (potato, chana) which is then served with rice and salad. Make sure to try the house yogurt which adds more spice and flavor to the meal. Top off the meal with some Kashmiri chai sprinkled with pistachios. All of this for anywhere from $12-15 makes this place somewhere I'll definitely visit again!

Four stars for outstanding customer service. Manager reached me and apologized for the service. I went there today around 5:30 and greeted with super friendly staff and manager who gave very efficient service. The people on the evening shift is different than the morning crew. The service is like day and night. I feel like I was at different store.   The manager again apologized for the previous service.

If you go there around 5:30 and you are lucky you can get cookies for $1 each. Maybe I should change my visiting time to afternoon

I have been a loyal customer of Terminix for at least six years.  However, a recent service was imperfect. Confusion ensued when I received a call from the dispatcher asking to change the appointment date (the technician had a family emergency); but then the technician arrived about an hour later.  It is commendable that the technician was still completing his rounds. However, I was disappointed that a requested service was not completed. Although the phone representative said that she would make a note of my request for bee removal, the technician informed me that my request could not be completed. It is very surprising that a huge pest control company like Terminix does not offer the equipment necessary to remove bees from a tree. It is also VERY DISAPPOINTING that I am paying almost $120 every quarter for complete pest control and now I have to pay another company for bee removal.  If I have to pay a second company for services that Terminix is unable to provide, then Terminix should not market their services as comprehensive.
My favorite coffee shop. Supports local businesses. Comfy place to chill with amazing named caffeine beverages.

It's a very spacious eatery with ordering stations on your right. 

The best part of this place is there's nutrition information for each item that you pick. Their sweet potato "fried" is baked. The falafel is baked. You can find nutrition information on the website too.

In my opinion it's pricey considering the portion is kinda small. It's only half of the bowl for my zoodles wit falafel. Falafels were super dry. Service was fast

I ran into this place on my way to Trader Joe's. It sells healthy food and delicious "healthy"desserts.

There are prepared food served on the shelves and you can build your own meals too.

The black bean brownies is delicious. The sweet potato brownies was is amazing and you cannot taste the sweet potato. The mint cookies is awesome too. The chocolate chip cookie isn't very sweet. All of them are made from healthier ingredients such as avocado. I didn't feel too guilty eating them.

Friendly staff who gave nice recommendations. Definitely come back here.

Went there for the first time and I got a sample of taco half lamb half pork. Very good. Spicy but not to hot. I bought half kilo. It comes with tortillas, salsa, cactus, and other condiments. The tamales is very good too, it has pineapple, so it is sweet. Opens Friday at 9. Saturday and Sunday at 5. Cash only. Definitely will come back and highly recommended.

As expected, there weren't many options for me, little old vegetarian loner. I tossed between the caesar salad and the veggie burger, and ultimately decided on the veggie burger because carbs. The bread was good but the veggie burger itself wasn't impressive. I had the fried avocado as well, which was so good. The sriacha aoli that came with it was delicious. My mom ordered the Cajun grouper sandwich and she said it was too "thin" whatever that means. I had a beer for $2.50 and afterwards I had a sour patch kids watermelon slurpee from 7-11 down the road so overall it was a decent experience. (10/10 on the slurpee)

The service has improved today. The lady who served me is much nicer than my last visit.

The oatmeal chocolate chip with walnut is crispy on the outside with melty chocolate chips. You can't tell it is an oatmeal cookie, it taste like regular cookie, in a good way.

Amazing chocolate chip cookies with chunks of chocolate chips. I follow them on Instagram and on chocolate chip day you can get the chocolate chip cookies for $1 when you mention it at the register. Normally it's $2.50 a cookie.

I had an excellent time at Mango this past weekend.  Everything was excellent.  Our waitress mentioned that we should order seafood if we saw something good, because it is the chef's specialty.  I had a Mahi Mahi special and was very very pleased.  Instead of a heavy starch like polenta or potatoes, it was served with a fava bean puree; I appreciated that very much.  We were plenty full with a single 'hot plate' tapa to start and our own entrees.  We ended with an awesome piece of cake that was stuffed with hot caramel.  

The cocktail list is excellent, I recommend a Pisco Sour to get in the South American mood.  

I have three thoughts on the negative side: we had reservations, but were seated at the bar.  I ordered a Torrontes (dry white Chilean or Argentinian wine) but was served a red - to be fair, I'm sure that the waitress didn't hear me and it was a miscommunication, I did not complain because the wine was excellent.  Finally, it was pretty loud in there, and again - not easy to communicate back and forth with the waitress due to the volume.

Upstairs Lounge is the perfect place to end you're night if you're into dancing and are up for something unexpected.  My last visit (Saturday) was a dubstep night.  We got a couple drinks, some crab rangoon and some dancing done before it was time to go home.  
All-in-all, a little shady, but exactly what I was in the mood for at the time.

This place is very unassuming. From outside it looks like a neighborhood bar but the food is awesome. It's well known for the burger. It is one of the best in the city. Same owner as Triangle tavern. A lot of vegan, vegetarian food. The salad is really good with refreshing dressing with nice presentation. The chicken is perfectly cooked and chopped on top of the salad.

The kimchi burger was amazing. It's not spicy at all. It has slices of sweet Chinese sausage and sunny side egg. Burger is so moist and juicy with soft toasted buns. The burger is humongous. The fries is great too.

Finally got the Nutella danish that has been taunting me from the pictures posted on Yelp. There's toasted hazelnuts sprinkled on top and I can taste some salt on top too. However to be honest it's too dry and the Nutella is not much . The place itself has plenty of seatings.

I came here because of free drink with Yelp check in.

The place is nicely decorated and clean. Very friendly and helpful staff. I got pulled pork and half chicken. The pulled pork is dry and had some light spicy kick. I don't taste strong barbecue flavor by  itself. I have to add the barbecue sauce.

The chicken is tender and okay. Taste like regular rotisserie chicken.

Corn bread is warm and moist but a little bit crumbly.

Baked bean is my favorite from what I got today. Not overly sweet and I had a slice of small bacon.

There are several side dish options including veggies, Mac and cheese, salad. 

I like the environment friendly containers. 

Overall it's an okay place. I don't find anything special that makes me come back.

Omg!!! I just went here for lunch with my better half.. The food was superb... To start out we had the fried pickles they are great, if u have never tried them before u must they are awesome.. I ordered the fish and chips they were excellent my fish was flakey and just enough batter.. He had the blu burger and that was good too, he only let me have a little bite tho. All and all I will be there weekly to pick me up some fried pickles!!

We have gone here before and the food had always been good,  but not tonight. My crab rangoons were cream cheese filled fried wontons. My husbands bourbon chicken was "not edible". The homemade iced tea tasted like powdered sweet tea.  This will probably be the last time we go there.

Ok. So I like some cheap Mexican food from time to time just like everyone else. This is not cheap but it is SOOOO worth the extra cost. We got a half price pitcher of margarita (arriving before 6pm). Enough for two good buzzes. The rojo salsa and chips from the bar is awesome. After a 37 minute wait (quoted 1 hour) We got seated and ordered the chorizo queso... awesome. The best I've ever had. We both got tacos and each were highly pleased although the pastor were better than the hot chicken. Being a nashville resident makes you a bit of a hot chicken snob. We just moved within two blocks of here and my savings account will now suffer. Just found our new go to place.

Great food at great pricing! They've got the best fresh rolls in town and not to mention there combination beef pho and chicken fried rice are to die for! Food served hot and fresh always and they are very generous with portions. If ever in the area I highly recommend to give them a try.
My review is for the donuts: the s'more is okay. The chocolate with cookie butter is moist and delicious

This is our favorite Mexican restaurant in the area. The service is always on point and the food is great!  Their "giant" burritos are my favorite menu item. However, the menu is quite extensive and should fulfill any Mexican craving that you may have.

Why the 3 star?? Well, right above the bar is this official looking 'notice' that read: '*sexual harassment will not be reported. It will however, be graded*'. It disappointed me so much. Made me so uncomfortable. I hope the management considers removing it. 
Un/fortunately I saw it at the end of my stay. Apart from that it was pretty fine.
Went in Christmas eve at about 7 pm. They were open, although not very crowded, and had food, though no crawfish. We had the cheesy hash browns and the battered mushrooms. The mushrooms were terrific. The hash browns were good, and I wish I hadn't asked for the cheese on top (it was overloaded for me).
