He spent most of his shift with his cell phone.   Note to owner - fire this mutt.   He was lifting a blond waitress behind the bar.  Not sure this helps your brand.   

Avoid McFaddens at all cost.
I had Vietnamese coffee and sticky rice mango. Both are good. I would recommend sticky rice mango with chopped mango mixed in

Tons of character. And a few characters! Biggest tap selection I've ever seen but the stouts are mostly high gravity. Needs external building refresh. When we rode up elevator from the parking lot it was clear that the elevator is used to transport the trash. Yuck!
This is probably as close as you can get to authentic Texas BBQ. If you go here, you absolutely MUST try the ribs, they are to die for!
Nice clean bar, good bartenders and good food, they have snow crabs Thursdays that are the best you can get for your money!!!  Good food, cheap drinks and great people, what more can you ask for?
We would NOT come back!! Our food is just okay, our service was terrible, and The view is amazing! The view is the only thing this place has going for it. That and there ceviche, it was awesome.

Allow me to start off by saying I was initially turned off by this place because I found out the hard way that you need a reservation to sit at the bar. Which is kind of lame. However, I'm very ecstatic that I went ahead and made a reservation. The servers were all cohesive and attentive. The bartenders were all personable and just as important knowledgeable. In addition they had a thought out and unique cocktail list. Last but not least the cuisine was spot on, the duck was cooked perfectly and the proportions were fair. I only wish they had a prix fixe menu so I could have tried more of their menu.

Ray offered to paint our classrooms at Storyteller Children's Center, gratis. As we are a non-profit, we were truly appreciative of his time to help us.
Ray and his crew's work was professional and the crew was very friendly.
Storyteller Children's Center will forever be grateful to Ray.

Thank you Ray for supporting your community!

We highly recommend him to paint your home or whatever you need done!

I love this bubble tea place, I also get one when I go to the mall. I usually get the taro or red bean boba. Wonderfully sweet with lots of tapioca pearls, which I personally love. My mom enjoys their fruit smoothies which are very fresh and delicious. They are always very nice and quick to make their drinks.

I recently tried Xi'an Famous Foods in NYC and wanted to have something similar in Philly. I looked this place up and gave it a go. Xi'an cuisine is different than your typical Szechuan as there is lots of lamb and beef and less pork options. I would stick with the meat and rice dishes, as the soup was too watery and diluted. Try the Biang Biang noodles.
The best crab cake I've ever have. No fillers, only jumbo lump crab meat.You can buy uncooked and bake it at home only for 15 minutes at 450 degrees. The instructions is on the container

This is probably a one and done for me.  There was so much hype over this store opening.  I got a plain bagel toasted with veggie cream cheese. While the employees are very friendly, the product is just okay.  if I'm going to get a bagel and eat those calories id much prefer Manhattan bagel.

Good food, nice location- that's why we come here about once or twice a month for lunches. Although my $17 grilled cheese was delicious I was not expecting to be charged 3 dollars for a little side of hot sauce. I request this at most every other restaurant and usually am charged a mere 50 cents when it is homemade. This was most definitely Frank's hot sauce. I would give 4 stars but the server should have mentioned the excessive charge before hand.

Nice upscale ambience with lots of nooks and crannies to make for intimate dining amid a lively atmosphere.  All of the appetizers were very good ( fried oyster mushrooms, escargot "po boy", pommes frites) but the tempura avocado with crabmeat was especially good.  The highlight of the meal was the drum with grapefruit and tarragon meunière sauce.  Who would have thought that combination would have been so good?? It was a generous portion easily split with another person so there was room for dessert.  The flour less chocolate cake with coconut sorbet and toasted coconut should definitely not be missed.  Wonderful restaurant and great service as well!

Be very careful when u buy a computer from them  .  I had an issue and 15 days old and they would not take care of it.  The General Manager  Danny James was short of rude, and was not willing to help
Customer service is horrible
Excellent stay! Very comfortable, pleasant and helpful staff, hotel is very up to date, will definitely return!

This review is for Beiler's bakery particularly the prepared salad. My favorite is the cranberry walnut salad and the buffalo ham which is spicy. They sell it by the pound in different sizes of containers. It's right next to the donuts
This review is for Iovine. This is a great place to get fresh and cheap produce. How can you beat 99 cents a pound for organic tomato. They have a dollar a bag section.

Delicious, inexpensive Mediterranean food. Parking is a little difficult. I ended up going with the Mergez sandwich, Cheesesteak, and the Mishwi platter, which was recommended to
me by a friend. The Mishwi platter is excellent and is a Tunisian specialty.

I ordered the Indian Pancake with curry sauce expecting it would be like roti canai at Penang, it turned out it was very greasy. When I complained about it, the waiter just said sorry an did not offer any substitute. Penang has the best roti canai. The blue crab salad was Ok, small portion with a very small dollop of crab meat with mayo in the middle and balsamic vinegar dressing. However, the drunken chow fun is very tasty and highly recommended.
Very good food, good prices and nice atmosphere. Great addition to Glenside. :)

Delicious food, mellow vibe, all around great atmosphere. Enjoyed ordering from an iPad. The waiters are all knowledgeable about the menu and are on point with their recommendations. Stays open late. The night I was there, the music was on point too. Would definitely go again for a late night snack.

Great food, drinks, and atmosphere. Gem in Fishtown. We have been going here regularly since it opened.. dinner, happy hours, special occasions.. and highly recommend it to everyone we know. Though, have to say the vibe has become quite stiff since the Manager Michael left.

This review is for Wursthaus Schmitz. You can get German sausage, potato salad,  cucumber salad, spatzle, red cabbage which is awesome, sauerkraut (regular or with bacon). All of them are very authentic and can satisfy your craving for real German food. It sell imported German candies such as Kinder. At Christmas time they sell stolen, ginger bread cookies from Germany. They have shelves filled with German grocery items. Don't forget to stop by here when you are at Reading.
Great meal. Wonderful outdoor table on St. Charles. The fungi pizza and the Brussels sprouts were the best!!
I always get the German goodies from Trader Joe's especially the ginger bread cookies and stolen.

Bartender is very good and the service is great AT THE BAR.  Do not sit out on the patio, as the service is BAD.  The Brewery has a great Oatmeal  stout and the Schwarzbier is great.  Goes with double bacon BBQ avocado fried egg burger with sweet potato waffle fries.

Order through Grubhub because of $7 discount.

Chicken schwarma platter: pretty good. Chicken is tender. Rice is moist. It comes with cucumber salad and hummus.

Hummus: has spicy kick in it, more to the salty side.

Baba ganoush: very heavy on coriander. That's all I can taste. Lack of smokiness of baba.

Tiramisu: don't get this. It's not tiramisu at all because there's no lady fingers. Waste of my money.

Baklava: big and pretty good it maintained its firmness.

I had the rum raisin and caramelized banana. A little disappointed because there's not many raisins and cannot find banana. I don't recommend this flavor. The mint chocolate chips were is really good and refreshing. The peach has chunks of fresh peach. The waffle is a little bit to thick in my opinion

Absolutely awesome. I decided to head over for an early Sunday dinner on the first night of a work trip. At 4:30 there was no wait.

Tried both the St. Bernardas abt 12 degrees, and the house Monk flemish sour ale. Both amazing beers.

Pome frites were good, could have been crisper, only negative of the whole meal.

Ghent mussles, awesome. Small order was overkill for single persons starter.

Boudin blanc sausage sandwitch with abbots pomery crock mustard. Great sausage and the best mustard you can buy. I keep a jar at home (can't find in the regular supermarket but igourmet.com can mail order $$$).

Very happy my friends recommended Monk's cafe!

They make the best ice cream in Philadelphia. I love coffee flavored ice cream, their lightning rod is my favorite. It is coffee ice cream with espresso beans, dark chocolate brownies, espresso, and pretzel rod. It is insanely good. The southern sympathizer (rum raisin, praline, pistachio) is really good too.

You can return anything that you don't like. I mentioned to the cashier that I didn't like the mango mochi and she gave me refund without bringing the merchandise back. That's amazing service . Now I am not hesitant to try any of their products.

Cold sesame: very tasty, noodles is very soft, more to sweet, not spicy at all. 

Dan dan : a lot of noodles, you can make several meals from it. Make sure you choose the right spicy level.

Cucumber appetizer : very good and very spicy

This review is for the what I tried: 

Mango mochi: the sticky rice dough is very thin and breaks apart, filled with refreshing mango sorbet. Not wort it.

Canele: pretty good, nice custard filling but lacks the crunchiness 

The assorted dessert: my favorite is opera cake, the others are meh.

Best breakfast ever...

Gallo Pinto. Two eggs, bistec and onions, rice and beens, fried cheese, avacado.

Amazing!
The staff is very friendly and helpful. Of course don't forget to stop by at the sampling tables near cheese area and another one by the dairy. The line can be very long but it moves really fast.

The first time I visited I thought I'd found the be all and end all of great burgers. I continued to go here occasionally over the past several years. They've become less consistent and more tourist trap oriented. People come for what the pharmacy used to be and because they have a friend that went two years ago and loved it. I find myself wondering if the visitors today are telling people two years from now that this is the place to go...

The chocolate babka is awesome. Definitely get this. Loaded with chocolate goodness. Even better when it's served warm. The chocolate melts in your mouth as if you are eating brownies. 

There are a lot of varieties of gourmet cheese. Much cheaper than DiBruno's but you get almost the same quality. Perfect pairing with their crackers such as the fig olive crisp.

Bamba snack is very addictive, only 99 cents. Very light snack. It's basically a peanut butter version of cheese puffs. It melts in your mouth. You can easily eat the whole bag. Also good is the seaweed snack.

Dr. Novatt has always been very conscientious when I have seen him.
He quite busy, but I believe that goes with the territory of being a doctor.
His office staff is exceptional.
love that place，be back。they have new sausage dish for Chinese New Year ,you can chose spicy or not spicy,they both taste so good, it's perfect for the new years

Grab some chicken burrito. I should have paid attention to the menu because the lunch special doesn't have rice and beans in it. Chicken is a little bit tough.

Flan is ok.

Nice settings and decorations

One of our favorite dine-in pizza places in the area. The pizzas are great and the waitstaff is always on point. You'll never have an empty drink glass on your table and they'll take care of any need you may have. Highly recommend, however use the online waitlist since they're typically pretty packed around dinner time.

Ordered two hamburgers WITH THE WORKS and fries.  

What I found when I got home was two double hamburgers with NO WORKS between the buns. 

Doesn't matter if the cashier has hearing problem or if the prep staff can't read.

I won't be back.
Great water ice with varieties of flavor. Friendly service. You can try first. They sell ice cream, frozen banana, pretzels to dipped into the water ice. You can make gelati too.
Terrible service, long wait for food, burger was so so.  The Manager was no where to be found.  Employees had a bad attitude.
Quick trip to Tohono: honey, bag of veggies, navajo taco, ceviche, and even an old wooden cart... EVERYTHING and ANYTHING... one stop shopping for your week's produce and hidden treasures!

It's alright.  They have a large selection but I couldn't find the albums I was looking for.  They have a cheap CD bin, with some semi-decent stuff for a few bucks.  There was sticky stuff on most of the cd cases.  I guess I've become a record store snob but I prefer to spend a dollar or two more, find exactly what I'm looking for, and not feel all dusty and thrift-store sticky when I leave.. and unwrappin CD' in my car.  For certain stuff this store is good... like if you want to pick up anything that was in the BMG cd club for cheap.  Or certain metal, punkrock, and classics like Lenard Cohen or Neil Young were well represented.  If you are familiar with Austin record stores, this is sorta like Cheapos Discs.  Which is good, but I'd take Waterloo Records, anyday.
Got falafel platter. Falafel was ok but the hummus is very watery and leaks out from the container

I had just worked a twelve hour shift over night when I came here for the first time with some coworkers. My waitress was the most attentive sweet lady who brought out some of their French toast crunch for us to try after we asked what it was. The eggs Benedict were so good! Would definitely go back any time

A small bakery wit delicious babka as its signature item. The chocolate babka is very moist with layers of chocolate but not overly sweet. You can buy a slice for $3 or a loaf for $16. You can call ahead to reserve your babka because it sells out fast especially on weekends. They have cinnamon hazelnut too.

The almond croissant is super crunchy and buttery with moist almond paste filling inside. 

The fruit pastry is very delicious with custard in the middle topped with fresh fruit. Definitely try this.

The chocolate rugelach is very moist and soft too.

They also sell bagels, rye bread, challah, black and white cookies, also big cinnamon buns. 

I need to come back for the cinnamon buns they are so enticing. 

Very friendly and accommodating staff.

It's a great Philadelphia staple. 


It's a very small place. Mostly for in an out pick ups. If you do want to sit down they have a couple window seats and a couple of single seats along the wall. 

Usually their specialty doughnuts sell out rapidly and by lunch time the selection is pretty limited. But, you can get some hot and fresh doughnuts that they will literally make right in front of you and they're DELICIOUS. 


They also offer some of the best friend chicken in Philadelphia. I swear. If your more of a chicken sandwich kind of person theirs beats out shake shack by a long shot. Probably beats out lots of places but I don't eat many chicken sandwiches so I'm not the best to go off of. 

The staff is always always always very kind and welcoming. 

If you haven't been. You HAVE to go.
Super friendly service. Once you come in you feel welcomed. I bought their amazing popcorn and never disappointed.

This food truck is at the corner of 12 and Norris across Temple School of Engineering.

Line can be long during lunch time. After placing the order you are given a number and your number will be called when it's ready.

I had veggie burger which I asked to be turned into wrapped. It's really good. It has spicy mayo and sweet and sour sauce with some greens and fresh avocado.

Chicken and waffle is delicious too.

I took a star down because the wait is so long for my order. My boss who ordered after me got her food before me.

Excellent chocolate babka. Very moist, gooey, melt in your mouth layers of chocolate. The hazelnut babka is good too, but chocolate is my favorite. They make challah bread the too: plain, cinnamon-sugar (zatar), and seeded. I tried za'atar, it's soft and moist. The cinnamon-sugar is sprinkled on top, enough to give a touch of sweetness to it. Tova, the owner is very friendly. Get there early to get freshly baked bread because by afternoon it might be sold out. You can make a call to reserve your bread.

Emli bangun: sliced eggplant with some seasoning on top. It's a light appetizer however the skin is tough, inedible, and bitter.

Choley peswary: good amount of chickpeas  with strong spices.

Shabzi Bhuna: fresh veggies with great curry flavors.

Tarka dal: it has mashed potatoe consistency and very salty in my opinion.

Veggie samosa: thick crust and the filling has good curry flavor. It's ok, you can pass on it.

Seabass Tikka Masala 
I had my food delivered through Grubhub and I had no utensils and napkins.

What a place. I was really disappointed with this place. One of the employees that was cleaning the tables that had a gray shirt that said the RIB on his left side was scratching his growing all the time. It's not just over his pants, he was putting his whole hand inside himself. Yes I was watching him all the time to make sure he would not touch our food or anything that came to us. He was also seating new customers graving the menu with his dirty hands. I did tell another employee and said that she was going to tell her manager. But it looks like nothing happened because he was still around still scratching his growing like no one was watching him. That's when the wife saw him so she stop eating. Will never go back to this place because it seems they forget what their job is.
Nice selection, reasonable prices, and a very professional staff.  The walk in humidor is great! Their Mayan imports house cigar (sungrown) is a good value
I had the mocha crunch. It's really good. It's a chocolate donut with some coffee crunch on top. The donuts are really moist.

If you're looking for a good dive bar check out this place. 

The owner is amazing and very accommodating. The bartenders assist in a timely fashion. Prices are pretty regular/definitely affordable. It is cash only but there is an ATM inside. 

It's located in a convenient more on the quieter side of an area, so most of the attendees are locals. The crowd is mixed but there's always good energy and I've always found everyone to be very friendly. 

They have two pool tables, several TVs, and a juke box. The atmosphere is that of a generic dive bar, but definitely a great place to watch the game. 

They don't serve food however, but there's plenty of restaurants in the area.

The review is for my order through Caviar. 

Rock shrimp tempura: shrimps are on the small side, I was expecting bigger size. It comes with candied walnut and pineapple.Seasoning is on point.

Chicken dumplings have good amount of fillings but not much going on flavor wise. I only tasted salt. Not recommended

The fancy donuts are very unique. You cannot find it anywhere else. They always change the flavors. So always check the menu .

I had the s'mores and peanut butter malt. The peanut butter is amazing. Very rich in peanut butter flavor and not too sweet at all. The donuts in general are very light and moist. 

The fried chicken is really good too with different flavors. 

Always check out this place for your sweet tooth

Amazing authentic Philipino food. Very friendly owner and service.

Lumpia: is very crispy not too greasy filled with meat. Definitely get this.

Flan: delicious with perfect sweetness and density. Highly recommend.

Container except for the porridge is environmentally friendly.

Chicken rice porridge: special menu. It's a chicken congee with ginger. Really refreshing. Perfect for cold winter day.
It's a Burger King in a mall. Just like any other Burger King in a mall. They lost one star because I was their only customer at the time I ordered and still they were all oh so slow.
Service was great, Bartender took good care of me.  Ribs were tough, needed another hour to cook

L'etage is best night is on Friday's with DJ Mohammed. - im biased though. ‍ 

Keep note that it's small and gets busy. But the atmosphere is inviting and the vibe is always chill.

This review is for the chicken Cobb salad. The romaine is fresh. The chicken is sliced thin and on the tough side. Disappointed.

Service is slow. Restaurant wasn't too crowded.

My brother in law enjoyed his bacon and pecan pie French toast.

My recommendation is stick with breakfast choices.

Emli bangun: sliced eggplant with some seasoning on top. It's a light appetizer however the skin is tough, inedible, and bitter.

Choley peswary: good amount of chickpeas  with strong spices.

Shabzi Bhuna: fresh veggies with great curry flavors.

Tarka dal: it has mashed potatoe consistency and very salty in my opinion.

Veggie samosa: thick crust and the filling has good curry flavor. It's ok, you can pass on it.

Seabass Tikka Masala: It's dry with thick cream but flavor is on point 

I had my food delivered through Grubhub and I had no utensils and napkins.

This place is where Key Pizza used to be. It's a small place, no seating area to eat. Super friendly staff. There are 2 kinds: hand  tossed and personal. You can have several toppings on top. They have sandwiches too. They will text you when the order is done 

Hand tossed is 16 inches pizza with thin crust. Overall it's a decent pizza. Good amount of small pepperoni and good quality of cheese.

Personal pizza has thicker dough. I ordered vegan. Only tomato sauce with small basil leaves. The best part of the pizza is the outer crust which is super crunchy. The texture of the pizza in my opinion is close to focaccia bread.

Unfortunately I saw the pizza took out I believe half-way-cooked pizza and blew it as if blowing birthday candles and put it back in the oven. I cringed when I saw it especially during this Coronavirus pandemic.

I had pork arepa at South street festival. The arepa is dry but you get a lot of fillings. The shredded pork is tender and well seasoned.

The fried plantain is greasy in my opinion but very sweet and soft.

Highly recommend for a nice night out!  My wife and I have been here a couple of times and always enjoy our experience. They have quite an extensive menu and we never leave disappointed with whatever we order. Our favorite part of this restaurant is the pacing by the waitstaff. There is always just a slight amount of time between the appetizers, salads, and entrees so you never feel rushed to leave at the end of the meal. They are even happy to have you stick around for a couple extra glasses of wine after the meal is complete.  It's a little pricey compared to other restaurants in the area, but you'll be happy with your experience at the end of the meal!

Very friendly and helpful staff. Don't forget to stop by at the sampling station near dairy section.

There are a lot of varieties of gourmet cheese. Much cheaper than DiBruno's but you get almost the same quality. Perfect pairing with their crackers such as the fig olive.

Bamba snack is very addictive, only 99 cents. Also good is the seaweed.

As soon as I entered the restaurant I feel like I was transported to Cuba. The salsa music definitely creates the atmosphere too. Great settings with palm trees and fans on the roof.

My waiter Eric is super friendly and attentive. Even the manager was checking each table to make sure everything is ok. 

Complimentary warm bread and mango butter is awesome and addicting. 

Pineapple guacamole with fried plantain is a must have. Guacamole isn't spicy and the pineapple gives more flavor and freshness to it. The long crispy fried plantain isn't greasy at all.

Three dips appetizer is ok. It has black bean hummus, salsa, and cauliflower pure served with malanga and plantain chips. Nothing special about it.

Shrimp entree is small. The shrimps are fresh and perfectly cooked. It's acidic but still enjoyable. The maduros is good too not to greasy or over charred 

Dessert:  chocolate torte with dulce de leche and blueberry compote is awesome. It has crunchy crust. Perfect sweetness.

Flan is delicious too. Perfect firmness and not overly sweet.

Tres leches is your ok and the cake taste grainy. I don't recommend it. The table next to mine also commented that it is just ok.

This place has a nice painting along the wall. We came on Valentine's Day weekend and it's decorated with Valentine's Day balloons.

The waitress who took our order is very friendly but she screwed up our orders. I ordered Tamalex salad but never came out. My mother in law order cheese quesadilla but got chicken quesadilla. The cactus salad was salty. My husband ordered a dish with enchilada, rice, retried beans, sliced beef. The refried bean wasn't flavorful and the beef lacked flavor and salty.

Pupusas is served in 3. Great cornmeal with a lot of fillings. I ordered pork. Again, it's on the salty side, but it's not dry.

The only dish we enjoyed was the maduros. It's not mushy or overly charred. The sweetness made it very addicting.

The complimentary chips are a little bit thick but fresh

DO NOT BOOK ANYTHING AT THIS PROPERTY
This man Henry is a total thief. I booked a room through Expedia without realizing there is a $500.00 hundred dollar security deposit on top of a $350.00 dollar pet fee AND a $1,500.00 security deposit for a pet. That's over $2000 dollars in FEES folks. I am reporting him to the better business bureau, Expedia is in the process of dropping this property from their roster and I am reporting this change as fraud to the bank.

It's a nice place for brunch on weekends. There are plenty of options. Nice decoration with paintings.

The complimentary bread it's warm and very soft, slightly toasted. I can eat the whole basket 

My order was salad with mango and avocado. Really nice combination and refreshing. I wish there's more greens. I added grilled salmon for another $10 and it's a decent size. 

My husband had the heart of palm salad with tuna. Nice presentation. The carrots are very delicious.

Dessert: flan with dulce de Leche is highly recommend. It's firm and sweet.

Vanilla tres Leches: it's good. The cake is very soft and moist. I was expecting meringue topping as described in the menu but I think it's just sweetened whipped cream and  I don't think it has a wow factor. You can pass on it.

I was excited to hear about a new restaurant opening up in the neighborhood! My husband and our three kids headed over here for lunch. We walked over with a double stroller--the entrance is stairs only. We tried to go next door as they have a lift for wheelchairs (suggested by the hostess), but were told we couldn't use it so we just used muscle power to  lift it up ourselves. 

Anyway, we were seated at our own table. The food was good with generous portions and the pretzel was amazing! Husband got a beer which he approved of. 

Service was top notch and someone helped us with the stroller and stairs on the way out. We will be back, but will leave the stroller at home next time.

Great pub in center city. 

It's definitely a great place to grab a beer as they have a large (sometimes overwhelming) selection of beers on draft and in bottles/cans. All of their bartenders are very knowledgeable and always recommend a great option based on the beers you usually drink if you find yourself lost.  

The food is pretty good here. I have to say spice level warning for their wings. My mouth was literally on fire, and beer was not helping.  I think it's a little
Pricey for what it is honestly. Their burger is just alright but what they lack in burgerness they make up for in beer. 

It's pretty dark in the restaurant, and they're definitely going for the gastropub kind of feel. 

The bar gets pretty crowded but they also have a whole other separate bar in another room that's usually easier to grab a drink at.

Perfect if the only Mexican food you've ever had came from Taco Bell. This is more of a entry level Mexican food place. Food was just incredibly average and definitely had been dumbed down for the locals who think mayonnaise is too spicy. Everything we ordered looked straight from the Old El Paso box. If you want a notch above TB but don't want authentic Mexican food this is the spot. Service was very good, just food was bland and had no authenticity.
Seriously the best burger!!! I ordered mine with bacon and lettuce instead of the bun and it hit the spot

This place has the worst service ever, the girl that was waiting our table didn't know what she was doing and kept messing everything up. It took us almost an hour to get our food when it was found out that she didn't even put in the order. At least the manager made up for it by taking 30% off our bill, but that place seriously needs new staff. The girl also apologized by stating that she was not trained properly and was just thrown in the fire at the job. That's not a good excuse, the wait staff should not be on the floor on their own until fully and properly trained. I definitely will not be returning.

https://www.renaissancepropertiesgroup.com/agents/henry-friedman/

Just in case you see this guy on the street - you can get out of the way before he rips you off.  Read all the other reviews.  The positive ones are fake.

Ordered for delivery through Grubhub. Food arrived on time. The delivery person was courteous and wearing a mask.

Chicken schawarma platter comes with a small salad and hummus in a comparted container so they don't mix together. Rice and chicken were a little bit dry and needs more flavor. Hummus is decent.

Baba ganoush doesn't have the signature smoky flavor, it has strong garlic flavor. It's the winning dish in my order.

Foul mudama has weird taste. I didn't enjoy it at all .

Baklava is small and the pastry isn't crispy, I don't think it's fresh

Have ordered here several times now and everything has been excellent! My favorite so far has been the kimchi fried rice. The chicken is occasionally a little over cooked but better than the opposite. Will update once we're able to dine in.

The service was great. Food came out fast. Staff is friendly. Good portion size. Big pancakes.

I ordered build my own omelette. It's filled with fresh veggies that I picked.

There are several enticing desserts. I picked baklava. It has generous amount of ground walnut. However the phylo is soggy and not crispy at all because it's refrigerated. That's why I took a star down.

With heavy heart I have to take a star out. The lady at the restaurant is so nice and friendly. One of the best customer service I've encountered. I ordered an al pastor tacos. It's generously filled with nicely seasoned pork. However it's missing pineapple flavor. Most importantly, they need to improve the packaging of the tacos. They were wrapped in paper with slices of limes so when I opened it it didn't look appetizing. 

Churros: Fresh and super crunchy, so good.

Bean pupusas: a lot of fillings. When I ate it by itself it has not much flavor but when I dipped it into the sauce, it's pretty delicious and flavorful. 

Plantains: not overly charred and not greasy. Chunky slices of plantains and pretty big portion size

Pizza is so thin, the crust is so crispy. They sell by the slice. It is heated up for your order. You can buy tomato pie too in slice or as a whole. The tomato pie has thicker dough. You will be asked with crust or no crust. With crust means you get the corners. Definitely get this, so crispy. Tomato sauce is very fresh. 

Service is great and friendly.
my absolute favorite place - my weekend is not complete until i come here for a breakfast sandwich! love how friendly the staff is. i only wish they were open on sundays!

So good!  I ate here over the weekend and was pleasantly surprised by how delicious and authentic the food was.  They start out by giving you corn chips and three homemade salsas to snack on.  It was a green tomatillo salsa, pico, and a green super spicy salsa.  Each was sooo good and unique!  Unlike any salsa I've had.  My main meal was the veggie fajita bowl which was also very tasty.  The flavor palate was different and unique (for all the food, even the nachos!), I will definitely be going back to this place the next time I'm in Doylestown.  To top it off, the server was so nice and attentive.

The review is for the sandwiches: they are huge. You can make two meals from it. Cash only.


They don't have phone number yet to place order in advance.


When I went there they didn't make pizza because there's a sign saying that the dough sucks. They usually use Sarcone bread. But since they didn't make pizza, they made their own bread so it's fresh.

Both sandwiches are loaded. The bread is fresh with crunchy crust. Definitely come back for the pizza and others

This 5 stars is strictly for the food! The restaurant itself is old and looks like it could use a good deep cleaning. The employees are not the nicest but the cashier is usually very friendly. The restaurant is cafeteria style where you wait in a line and there's a buffet style assortment of the food items they have for the day. There is an assembly line of food handlers and you tell them what you want on your plate as you move down the line. I got the fried chicken, which they have everyday along with baked chicken. I also got the Mac n cheese and yams. They. Were. Bomb. The second time I went I got the peach cobbler (yes I went twice in one week lol). That peach cobbler is slap ya mama good! I was in St. Louis for 2 weeks for work so I'll probably go again before going back home lol.

As soon as I came in I was greeted by friendly lady who is very knowledgeable about the food.

I had muhamara dip which is made from roasted peppers. It has addicting sweetness and not spicy at all. 

Falafel has a nice crunch. Schawarma sandwich has great flavor from the spices.

Just opened and offering 10 percent off. 

Challah with raisin is fresh and sweet but not many raisins.

Hammentaschen has decent size but not much fillings. It's very fresh and not dry. They are still on baking trays.

Not many selections of parties. Hopefully they will start making almond croissant.

Owner is friendly. Staff is friendly too but need more training as they still figured out to place orders

Don't expect that you will find the cakes and dessert at the old Swiss Hause on 18 street. Maybe not yet. No hazelnut cake, mocha, rum cake, and horse shoes.  They have cookies but not the same as the old store

This review is for the order placed for delivery. The hummus  is smooth and creamy, baba ganoush has perfect smoky flavor. Chicken  schawarma with grains has perfect flavor and seasoning. Tabouleh doesn't have much bulgur.

Baklava is a perfect dessert to end the meal. Nice flaky layers of phyllo.

This review is for the kettle popcorn. It's fresh, perfect crunch, not hard at all,  to the sweet side. Very addictive. I can eat the whole bag myself. 

Nice customer service.

All I can say is this establishment is REMARKABLE. Not only is the location ideal, the architectural set up was made to make the children safe and secure from any danger or threats. Upon taking a tour I was blown away by the professionalism of the staff and teachers. There weren't an abundance of children which showed that they follow teacher-teacher ratios were being followed, which is a huge plus for my husband and I. I am prior military and my husband is currently still serving so safety and security is high on our checklist for our son and so is a structured environment. Our son thrives on structure and I feel that Pusch Ridge offers just that on a day to day basis. My husband and I were sold the minute we stepped into this establishment and are more than thrilled for our son to be attending Pusch Ridge starting in the new year.
These cookies are really good but probably over to expensive for most people.  I love all of the different flavors.

This corner restaurant is a nice place to have a cozy and intimate dinner. It's BYOB.

There's only one waitress and she's very friendly and engaging. Our food came out fast.

My salad is fresh, the portion was small. The dressing wasn't overwhelming, very good.

My husband ordered steak and asked for medium rare. It turned out the steak was medium well. In spite of that, it's delicious.

I had cioppono. The seafood was fresh, broth was not too salty. It came with pita bread, perfect for dipping into the broth.
Flourless chocolate cake was decent, not too sweet

This place is very popular. I arrived at noon and there's already a line outside. Make sure you ask around if those people are waiting in line or waiting for the orders because it can be mixed up.

I ordered upside jawn pizza half with pepperoni. It is the thick crust version. Inside the store is very packed with people waiting for the orders. You can see an army of people working. It takes about an hour for the whole process. 

It's definitely worth the  wait.  The bubbly side crust is so crispy. The dough is soft. It's a heavy pizza. I definitely recommend  this.

This place is good as I remembered it as a kid.  I started out with the place on the campus of St. Joe's on city line ave. But I moved and now I am going to the one in north phila.  It is just as good and can compete with any cheesesteak shop in Philly.  My son had one which was his first at 21 and my wife had one and they both those that it was the beat steaks they had ever had and that is saying a lot seeing that they both had steaks from most of the popular pots in Philly.

I had an amazing experience I went from being pretty much terrified to drive and get my license to being comfortable on the road. Beverly and Mindy are great highly recommend to anyone with anxiety who's struggling to learn how to drive I went from sitting on a permit for two years to having my license in a month with 4 lessons. From someone who usually gets very anxious driving I felt very relaxed with them. Helps too that they offer female instructors. Very thorough and I felt like I was really learning how to drive better than my parents ever could have taught me. Really prepares you for the test and beats going to the DMV any day.
Breakfast was crazy expensive..dinner menu could use some improvement and creativity. Set yourself apart!

Lazy and unprofessional workers. He said he did not want to deal with my car issue after stating on the phone that he could. Went to another mechanic in the area and he said he could take care of it no problem and it was simple laziness on Tec-One's part. I agree.

Good coffee, friendly staff, but LOUSY parking lot with the associated traffic problems! No turn light into the business and VERY limited parking. We went this Saturday and in 15 minutes, 3 potential accidents getting in or out of the parking lot, even with staff directing traffic. Be aware and cautious!

Very clean and spacious restaurant. $15 minimum for credit card. Friendly staff, food came out fast. I had summer rolls. One order consists of 3 summer rolls. Unfortunately they fell apart. The peanut sauce is ok, I was expecting more peanut flavor.

You must place the restaurant on your list of places to visit.  They have the beat breakfast and lunches in the city.  This is mediterranean food mixed with an infusion of American but every dish is fun and a nice change of pace.  The owner who is always there is the nices person you will ever meet and will make you feel like you are eating at a warm family member's house.
This store offers varieties of plants perfect for the size of Philadelpha row homes. If you don't have much space for plants you can opt for cute cactus arrangements that don't take much space.
They got a health score of 51. Not the 83 that yelp has posted. I've included a photo of their online posted health score.

Delicious, fresh, and unique food!  We ate here for the first time (take out) and were ecstatic to have found a good Tibetan restaurant in our area.  The food was super rich in flavor, super fresh tasting and high quality.  We got the tofu Khatsa, Shoko Sisi, Vegetarian Beef Shatrak, Thenthuk, and beef shatrak.   It was all soooooo good!  

Also, I have Celiac Disease which means I can't have gluten so called to ask if they had any gluten free options (because it's not indicated on their online menu) and the woman on the phone was so nice and accommodating.  I had to call back to place my order and the gentleman who answered was also super nice and accommodating to the gluten free issue I have.  So refreshing to have a nice voice on the other end!  I am always reticent to call places and ask about gluten free dishes because I often don't get a warm response.  They were great about it.

Great food and great service!  We will definitely order from there again.

I placed my order through Uber Eats to take advantage of free delivery and some discounts. I ordered pernil with, according to the menu, yellow rice. To my surprise it's actually arroz con gandules which is the perfect companion of the pernil. The arroz is perfectly flavored, the portion is huge. Pernil is also perfectly cooked and flavored. Very authentic.

Maduros is greasy and a little bit burnt. Flan is ok, good size of portion. 

I definitely recommend the pernil with arroz con gandules, I wish they put more of the pernil.

I can't review the quality of care, because the office staff / receptionist was so rude that I decided to use another office. Not sure why anyone would have a receptionist who is rude and snarky to customers - it's a service position - but unless you enjoy rude staff, I suggest finding a different place.

The ambiance is nice, the wait staff is efficient and friendly. Ma po tofu was alright, the broccoli that it came with however was not fresh (frozen & thawed from a $2 bag at the store). The bathrooms were gross and creepy, but there's unlimited refills for water so it evens out. Would probably come back again if I was starving and they were giving away free chipotle burritos.

I was traveling with my vegetarian family and happened to stop for lunch at  Santa Barbara. Thanks to Yelp, I found Mesa Verde and decided to give it a shot based off of its reviews. And thank God I did because Mesa Verde did not disappoint!

It has an indoor and outdoor seating. While I really liked the outdoor setting, we decided to sit inside as it was a little windy that day. Since we happened to visit on a Saturday afternoon, we got a chance to try their brunch menu. Here's my 2 cents on the dishes that we tried:

PICADILLO EMPANADAS - They were nice and crisp on the outside with some delicious stuffing inside. The bed of black beans that they were served on were also cooked well. But the chimichurri on top is what stole the show for me and perfectly complemented the dish.

POTATO LATKES - The grated potato pancakes were pretty good but could have been better. It was a little undercooked in my opinion. The picked cucumber on the side was fantastic though.

FALAFEL BOWL - This dish was a winner. It didn't only look beautiful but was also packed with flavor with lots of ingredients that worked extremely well with each other. The falafels were amazing too. 

BAKLAVA - While the baklava in itself was pretty amazing, it was either the pomegranate molasses or the sumac that was probably in excess and added a lot of tart to the dish. But apart from that, I absolutely loved this dessert and is totally worth the hype.

Had a pretty good experience on the whole. Would highly recommend to vegan and non-vegans alike!

We decided to visit this restaurant as it was one of the very few places that served a vegetarian Jambalaya. We went on a weekday for dinner without any reservations. Like most restaurants, they said that the bar seats were available and we decided to grab them.

Our server was probably a fairly new guy who wasn't able to answer our questions on what was the cocktail or the dish for the day. 
He even dropped leftover food on my sandals and purse while clearing the table. Overall I wasn't too happy with the service.

The food was also just about average. I got the SHRIMP CREOLE and my husband got the VEGGIE JAMBALAYA. Both dishes were overpowered by the flavor of tomatoes. The creole or Cajun flavors were just not coming through one any of the dishes.

The cocktail was also fairly okay. We tried the HURRICANE at a couple other places which were far better. This was one way too much on the sweeter side, I'm guessing due to using canned fruit juice vs adding a fresh one.

I was slightly disappointed with my experience here. Very little value for money!

The manager, Amy, became condescending and made several audacious remarks after I signed the contract. She was so rude she chose to not speak to me anymore and had her assistant manager face me instead. They kept all my deposit and charged even more for "cleaning and carpet cleaning fees" $400+ after I moved out but when I was given the apartment it was swarming with dog hair and ants. There was even an INJECTION NEEDLE ON THE FLOOR. From the day we moved in to the day we moved the apartment reeked of weed. The apartment had several defects and many things never worked. The doors did not latch when closed, the dishwasher constantly overflowed, outlets stopped working randomly and the water heater constantly turned off leaving us with no hot water and no heater in the middle of winter. To make matters worse the "emergency" line was rarely picked up and they called back days later. There was also lots of miscommunication between maintenance and the office leading to our service requests not being completed in time.

Upon entering, you will feel the coziness of the restaurant. Nice arrays of paintings on both sides of the wall. Mediterranean music gives an ethnic atmosphere.

You can see the pizza oven burning at the back. 

Margarita pizza: crust is thin, perfect chewiness of the dough. Fresh mozzarella and basil. 

Hummus with pita: the pita is the thinner version of the pizza. It's freshly made in the oven. You can see it bubbles in the oven. It has crispy charred parts. Hummus is so fresh and perfectly seasoned. It's really a purée of chickpeas, not much tahini fillers

Chicken kebab is awesome too. Seasoning is on point.  So tender and juicy. It's served with pomegranate that give crunchy texture.

Chocolate cake and baklava are delicious too. However the baklava only has a layer of the phyllo.

The reading terminal is a must go to in Philadelphia.  The food at the little booths are always fun and adventurous.  If you can get a seat at the diner inside you are lucky but you must try.  A good place to grocery shop of you live I. The city near buy all the food is very fresh.  The bakery items are specially good a must have it the Pa. Dutch stand which only opens on certain days.

I usually get my babka early in the morning to enjoy moist delicious babka. The other day I came in just when they were about to close. My babka is super dry as if it's a day old. I was super disappointed.

Lesson learned: get your babka early in the morning

WOW! I've always passed this restaurant, but never thought of stopping until one day for a quick bite to eat. My mom ordered the soup of the day, the potato soup, and I ordered the pizza bites and mozzarella sticks. Let's just say the food was so good, we both had a little bit of everything! Their potato soup was phenomenal, no where even compares! I wish they offered this soup daily, my mom even enjoyed it more than their crawfish bisque soup that she's had in the past. I raved about it to my coworkers, so we decided to drive all the way over there and pickup for lunch. Their wrap was AMAZING! Plus their pickup time is pretty quick, and their staff is lovely. Thank you guys!

This review is for the birria tacos that has become a culinary trend recently. After you place your order you have to wait outside. There's a sign in Spanish for this procedure. I'm glad I know Spanish.

The beef is on the border line of being chewy but still enjoyable. The flavor is bland. The consommé has some shredded beef in it.

The review is for the tamales which is available in the morning on weekends. I called at 10 in the morning for pickup and they are piping hot. The cornmeal is so smooth, not too skimpy on the fillings, pretty good flavor. The size is pretty big. Perfect for breakfast. Not spicy.
